# LANGUAGES OF THIS UNIVERSE.

By their Hebrew letters and vowel points, the names and titles of all things are established with great energy and force in their meaning and power. In all these powers, one sees sacred mysteries <note>original: "Sacrements"</note> in these characters and letters, situated and arranged by order and revolution. Thus, Orpheus, Zoroaster, Plato, Iamblichus, Synesius, Al-Kindi, Origen, and several other great ancient figures believed that Hebrew words, when translated into another language, lose their force and power. This is confirmed by Agrippa in Book 3, Chapter 11 of his *Occult Philosophy*: because these were the first names given to all things by a natural activity at the beginning of the world. For this reason, we see the four vowels of the Hebrew characters <note>This likely refers to the letters of the Tetragrammaton (YHWH), often treated as vowels in mystical tradition.</note> joined together, revolved and transposed one before the other, in up to twelve different ways. These represent the twelve tribes of Israel, the twelve Prophets of the old law, the twelve stones of the breastplate <note>The priestly breastplate or Ephod worn by the High Priest.</note>, the twelve stones planted in the middle of the Jordan, the twelve loaves of proposition <note>Also known as "showbread," these were twelve loaves placed weekly on a golden table in the Tabernacle.</note>, and the twelve Apostles of Christ. They possess a marvelous and incomparable power in the meaning of the great names of God—both the יהוה <note>original: יהוה (the Tetragrammaton)</note> Jehovah, invoked from the time of Moses until Jesus Christ, and the others of which the Hebrew Cabalists <note>Kabbalists: practitioners of Jewish mysticism.</note> recount so many wonders that one would never finish even a small part of them. These two names of God, אל <note>original: אל (El)</note> El and יה <note>original: יה (Jah)</note> Jah—the first of which sometimes implies His severity and rigor toward our offenses, as in *Elohim*, and sometimes His kindness, as in *Emanuel*. The name *Elohim* is repeated 32 times in the story of creation before coming to that of יהוה <note>original: יהוה (Jehovah)</note>. It was invoked from Adam until Abraham, denoting a fiery spirit, and consequently the Holy Spirit. From Abraham until Moses, the name was שדי <note>original: שדי (Sadai)</note> Shaddai: Almighty, strong, and terrifying to demons; but it more properly signifies "He who is self-sufficient," needing nothing. From Moses until Christ, the ineffable four-letter name was used, which bore His name silently. But that of יה <note>original: יה (Jah)</note> Jah always denotes sweetness and clemency. Therefore, not in vain and not without great mystery, the Church has ordained that from Septuagesima <note>The liturgical season roughly seventy days before Easter, serving as a prelude to Lent.</note> until Easter—which is the time of penance and return in which we must reconcile ourselves to God to worthily receive His grace—one does not sing "Alleluia" <note>An expression of praise containing the name "Jah" (Hallelujah).</note> until we are made capable of it. Therefore, to demonstrate what I have promised, we shall learn that everything comprised from א <note>original: א (Aleph)</note> Aleph to י <note>original: י (Iod)</note> Yod—that is to say, from one to ten—Aleph being the beginning of an infinite number of the names of God, designates the enclosure and region of the Angels. That which is enclosed between י <note>original: י (Iod)</note> Yod, which is greatly mysterious, and the כ <note>original: כ (Kaph)</note> Kaph up to the ת <note>original: ת (Thau)</note> Tav at the end of the alphabet (adding the five final or extended letters to end in צ <note>original: צ (Zade)</note> Tsade) demonstrates the types and specific differences of this changeable world, the firmament, the Cube being seated. For whoever would wish to go further to count 1,000 or 2,000 would have to take up א <note>original: א (Aleph)</note> Aleph again, which is worth 1 and also 1,000—that is to say, the beginning and the end, a thing which belongs to God alone. These letters, being moreover very simple above all other simplicities, without any addition of matter, were formerly held until their explanation within the *belimah* <note>A term from the *Sefer Yetzirah* meaning "nothingness" or "without anything," signifying the state of the Sefirot before they took form.</note>, or the taciturnity or silence of the divinity. Because of this, it should not be found strange if they are said to be the Creator's own handiwork. 

Furthermore, the aforementioned *Zohar* expressly carries that the world was fashioned by the 22 letters of the Hebrew alphabet; and the Kabbalists have been so speculative and curious as to think that through the various combinations of their Hebrew letters, they could manage to know the number of created things—which could well be calculated, but neither uttered nor almost understood, except by Him who knows the count of the stars and gives them all names: the hairs of a man's head, the grains of all the sand of the sea, and the drops of rain. ...numerical portions, as is more amply and profusely treated in the *Sefer Yetzirah* <note>original: "Ieſirabi," the *Book of Formation*, an ancient text of Jewish mysticism.</note> and the *Zohar*, from which I have recited only a few words in passing, and not everything that may be found worthy of consideration and contemplation within them. Furthermore, the book *Bahir* <note>original: "Habbair," the *Sefer HaBahir* or *Book of Brightness*, one of the earliest Kabbalistic works.</note> or *Elucidary* writes that the Hebrew letters can be compared to the human body, the accents to the spirit, and the points serving as vowels to the soul: for they lead the letters—which are mute of themselves—to some significance, just as the soul does for the spirits and the body in which they are plunged. Some of the modernizing Kabbalists say this: that the simple letters of the Hebrew alphabet denote the common people and the order of artisans and laborers who live day to day by the work of their arms; the points serving as vowels represent the bourgeoisie <note>The middle class or citizens of standing.</note> who already possess some wealth and means; the words represent the nobility and the principal and most prominent citizens; [the verses represent] the Princes and Great Lords; and finally, the complete work represents the sovereign magistrate. Writing is thus a certain outward expression of the conceptions of our soul, which incorporate themselves into notes, marks, and sensible signs to manifest themselves peacefully to one another; and this conception of thought is like a symbol of God the Father, the marks and notes [the symbols] of the Incarnate Son, and the sense contained thereunder [the symbol] of the Holy Spirit, as the aforementioned book confirms. This writing presupposes reason—the most precious thing in the world—without which writing could not exist at all.

All these aforementioned deductions demonstrate that it is no invented thing, nor something made for pleasure by the Hebrew Kabbalists, to say and assert that the letters of the Hebrew script—in whatever way one wishes to fold, return, turn, or take them as they are situated in the alphabet—consist of number, weight, measure, sacraments, mysteries, and miracles. This is surely confirmed by Rabbi Simeon ben Jochai <note>A 2nd-century sage traditionally credited with the authorship of the *Zohar*.</note>, Elkanah, and other Hebrew Rabbis who have endeavored not only to interpret all Hebrew sentences and words, but also to give account of the smallest letters and figures of their alphabet, together with the points and accents placed below and above them. They prove this through infinite trials, which can teach and show the passage and opening to the decoration of all other curiosities and researches that one could desire in this matter. It is a certain thing that Wisdom and Eternal Truth have assured us that Holy Scripture must be anatomized and searched by us down to a single *Yod* <note>The smallest letter of the Hebrew alphabet.</note>, which is like a little point, the least of all Hebrew letters, yet nonetheless their mother and matrix and the end and beginning of the members. The Jews hold this to be indubitable, saying they have always learned through their Kabbalah that there is no letter or tittle <note>original: "apicule," the smallest decorative stroke or point on a letter.</note> in their Law upon which many great and high mountains do not depend—that is to say, many great, high, and arduous mysteries and miracles.

# *That the same Hebrew Rabbis and Kabbalists clearly show and prove that within their Hebrew law all the arts of the world are included.*

## CHAPTER XIII.

The Hebrew Rabbis and Kabbalists, in order to demonstrate that all the arts and sciences of the world are found included in the divine law—which is written and composed in the Hebrew language within the Old Testament—have seen fit to share with posterity the means and method for attaining knowledge of this contemplation. They say that Holy Scripture in general can be understood, examined, and interpreted through four primary ways and manners: namely the literal, the moral, the allegorical, and the analogical.

The first of these is like a great beaten path and a very wide gate where all sorts of people may enter, which can demonstrate only an exterior appearance. It is named by the said Hebrews in their language <term>Derek hapeschat</term> <note>original: דֶּרֶךְ הַפְּשָׁט, meaning "the way of the plain or literal meaning."</note>, a path that is level, extended, and smoothed; and by the Roman doctors <note>Catholic theologians and scholars of the Latin tradition.</note> the <term>historical sense</term>. It is as if they wished to say that the literal sense places before the eyes only the outside and the exterior face, like the bark of trees or the skin that serves as clothing for the body. Within this sense, as in a painting or a large map, we can observe in the figures and characters arranged there the lives and deeds of those chosen and loved by God, as well as the wicked and the reprobate.

The <term>moral sense</term> is more modest, trimming away much of the great license of the literal. It acquired among the Greeks the name <term>ethos</term> <note>original: ηθος, referring to character or custom.</note>, and among the Latins that of <term>moral</term>, and among the Hebrews this beautiful title of <term>Midrash</term> <note>original: מִדְרָשׁ, meaning "search," "inquiry," or "exposition."</note> or <term>search</term>. Although it is a neighbor to allegory—and the term seems somewhat to confound it with it, as I shall say hereafter, and to transfer the significance and property to that which is called in Greek <term>tropology</term> <note>original: τροπολογια, a figurative interpretation that explains the moral application of a text.</note>, so called because it teaches us the way to interpret the phrases, figures, and properties of words and sentences—it aims and tends toward this single goal: to tame and conquer the rebellions and revolts of the flesh, in order to acquire a simple and natural beauty.

<term>Allegory</term>, of which this [moral sense] is a species, is like a kind of inversion or trope that occurs when we turn a word away from its proper and natural significance to use it in a sense improper and distant from its nature. It differs from the metaphor in that the metaphor is attached to one or two words at most, whereas <term>allegory</term> is a perpetual metaphorical transfer, so named because it expresses and designates things other than what the words propose. This is considered in various ways: either according to history, or according to the world. It is found founded upon the figure of the Church, or upon the symbols of both numbers and Hebrew letters; hence it is either <term>historical</term>, <term>worldly</term>, <term>figurative</term>, or <term>symbolic</term>, all of which I shall mention hereafter when the need arises. Therefore, <term>allegory</term> belongs to an entire and perfect sequence of discourse; it relies entirely on similarities or comparisons which cannot be of things that are already conformable and suited to one another, but rather of those which take their source from the marriage of heaven and earth, and of corporeal, sensible, and perishable things compared and related to those which are everlasting, invisible, and devoid of all corporeal accident. We can further understand under the general name of the mystical and allegorical-historical sense—as under its own genre—that which I promised was named by the Hebrew interpreters <term>Misdrafz</term> <note>A variant spelling or corruption of "Midrash" used by the author.</note> which I mentioned before:

compared to <term>Tropology</term> <note>The "moral" sense of scripture, which seeks to provide guidance for human behavior.</note>, which in the judgment of many belongs to and consists entirely of doctrine; and even though **Elias Levita** <note>A renowned 16th-century Hebrew grammarian and scholar.</note> understands under the word <term>Midrash</term> <note>original: "Midrasz." Under the scope of this word, the Hebrews include the moral sense, which declares the battle between the flesh and the soul; the <term>Tropological</term> sense, which agitates the quarrel between the letter and mystical intelligence; and **Allegory**, which assembles and allies lower things with higher things, and treats—as some claim—the war of the Church Militant against the agents of the devil. However, according to the opinion of these scholars, this should be understood insofar as it draws its reasons and arguments from Ecclesiastical history, where the mystery of the Church is contained.

And so as not to cut short our discussion here, we shall learn that **Allegory** wanders and roams through all of nature; being aided and supported by two or three chords, it hoists itself up through nature or above the heavens to communicate with the Angels, and is then called ***Theological***; sometimes, sliding back down from there, it returns toward us and is called ***Natural***; and sometimes, balancing between the two in the supreme region, it depicts the various miracles of the middle ground and is called ***Celestial***. In this way, it observes and maintains the "compositive method" while ascending, the "analytic and unraveling method" while descending, and follows the "definitive and bounding method" when it remains between the two.

There are still others who derive **contemplative prayer** from Allegory; the nature of which is to completely contain everything of this world and its conversation in order to strive for the ornament and divinity of the soul, having the gifts of the Holy Spirit as its subject. By this means, it would be distinguished from Tropology, near which they place it in the same way that we discern the good religious and contemplative man from the secular man of the Church. For this reason, ***Tropology***—being close to the **moral sense**, which has as its proposed goal the moral virtues that (according to the opinion of Philosophers) consist in action—retains much of its nature and seems to hold such a place among spiritual expositions as the intellectual virtues hold among themselves: those concerning morals and those called ***Theological***.

***Anagogy*** <note>The highest level of interpretation, relating to the soul's ascent toward the divine or the afterlife.</note>, like a reduction or an escort back, must be related—as if from the center and point which is everywhere in virtue and power, to the circumference which is nowhere—to all that we can see, touch, taste, smell, hear, understand, or love, stripped of its accidental qualities, to Him who is the Father of eternal and sensible things, yet is nonetheless above all feeling, dwelling solitary in His Eternity. Thus far ***Affirmative Theology*** extends, and here, furthermore, the science of the **tree of the ten names** <note>A reference to the *Sefirot* in Kabbalah, the ten attributes or emanations through which the Infinite (Ein Sof) reveals itself.</note> and divine dimensions is supported, to which (as if under ten universal <term>predicaments</term> <note>Categories of being or logic.</note>) the reasons for all things are related. Above this, if we desire to soar, we enter an abyss and, as if lost and led astray, we become true students and apprentices in ***Negative Theology***, which demonstrates to us that God is nothing less than what we affirm of Him; rather, He is infinite, incomprehensible, and inexplicable, as says the—

This is because this sense is primarily cultivated by the Kabbalists, who leave the <gloss>Plain or Literal sense</gloss> <note>original Hebrew: פשט (Pshat)</note> and the <gloss>Interpretive study</gloss> <note>original Hebrew: מדרש (Midrash)</note> to the Rabbis and Talmudists, and to the Philosophers they leave the rational progression which they call the <gloss>Way of the Intellect</gloss> <note>original Hebrew: דרך שכל (Derekh Sekhel)</note>. It is true that this Kabbalistic method, insofar as it does not stop at the letter—which of itself can only be dead and unable to supply or furnish us with living intelligence—but instead rises up to make a display of all nature, can easily be subdivided into those senses mentioned above. However, it is one degree inferior to the anagogical and divine sense, which perfects and accomplishes all the others and in which all of them are comprised. This is something I could easily and readily prove with great deductions of words if time and leisure permitted. 

But passing further, I will say that under allegory, some have included and numbered the "typical" sense, upon which allegory depends. This figure has divisions and parts which are as follows: the first and oldest in terms of history, but of lesser extent than any of the others, is **The Equal** or **Judaic**, because its limits do not go beyond the enclosure of the synagogue. The second, already much more embracing, is named **Christian** or **Evangelical**. The third, which surpasses the second as much as the second surpasses the first, is called **Spiritual**. The fourth, which brings the Hebrew people back into the Greek Church, is rightly called by a name mixed of two: **Greco-Jewish**. The fifth, which considers in the cloudy mirror of the Hebrew people the pure, shining, and transparent crystal of the Latins, can be named **Latino-Jewish**. The sixth is called the **Christian Spiritual**. And the last, which contains the other six, deserves the title of **New Jerusalem**, seeing as in it the others come to complete their course and revolution. 

All of this cannot be made as clear as one might desire except with a great weaving of discourse and examples, which would fill a whole volume. regard for anything else: in the same way, **Geometry** embraces continuous quantity and magnitude—stable and not subject to movement—rightly leaving "moving magnitude" to **Astronomy**, which encompasses the dance and measured ballet of all the celestial bodies. Just as **Arithmetic** and **Music** have their foundations in number and plurality (which distinguishes things, being itself a form of distinction), similarly **Geometry** and **Astronomy** have as their base and foundation "magnitude," a term that bounds and limits physical things. 

Therefore, by proportion and symbolic reasoning, number—both in the way of counting and in music—is used by philosophers and theologians to discuss divine forms and species, both intellectual and substantial. Conversely, through the other two [Geometry and Astronomy], one treats the figures and qualities of both the higher, active, and celestial bodies, and the lower, passive, and corruptible ones. This is amply demonstrated above all other ancients and moderns by the great and admirable **Francesco di Giorgio** <note>original: "George Venitien," referring to Francesco Zorzi, a Venetian Franciscan friar and Christian Kabbalist</note> in his book *The Harmony of the World* <note>original Latin: "De Harmonia Mundi"</note> and by **Nicolas Lefèvre de La Boderie** in his introduction to that same book.

### CHAP. XIV.

The aforementioned Hebrew Rabbis and Kabbalists have, from all time and antiquity, used the specific characters of their common and open Hebrew writing in place of ciphers. These characters were intended only to secretly denote and express the most hidden mysteries of their divine Law, whereas we only apply and profane them for the affairs of the world. Furthermore, they have several sorts and manners of doing this, all of which depend on six principal paths, namely: <term>תמורה</term> (*Themurah*, meaning exchanges), which is to say, metatheses, transpositions, or material commutations of Hebrew letters in the form of anagrams; <term>צרוף</term> (*Ziraph* or *Ziruf*, meaning combinations), which is to say, combinations, pairings, and formal exchanges of these letters when they are moved from their true faculty and power into others, with reciprocal commutations; <term>אתבש</term> (*Aetbatsz* or *Atbaz*), which are the dances and transpositions or leaps of the aforementioned letters into one another <note>Atbash is a substitution cipher where the first letter of the alphabet is replaced by the last, the second by the second-to-last, and so on.</note>; <term>גמטריא</term> (*Ghematria* or *Gematria*), which is an equivalence of numbers, measures, and proportions; <term>גלגol</term> (*Ghilgul*), which is a numerical quantity <note>Often referring to the "rolling" or cycling of letters or souls.</note>; and <term>נוטריקון</term> (*Notariacon*), which is when one puts a letter or a syllable for a word, or the reverse; together with the <term>ראשי תבות</term> (*Rasce Theuoth*, or heads of dictions) and <term>סוף תבות</term> (*Sop Theuoth*, or ends of Hebrew vocables). All these varieties of Hebrew mysteries and secrets come, as the aforementioned Hebrew Rabbis and Kabbalists say—and even **Rabbi Moses Gerundense** <note>Moses ben Nahman, also known as Nachmanides (1194–1270).</note>—from the fact that God gave the Law to Moses written in confused and tangled letters, such that one could read it from all sides: to the right, to the left, forward, backward, from top to bottom, and from bottom to top. As we shall say more particularly hereafter, each person could form diverse meanings from it; this is the true Stenography <note>Secret or shorthand writing.</note> that the **Abbot Trithemius** <note>Johannes Trithemius (1462–1516), a German abbot and polymath famous for his work on cryptography and steganography.</note> wished to imitate, though what he showed of it...

# HISTORY OF THE ORIGIN OF [THE LANGUAGES]

In further imitation of [the Hebrews], they [the Greeks] have a nearly identical form of Arithmancy <note>Also known as isopsephy: the practice of adding up the numerical values of the letters in a word to find a hidden meaning.</note> to the one previously discussed—that is, divination by numbers assigned to their characters. This was first devised, so they say, by the Greek philosopher Pythagoras, whose traditions are nothing other than a true Hebrew Kabbalah. In this regard, he employs that passage from Wisdom 11: *You have ordered all things by number, weight, and measure.* <note>original: "Omnia in numero, pondere, & mensura disposuisti"</note> Even Aristotle and Ptolemy do not contradict this, acknowledging that letters mystically carry within them certain numbers which, in the proper names of People, Kingdoms, Empires, Cities, and Republics, contain some secret regarding their fortunes and destinies. We can see this in the following verses from Terentianus <note>Terentianus Maurus, a 2nd-century Roman grammarian.</note>, who demonstrates its use and practice:

> *And they say names are thus recorded through their letters,*
> *So that some have greater numbers, others smaller.*
> *Whenever they enter the doubtful perils of battle,*
> *Wherever the larger number stands, victory favors that side,*
> *While the smallest sums reveal the omens of death.*
> *Thus they say Patroclus perished by the hand of Hector:*
> *Thus they say Hector soon fell to Achilles.*
<note>Original Latin: "Et nomina tradunt ita literis per acta... Presagia lethi minima patere summa."</note>

Namely, that by taking the names of two who wish to enter a duel or single combat, the one whose name’s letters surpass the other according to the aforementioned calculation will likewise obtain the victory. This was proven by experience in the case of Hector, who put Patroclus to death, and was afterwards killed by Achilles.

<margin>Hector</margin>
For the characters of the word <gloss>Hector</gloss> <note>Εκτωρ</note> together make 1225: specifically ε (5), κ (20), τ (300), ω (800) <note>The original text mistakenly lists omega (ω) as 8, but the total 1225 confirms it is the value 800.</note>, and ρ (100).

<margin>Patroclus: π 80, α 1, τ 300, ρ 100, ο 70, κ 20, λ 30, ο 70, ς 200.</margin>
Whereas those of <gloss>Patroclus</gloss> <note>Πατροκλος</note>, though greater in number of letters, nevertheless only reach 871, in this manner: π (80), α (1), τ (300), ρ (100), ο (70), κ (20), λ (30), ο (70), and ς (200). 

<margin>Achilles</margin>
It is exactly the same with Hector and Achilles, because <gloss>Achilles</gloss> <note>Αχιλλευς</note> goes up to 1276, as can be seen by the number of his characters. Some have even wanted to infer from this that it is a bad omen in marriage if the letters of the wife's name and surname exceed in value those of the husband, as if she were destined to dominate him. However, one should not dwell on this at all, because these are uncertain things that do not always succeed if there is no other skill involved than what is described above. This was encountered with <gloss>Carthage</gloss> <note>Καρχηδών</note> and <gloss>Rome</gloss> <note>Ρώμη</note>; the former, which was overcome by the Romans, far exceeds the name of Rome in its numerical sum. This is not to say, however, that there are not very great secrets and mysteries in numbers, as can be seen in the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation.</note>, chapter 13: 

<margin>Let him who has understanding calculate the number of the beast, for it is the number of a man, and his number is 666.</margin>

As for the other manner of Hebrew ciphering, we shall learn that from the Hebrew grammar mentioned previously proceeds and begins the artifice and curious speculative research declared above, which the Hebrews call <term>תמורה</term> <note>Themurah: a Kabbalistic method of substituting or rearranging letters to find hidden meanings.</note> *Themurah*, *Metapheses* or *Metatheses*, or material commutations of Hebrew letters and sometimes syllables. This is deduced—following the Hebrew Rabbis and Kabbalists—by Johann Reuchlin <note>A German humanist (also called Capnion) who was a pioneer in bringing Hebrew studies to Christian scholars.</note> in his books on the Kabbalistic art, and by Guillaume Postel in his commentaries on the *Sefer Yetzirah* <note>The "Book of Formation," one of the oldest and most important mystical texts in the Jewish tradition.</note>. Under this industry and curiosity, the secrets and mysteries of the ancient Hebrews teach that an infinity of very beautiful and serious things can be brought to light through the entire context of the Hebrew scripture. Therefore, to demonstrate this, the following example among infinite others may declare both the strange secrets and mysteries found in the context of Holy Scripture, in the Hebrew language and characters, for which others are not so well-suited.

The first word of Genesis, <term>בראשית</term> *Beresith*, or *Bresit*, consists of six different letters, denoting the six days in which God perfected the entire machine of the universe. The first three letters, <term>ברא</term> *Bra*, signify "he created." If you remove the letter <term>ב</term> (Beth) from the whole word, there remains *Resit*, which means "beginning." Furthermore, because this *Beth* is marked there as a capital, which is worth 2,000 in number, some Kabbalists have wished to infer from this (according to the words of Rabbi Moses the Egyptian <note>Better known as Maimonides, the preeminent medieval Jewish philosopher.</note> in the second book of his *Guide*, chapter 31, though he reproves them for it) that it was purposely placed before this word *Resit* to show that two thousand years passed before the creation of the world. They base this on what is written of the first, second, and third days, before the sun and moon were yet in evidence to distinguish day and night, months, and years; for how could one measure time without these two luminaries? By this, therefore, we see (says the same Rabbi Judah) that scripture testifies that the order of time has been from all eternity with God.

And regarding this, it must be understood that among the Hebrews, everything that passes the number of a thousand is taken as infinite, as can be seen in Psalm 119: *The law of your mouth is a very great good to me, more than gold or silver by the thousands.* By which means one should rather refer this to the fact that *Beth*, as the second letter, represents the Word, Wisdom, and the <term>SON</term>, the second person of the Trinity, who has been from all eternity inseparably joined and united with the *Aleph*, the <term>FATHER</term>. It is by Him, according to Psalm 33, that the heavens were established—that is to say, the entire Universe. This same truth is testified by Hermes Trismegistus in these express words in the fourth book of his *Poimandres*: <quote>The Maker crafted the whole universe with the word, not with hands</quote> <note>original Latin: "Universum mundum verbo non manibus fabricatus est opifex"</note>; before the creation of which...

Here then is a portion of the mysteries of the word *Bereshit* regarding its primary elements. Now, join the third letter, *Aleph*, with *Beth*, and you will have *Ab*, which signifies "Father." Redouble it with the second letter, *Beth*, which carries with it its vowel "a," and you will have *Bebar*, "by the son." Remove it from the whole word and *Reshit* will remain, meaning "beginning." Join the fourth letter, *Shin*, with the *Beth* and the last letter, *Tau*, and there will be *Shabbat*, "end" or "rest." Take only the first three letters and they make *Bra*, "He created." Leaving the *Beth*, take the three subsequent letters and you will have *Rosh*, "head" or "chief." With the first two removed, the two following will be *Esh*, "fire." Join the fourth with the last—namely *Shin* and *Tau*—and there will be *Seth*, "foundation." The second, *Resh*, with the first, *Beth*, makes *Rab*, meaning "great." If after the third letter, *Aleph*, you place the fifth, *Yod*, and then the fourth, *Shin*, there will be *Ish*, "man." The first two letters, *Beth* and *Resh*, with the last two, *Yod* and *Tau*, make *Berith*, "covenant." And the last, *Tau*, with the first, *Beth*, makes *Tov*, "good and laudable." Thus, all this redacted together carries in substance these words: *The Father through the Son, the beginning and the end, created the head...*

<header>HISTORY OF THE ORIGIN OF</header>

"It is believed that Lycophron was at that time renowned not so much for his poetry as for his use of anagrams, etc." <note>original: ἐνδοκεῖ δὲ τότε Λυκόφρον ἐν τοσοῦτον διὰ τὴν ποίησιν ὅσον διὰ τὸ λέγειν ἀναγραμματισμοὺς. Lycophron of Chalcis (3rd century BCE) was a Greek poet famous for his complex wordplay.</note> Regarding this, one should see what Eustathius writes in his commentary on Homer’s *Iliad*, as well as Constantinus and Henri Estienne in their *Thesauri* <note>The *Thesaurus Graecae linguae*, a massive Greek-Latin dictionary published in 1572.</note> of the Greek language. From this artifice depend the **Acrostics** of words, which are found in several passages of Greek authors and in some places in Holy Scripture, through which great secrets are revealed, even concerning the *Messiah*. Saint Augustine in Book 18 of *The City of God*, Chapter 23, following Cicero and Lactantius, brings forward such an example from the Sibyl in Greek verses, where the first letters of each line, when joined together, form these words: *Jesus Christ Son of God Savior* <note>original: Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς Θεοῦ υἱὸς σωτήρ. This forms the Greek word ICHTHYS (fish), a famous early Christian symbol.</note>. And in the first place, in Genesis 49 <note>The source text says "Exode 49," likely an error for Genesis 49:10.</note>: "Shiloh shall come, and to him [shall the gathering of the people be]" <note>original: יבא שילה ולו — Iabo Siloh, vel donec veniat Messiah</note>, the first letters of these three words form the name *Shiloh* [ש-ו]. Likewise in Psalm 72: "His name shall endure, and they shall be blessed" <note>original: ינין שמו וית ברכו — Ianin Semo, vait barcu</note>; and in Psalm 96, again in this place: "Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth be glad; let the sea be moved, and the fullness thereof; let the fields be joyful, and all that is in them." These are all predictions of the Messiah; the first letters of the first four words, *Yismehu, Hashamayim, Vetagel, Haaretz*, form the great <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter divine name of God: YHWH.</note> יהוה *Jehovah*. And those of the three subsequent words—*Yirham, Hayam, Umlo'o*—form the same again, but without the final *He* [ה], which denotes human nature, which Christ had not yet clothed himself in at the time of this prediction. Finally, the other first letters of the three remaining words, namely *Ya'aloz Saday, Vekol Asher-bo*, form the name of *Jesu*. There are infinite other such mysteries that present themselves on every side in Scripture and in the books of the Sibyls, according to Cicero in the second book of *On the Nature of the Gods*, and in some verses by the poet Ennius. However, I will make no further particular mention of them here, to advance my subject; contenting myself for the present to say that our French language is very well-suited and convenient—just as are Hebrew and Greek—for these Anagrams. This can be seen by many names and surnames turned and reversed, which are found in books composed on this matter, such as the poems of Jean Dorat, the poems and anagrams of Sylvain and Nicolas Clément of Troyes, and other modern writers. Above all authors, one should consult Caspar Peucer in his book on the *Principal Types of Divinations* <note>Gaspard Peucer (1525–1602), a German scholar who wrote on magic and divination.</note> and Blaise de Vigenère in his *Treatise on Ciphers*.

# CHAP. XVI.

Above we have explained how the Hebrews performed Anagrams and inversions of names, and from how many letters and how many "houses" and words these curious observations can be built. Now it is very necessary to speak and treat in this place of the other mystery of the aforementioned Hebrews called צירוף <term>Ziruph</term> (or *Ziruf*), which means "Combination." This we can define or explain as the formal pairings and exchanges of Hebrew letters, when they are moved and commuted from their true function and power into others through transpositions.

This artifice is almost the same as the sort of divination by numbers commonly used and practiced today among the Moors and Africans called *Zairagia* <note>The *Zairja* was a complex mechanical device or system of tables used by medieval Muslim scholars to generate answers to questions through numerical and literal combinations.</note>, which is to say, in the Moorish language, Kabbalah, or "traditional reception." This **Ziruph** or **Ziruf**, a word derived from the Hebrew verb צרף *Zaraf* <note>meaning "to refine" or "to purge," often in the context of smelting metal</note> (as Guillaume Postel <note>A 16th-century French polymath and Christian Kabbalist</note> explains at length in his commentaries on the **Ieziraph** <note>The *Sefer Yetzirah* or "Book of Creation," a foundational text of Jewish mysticism</note>), which signifies in the Hebrew language "to purge," is performed by the arrangement and conjunction of the letters of the Hebrew Alphabet two by two. It involves marrying and coupling Aleph with all the aforementioned letters; Beth, likewise; Gimel, similarly; and so on with the others following. From these marriages and couplings, the Hebrews embrace as many orders and ranks as there are Hebrew elements, which are twenty-two in the whole Hebrew Alphabet, as taught by Rabbi Isaac, Jacob Cohen, Tedacus Levi, and other Hebrew Rabbis and Kabbalists in their commentaries on the said *Jezirah*: and by Johannes Reuchlin (also called Capnio) in the third book of *The Art of the Kabbalah*.

> The fourth species and third part of the Kabbalah is **Ziruph**, that is, literary exchange, so that a word written with certain letters symbolically designates another word composed of other letters. This is done through alphabetical revolution according to the *Book of Jezira*—that is, the Creation of Abraham—with twenty-two variations, corresponding to the twenty-two alphabets read there. The aforementioned G. Postel, in the place cited above, wrote the following about it: *Ziruf* <note>original: "Ziruf est in lingua sancta mutatio, sed formalis."</note> in the holy language is a change, but a formal one. For because the proper meaning of the word *Zaraf* <note>original: "צרף"</note> is "to purge"—as gold or another metal is usually purged in fire—therefore this change is properly "formal," while another is "material." For *Themurah* <note>original: "Themurah, est proprie mutatio." This refers to another system of kabbalistic letter substitution.</note> is properly a change where the underlying material does not change; but *Ziruf* belongs to a more obedient nature, driven by will alone, such as the nature of forms. Concerning this sense, the author of the Talmudic *Arukh* <note>original: "Haruchi Talmudici." The *Arukh* is a famous 11th-century dictionary of the Talmud and Midrash.</note> says: "It is handed down from the *Mishnah* <note>original: "Ex Miſna traditum est." The Mishnah is the first major written collection of Jewish oral traditions.</note>: On the day that Jeroboam set up the calves, one in Bethel and the other in Dan, there was constructed, like a building, a *Tzarif* <note>original: "צריף"</note>, that is, a combination and a transfer of power from one to another; and this refers to Italy and Greece. For whenever a special alteration is made in the Church of God against the will of God, it is also made in the world and the common Church." Even though Romulus had not yet founded Rome in Italy then (which happened 240 years later), nor Alexander 500 years later, it was nevertheless foreseen by the saints that there would be a change of the power of the Macedonians to the Kingdom of the Romans. *Themurah*, therefore, will represent the substantial and constitutive number of letters; **Ziruf** represents the ratio of number and power ordered among the letters themselves, from which come the changes of all the kingdoms of the world.

# HISTORY OF THE ORIGIN OF THE

...the great antiquity of secret writing and ciphers, which undoubtedly first came from the Hebrews regarding these **Ziruphs** or **Zirufs** <note>Also spelled *Tziruf*; a Kabbalistic method of permuting or combining letters to reveal hidden meanings.</note>. On this subject, those who are curious enough to meditate at leisure will undoubtedly find many beautiful and excellent ways of writing in all languages. To avoid wordiness, we shall intentionally leave these to their own diligent research and mental dexterity. For this is the true root and foundation of all types of ciphers that proceed by way of transpositions and exchanges of letters, whether they be simple or double. However, this system is not here in its complete square form, but only halfway—namely, the part from the right side moving toward the left, following the Hebrew fashion of writing. Nor does it follow the same order and sequence of letters, but rather another manner of coupling peculiar to the Kabbalists. They devised it for their own use, both for the extraction of divine names from certain passages of the Hebrew Scripture and for the investigation and research of the internal sense hidden beneath the apparent and external context of the literal text.

For example, the word מצפץ **Mazpaz** <note>A mystical name derived from the Tetragrammaton through a substitution cipher.</note> is associated with the reign of David, called **Malchut** <note>The Hebrew word for "Kingdom," the tenth and final Sephirah in the Kabbalistic Tree of Life, representing the physical world.</note>, and consequently with the Messiah. Although it is not found literally in the Scripture, it is nonetheless a cipher and symbol of the ineffable four-letter name יהוה <note>The Tetragrammaton: the sacred name of God, often rendered as YHWH.</note>. It is drawn from the **Ethbas** <note>More commonly known today as *Atbash*, a substitution cipher where the first letter of the alphabet is replaced by the last, the second by the second-to-last, and so on.</note>, or the 22nd and final Alphabet of the **Ziruphs**, **Zirufs**, and permutations. As can be seen here, the מ **Mem** is substituted for the י **Iod**, the צ **Tsadai** for the ה **He**, the פ **Pe** for the ו **Vau**, and the צ **Tsadai** again for the ה **He**. 

This word is composed of **Maz**, which in the 5th and 6th order of Hebrew verb conjugations means "has sucked and squeezed," which befits **Malchut**, the **Sephirot** or numeration of the Moon <note>In traditional cosmology, the Sephirah of Malchut is often associated with the Moon because it reflects the light of the higher emanations.</note>, which receives all impressions from above to pressure and squeeze them into the world below. It is also composed of **Paz**, which in the first conjugation means to cry out and sing for joy, as it is written:
> Lord, you shall open my lips, and my mouth shall declare your praise. *Psalm 51*.

And in the second conjugation, it signifies making an incision, opening, separating, wounding, or delivering:
> I shall kill, and I shall make to live. *Deuteronomy 32*. <note>original Latin: "Ego occidam, & ego viuere faciam"</note>

Regarding the first point, one need only reverse the pairings to make the system square and complete: just as at the beginning where **Aleph** and **Lamed** are joined together, turn them around and you will have **Lamed** and **Aleph**, and so on for the rest, following what is written in the **Iezirah** <note>The *Sefer Yetzirah* or "Book of Creation."</note>: "Regarding which matter God appended the letters and permuted them: Aleph with all, and all with Aleph; Beth with all, and all with Beth" <note>original Latin: "Quæ de re appédit literas Deus, & permutauit eas: Aleph cum omnibus, & omnes cũ Aleph: Beth cum omnibus, & omnes cum Beth"</note>; and toward the end: "God made all things, one corresponding to the other" <note>original Latin: "omnia fecit vnum è regione alterius, Deus"</note>.

Saint Jerome and others believed that the Prophet Jeremiah, in his 25th chapter, followed this artifice by writing ששך **Scefzac** <note>Sheshakh</note> in place of בבל **Babel** <note>Babylon</note>, for fear that the King of Babylon might be provoked to anger against the Israelites. On this subject, see what **Sebastian Munster** <note>A 16th-century German cartographer and Hebraist.</note> wrote after the Hebrews in his annotations on this Prophet in his Hebrew Bible. In fact, **Jonathan** in his Chaldean Paraphrase <note>The Targum Jonathan, an ancient Aramaic translation/interpretation of the Hebrew Bible.</note>, who flourished long before the Incarnation, notably translated it as בבל **Babel** where the aforementioned Prophet wrote ששך in Hebrew, which otherwise has no meaning. These discourses will give us a clear interpretation of the following words taken from Book 3 of the *Kabbalistic Art* by **Jean Reuchlin Capnion** <note>A pioneering Christian humanist and scholar of Kabbalah (1455–1522).</note>: "I shall perhaps show you much more hidden things in this third..."

# LANGUAGES OF THIS UNIVERSE.

In that part of the Kabbalah named **Temurah** <note>original: *Themurah*; the branch of Jewish mysticism dealing with the transposition and substitution of letters to find hidden meanings</note>, where a mutual substitution of letter for letter occurs, this happens as many times as the alphabets are permuted. They are permuted twenty-two times according to the number of letters, because we count twenty-two Jewish letters. It is always possible, by joining any two letters, to take one for the other, and that combination is called <term>עירוף</term> <note>original: *Tzeruf* or *Ziruph*; the art of combining and permuting letters</note>. 

For instance, if I were to continually join these letters of the Latin alphabet—A, B, C, D, E, F—in pairs, so that under the first "yoke" <note>A metaphor for a pairing or coupling of two items</note> are A and B, under the second C and D, and under the third E and F; and if I wished to use a letter to urge someone skilled in this art to fall before the feet of a prince as a suppliant, I would write **DBCF**. He would understand this as **Cade** <note>Latin for "Fall" or "Yield"; by substituting D for C, B for A, C for D, and F for E</note>. The same applies to others. 

This entire mechanism arises from an alphabetic revolution or rotation, so that letters coupled in their own "yoke" succeed one another: namely, *a* for *b* and *b* for *a*; similarly *c* for *d* and *d* for *c*; and likewise *e* for *f* and *f* for *e*. This proceeds more easily in the Hebrew language without any hindrance, because the sounds which the Latins call vowels are not placed within the standard order of the Jewish alphabet <note>Hebrew is an "abjad," where the primary alphabet consists of consonants, and vowels are not treated as full letters in the sequence as they are in Latin</note>. 

Therefore, in an ancient age, our father Abraham, moved by this principle, said (as read in the *Book of Yetzirah* <note>original: *lib. Iezira*; the "Book of Formation," one of the most important works of early Jewish mysticism</note>, chapter 12): "Aleph with all, and all with Aleph; Beth with all, and all with Beth," and so on for each individual letter. This same author says afterwards: the mixing of Hebrew elements must not be understood in a crude or unlearned way, for all things are spirits. Thus it is written in the said *Book of Yetzirah*: "And with that spirit, God engraved twenty-two letters: three mothers, seven doubles, and twelve simples <note>The three categories of Hebrew letters in Kabbalistic thought, representing different elemental and cosmological forces</note>, and every one of them is spirit." Therefore, these things have been handed down to us for contemplation, to be approached spiritually and with great joy—not for mockery or speaking against them. Rather, one must embrace the mysteries of the Scriptures with pious faith, and so forth.

### HISTORY OF THE ORIGIN OF
<meta>catchword: Kabbalah</meta>

the great antiquity of secret writing and ciphers which, without any doubt, first came from the Hebrews regarding these <term>Ziruphs</term> <note>original: *Ziruphs* or *Zirufs*; from the Hebrew *Tzeruf*, meaning the permutation or combination of letters</note>. Upon this, those who are curious to meditate at leisure will find, without any doubt, many beautiful and excellent manners of writing in all languages. To avoid wordiness, we shall leave these specifically to their own curious research and dexterity of mind. For this is the true root and foundation of all types of ciphers that proceed by way of transpositions and commutations of letters, whether they be simple or double. However, this system is not in its complete "square" <note>Referring to a complete grid of all possible letter combinations</note>, but rather only half-complete; namely, the part from the right side moving to the left, following the Hebrew fashion of writing. It does not follow the standard order and sequence of letters, but rather another manner of coupling specific to the Kabbalists. They devised this for their own use, both for the extraction of divine names from certain passages of the Hebrew Scripture and for the investigation and research of the internal sense hidden beneath the apparent and exterior context of the letter. 

For example, the word **מצפץ** <note>original: *Mazpaz*</note>, appropriated to the reign of David, called <term>Malchut</term> <note>The Sephirah of "Kingdom," representing the physical world and the presence of God in creation</note>, and consequently to the Messiah. Although this word is not found in the Scripture, it is nevertheless a cipher and symbol of the ineffable Four-letter Name **יהוה** <note>The Tetragrammaton, YHWH</note>. It is drawn from the <term>Ethbas</term> <note>Atbash: a substitution cipher where the first letter of the alphabet is replaced by the last, the second by the second-to-last, etc.</note>, or the 22nd and final alphabet of permutations, as one can see here: where the **מ** (*Mem*) is put for the **י** (*Yod*), **צ** (*Tsadai*) for **ה** (*He*), **פ** (*Pe*) for **ו** (*Vau*), and **צ** (*Tsadai*) again for **ה** (*He*). 

And this word is composed of *Maz*, which in the fifth and sixth order of Hebrew verb conjugations signifies "has sucked and squeezed out" <note>Refers to the extraction of divine essence or influence</note>. This is appropriate to *Malchut*, the Sephirah or numeration of the Moon <note>In some older Kabbalistic schemes, the Moon was associated with Malchut because it reflects light from above, though it is more commonly associated with the Sephirah of Yesod</note>, which receives all impressions from above to press and squeeze them out below. It is also composed of *Paz*, which in the first conjugation means as much as to cry out and sing with joy, as it is written: *Lord, you shall open my lips, and my mouth shall announce your praise* (Psalm 51). In the second conjugation, it signifies making an incision, opening, separating, wounding, or delivering:

> I shall kill, and I shall make to live. (Deuteronomy 32) <note>original: *Ego occidam, & ego viuere faciam*</note>

Regarding the first point, then, one only needs to reverse the couplings to make the system square and complete. For instance, right at the start where **Aleph** and **Lamed** are joined together, turn them backward and you will have **Lamed** and **Aleph**; and so with the rest, following what is written in the <term>Jezirah</term> <note>The *Sefer Yetzirah* or *Book of Formation*, one of the oldest and most influential books of Jewish mysticism</note>:

> For which reason God weighed the letters and permuted them: Aleph with all [others], and all with Aleph; Beth with all, and all with Beth. <note>original: *Qua de re appédit literas Deus, & permutauit eas: Aleph cum omnibus, & omnes cū Aleph: Beth cum omnibus, & omnes cum Beth*</note>

And toward the end:

> God made all things, one over against the other. <note>original: *omnia fecit vnum è regione alterius, Deus*</note>

Saint Jerome and others believed that the Prophet Jeremiah, in his 25th chapter, followed this artifice and put **ששך** <note>original: *Sheshach*</note> in place of **בבל** <note>original: *Babel* or Babylon</note>, for fear that the King of Babylon might become irritated and enraged against the Israelites. Regarding this, see what Sebastian Münster wrote (following the Hebrews) in his annotations on this Prophet in his Hebrew Bible. Indeed, Jonathan in his Chaldean Paraphrase <note>The Targum of Jonathan, an ancient Aramaic translation/interpretation of the Prophets</note>, who flourished long before the Incarnation, notably translated it as *Babylon* where the aforementioned Prophet wrote *Sheshach* in Hebrew, which otherwise has no meaning. These discussions will give us a clear interpretation of the following words taken from Book 3 of *The Kabbalistic Art* by Johannes Reuchlin (also known as Capnion): *Perhaps I shall show you much more hidden things in this third [book]...* <note>original: *Multò fortè occultiora, ostendam vobis in hac tertia*</note>

X 3

In the part of the Kabbalah named <term>Themurah</term> <note>original: *Themurah*; Hebrew for "Exchange" or "Substitution," a method of creating ciphers by swapping letters</note>, where a mutual substitution of letter for letter takes place, this occurs as many times as the alphabets are permuted. It is permuted twenty-two times, according to the number of letters, because we read that there are twenty-two letters of the Jews. By always joining any two letters, it will be permitted to take one in place of the other; that combination is called <term>Tzeruf</term> <note>original: צרוף (*Tzeruf*); meaning "combination" or "permutation"</note>. 

For example, if from these letters of the Latin alphabet—**A, B, C, D, E, F**—I were to continuously join them in pairs, so that under the first "yoke" <note>An image used to describe a fixed pairing of two letters</note> are **A** and **B**, under the second **C** and **D**, and under the third **E** and **F**, and I wished to use this art to encourage someone in a letter to fall before the feet of a prince to petition him, I would write **DBCF**. He would understand this as **Cade** <note>Latin: *Cade*, the imperative form of "fall" or "drop down." Using the cipher: D=C, B=A, C=D, F=E</note>; and so it goes for others. This entire mechanism results from an alphabetical revolution so that letters succeed each other mutually, combined in their own assigned "yoke"—namely, **a** for **b** and **b** for **a**; similarly **c** for **d** and **d** for **c**, and likewise **e** for **f** and **f** for **e**. 

This process proceeds more easily in Hebrew without any obstacle, because the sounds which the Latins name are not arranged in the same order as the alphabet of the Jews. Therefore, moved by this in an ancient age, our father **Abraham** said—as is read in the <term>Book of Yetzirah</term> <note>original: *lib. Iezira*; the *Sefer Yetzirah* or "Book of Formation," a primary text of early Kabbalah</note>, chapter 12: **Aleph with all, and all with Aleph, no differently than Beth with all, and all with Beth**, and so with each individual letter. 

This same author says afterward: **The joining of the Hebrew elements is by no means to be understood crudely or ignorantly; for all things are spirits.** Thus it is written in the said Book of Yetzirah: **And God carved with that spirit twenty-two letters: three mothers, seven doubles, and twelve simples** <note>This refers to the three categories of Hebrew letters: the 3 "Mothers" (Aleph, Mem, Shin), the 7 "Doubles" (letters with two sounds), and the 12 "Simples" (the remaining letters)</note>, **and each of them is spirit.** Therefore, these things have been handed down to us to be contemplated spiritually with great joy, not for speaking ill or for mocking, but to embrace the mysteries of the scriptures with pious faith, and so forth.

### *Concerning the Atbash or Aethbaz of the Hebrews.*

### CHAPTER 17.

From the secret and mystery of the **Ziruphs** <note>original: *Ziruphs* or *Zirufs*; from the Hebrew *Tzeruf*, meaning the permutation or combination of letters</note> discussed above, there proceeds another that the Kabbalists call אתבש **ATBASH**, which is to say, the reversed Hebrew alphabet. We might call this an *orchésme* <note>from the Greek for dance, here meaning a rhythmic movement or shifting</note> or transposition, and a leaping of Hebrew letters into one another within the Hebrew alphabet. This is clearly explained, following the ancient Hebrew doctors, by **George the Venetian** in his *Harmony of the World* <note>Francesco Zorzi (1466–1540), author of *De harmonia mundi*</note>, **J. Mercier** in his booklet on Hebrew abbreviations, **Theodore Bibliander** in his commentary on all languages and letters in the chapter on secret letters, **Guy le Fèvre de la Boderie** in his Syro-Chaldean dictionary under the word *Atbash*, and his brother **Nicolas** in his introduction to the harmony of the aforementioned George the Venetian. This artifice is for the most part ingenious, shrouded, intricate, and full of many difficulties; nonetheless, it was treated by the great **Abbot Trithemius** in his *Polygraphia*, and after him by **B. de Vigenère** in his treatise on ciphers.

Here is an example of it reported by the Kabbalists regarding the beginning of Ezekiel in these words: (*being seated in the midst of the captives on the bank of the river Chobar*). Here, these Kabbalists interpret this **כבור** <note>Chobar</note> by this same *Atbash* or *Ethbaz*, or transposition of letters, as **כרוב** <note>Cherub</note>, which is to say an influence of the Cherubim, Angels of the second order. For these are the same letters differently arranged. Furthermore, the word "river" relates and corresponds very well to the word "influence," because they both come from the verb "to flow" or "to stream," just as it is the nature of rivers to always tend downward until they swallow themselves into the sea, which is the great receptacle of all things. So too is it with influx, which, no more than intelligence, never ascends, as **Zoroaster** writes in these Greek words: <note>original: νόησις μήποτε ἀναβαίνει</note> "understanding never ascends." And yet God always flows without ceasing through his channels like a perpetual source of living water without ever flowing back up; for where could it rise higher, given that the throne of His essence is above all? Of this descent of the divinity into inferior things, **Rabbi Joseph Castilian** <note>Joseph Gikatilla (1248–1305), author of *Sha'arei Orah*</note> speaks thus in the *Gates of Light*, following the ancient Kabbalists:

At the beginning of the creation of the world, the divine cohabitation <note>Referring to the *Shekhinah*, or the Divine Presence</note> was descending into inferior things; and as the divinity dwelt here below, the heavens and the earth found themselves united together and were the sources and the channels that flowed from it, acting in perfection, drawn from on high toward below, God accomplishing everything by the same means, both above and below. Thus, the river **Chobar** in this cipher stands in place of the first "shell" or outer covering of the mysteries of the Hebrews; the influence of the **Cherub**, to which this is appropriated, is the second, which covers the third, where finally the true sense and intelligence reside: namely, the light of the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter divine name YHWH (יהוה)</note> **יהוה**, of which it is written in Psalm 36: <note>original: *In lumine tuo videbimus lumen*</note> "In your light shall we see light," which is to say that by the light of the Son we shall see that of the Father. It was this light that descended into the understanding of the Prophet, through the second order...

->*On the Gematria of the Hebrews.*<-

### CHAP. XVIII.

Here is another wonderful mystery of the Hebrews for interpreting and clarifying their Hebrew scriptures, which they call <term>Gematria</term> <note>original: גמטריא (*Ghematria*)</note>. <note>The author provides a Latin definition: "That is, a calculation of numbers, as if a numerical measurement of earthly characters in turn, which nevertheless depends on that Arithmetic because of its abstract simplicity, untouchable by any senses, whence it is named Geometry rather than Arithmetic, although both are worth one and the same thing in this art."</note> By this method, as Kimhi says regarding Zechariah 3, <term>The Branch</term> <note>original Latin: *Germen*; Hebrew: צמח (*Tzemach*)</note> has the same value as <term>The Comforter</term> <note>original Latin: *Consolator*; Hebrew: מנחם (*Menachem*)</note>, which is a name of the Messiah, since the letters of both names result in the number 148 <note>In standard gematria, both words actually sum to 138; the author or printer may be using a variant calculation or there is a historical error in the source text.</note>. Similarly, in the *Tikkun Hazohar*, "the Throne" <note>original: כסא (*Kisse*)</note>—by way of <term>Antonomasia</term> <note>The use of a title or epithet in place of a proper name</note>—has the same value as <term>Elohim</term> <note>original: אלהים</note>, one of the divine names, since the letters of both names taken separately total 86.

Some Hebrew doctors and others have written that this Hebrew word, *Gematria*, which is an equivalence of Hebrew numbers, measures, and proportions, originates and proceeds <margin>from geometry <note>original Greek: ἀπὸ τῆς γεωμετρίας</note></margin>, as reported quite well by Elias Levita in his *Tishbi*, Guy le Fèvre de la Boderie in his Syro-Chaldaic dictionary, and his brother Nicolas in his introduction to the *Harmony of the World* by Georges de Venise <note>Francesco Zorzi, a famous Franciscan Kabbalist</note> regarding the interpretation of this word. However, in practice, this mystery does not fully retain its literal definition, for it relates more to number, and occurs when one word is substituted and extended for another through equality and calculation. The Kabbalists even construct systems of occult and secret writing through this path of Gematria—systems based on numbers and points on one hand, and the lengths of lines on the other, which they then disguise in many diverse sorts and manners. The <term>Ghilgul</term> <note>original: גלגול (*Ghilgul*), usually meaning "cycle" or "rolling"</note>, which is a "numerical quantity," is one part and rule of this system. For this reason, Rabbi Joseph of Salem (as I have already noted elsewhere) titled a discourse of his on these systems and secrets <term>Ghinat</term> <note>original: גנת (*Ghinat*)</note>—that is, Gematria, Notariacon, and Temurah—according to Johannes Reuchlin (also called Capnion) in book 3 of the *Art of the Kabbalah*, J. Mercier in his pamphlet on Hebrew abbreviations, and Guy le Fèvre de la Boderie in his Syro-Chaldaic dictionary.

# LANGUAGES OF THIS UNIVERSE

Cabalists <note>Practitioners of Kabbalah, a tradition of Jewish mysticism.</note> celebrate the letters of this word מלח *Malach* <note>original: מלח (*Melach*)</note>, which signifies salt, for rising in the calculation of their numbers to 78. For *Mem* is worth 40; *Lamed*, 30; and *Het*, 8. Now, divide these 78 in whatever way you wish, and there will always result some number that represents a mystery of the divine names. For example, half is thirty-nine, as much as the letters of כוזו *Chuzu* <note>original: כוזו (*Kuzu*), a protective name of God often written on the back of Mezuzah scrolls.</note> amount to—the "sheath" or "scabbard," as they interpret it, of the Great Name—namely *Kaph* twenty, *Vav* six, *Zayin* seven, and *Vav* again six. If divided into three parts, each will amount to twenty-six, which is the number of the Tetragrammaton <term>Tetragrammaton|The four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH.</term> יהוה: in six parts, they will be thirteen, which are equal to the measure of piety <note>The Hebrew word for "One" (*Echad*) also totals 13.</note>; in thirteen parts, they will be six, which is the value of the *Vav*, a letter representing the life from above, and six is the first perfect number. In twenty-six parts, it will be the number of the most holy and sacred Trinity, three; in thirty-nine parts, two, which is the value of the *Beth*, a symbol of the Word, or the second person and the "house of ideas" of the Archetype; and finally, the seventy-eight denote as many units, each of which represents the unity of a single God.

It is exactly the same with the word לחם *Lechem* <note>original: לחם</note> meaning bread, which is an anagram of the preceding word, whereby the letters similarly yield seventy-eight: *Lamed* thirty, *Het* eight, and *Mem* forty. But יין *Iain* <note>original: יין (*Yayin*)</note> or wine is worth only seventy, a number proceeding from the multiplication of ten by 7, which concerns the soul, which has its seat in the blood, into which wine is very easily converted. By this means, the Divinity has always taken great delight in these two substances of bread and wine, both for the mystery they denote of His Church—composed of many souls united in a common consent of belief, in imitation of how bread is made of many grains of wheat kneaded together, and wine is pressed from clusters of grapes—and because of the incorruptibility in which they participate more than any others, arising from the quintessence <term>quintessence|In alchemy, the purest "fifth element" or essence of a substance.</term> of the "water of life" <note>likely referring to alcohol or spirits</note> which resides there in great abundance. They are also coupled in the first book of Esdras, chapter six, with salt and oil as the four most useful and necessary things that Nature produces.

To make it short, Gematria <term>Ghematrie|Gematria; the system of assigning numerical value to a word or phrase.</term> is a circular revolution and a square and cubic multiplication containing many devices that depend principally on formal Arithmetic and Geometry employed in the profound meditations of the Hebrew Cabala. The aforementioned J. Reuchlin <note>Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522), a pioneering German humanist and scholar of Hebrew.</note>, in the place cited above, says these words:

> The Cabalistic Art consists of three principal things: first, the calculation of numbers which is named Geometry <note>meaning Gematria</note>, as if it were a numerical dimension of earthly characters, which nonetheless depends on that Arithmetic which, due to its abstract simplicity, is not manageable by any senses, and therefore is not subject to a crude or novice craft. Thus, the first part was called Geometry rather than Arithmetic, although both actually count as one and the same in this art. Then, syllables are sometimes transmuted, so that there is a transformed word, or a word is simply inverted. Secondly, a letter is put for a word, and it is called *Notariacum* <note>Notarikon</note> from the shorthand of Notaries, since there every letter is noted at the top so as to be a sign of some whole word. Thirdly, this art consists in the change of letters, when one is ingeniously placed for another, and it is called commutation <note>Temurah</note>, which is why Rabbi Joseph the Younger of Salerno called the books he wrote on this art "The Garden"—

# HISTORY OF THE ORIGIN OF

> -> ...[know] because of the three letters of this word ת <note>original: *Tav*</note>, as each of them designates one of the three portions of the Cabalistic art. For *Gimel* signifies *Gematria*, *Nun* signifies *Notaricon*, and *Tav* signifies *Temurah*. Thus, these are the parts of the entire art: *Gematria*, which is Arithmetic; *Notaricon*, as it were a system of shorthand; and *Temurah*, which is the transposition of elements, etc. <note>original Latin: *...nauerit.i.n. ת propter ternas huius dictionis literas...*</note> <-

In short, from what we have deduced above, we shall learn that the mystery or artifice of the aforementioned Cabalists <note>Practitioners of Kabbalah, Jewish mystical tradition.</note>, called *Gematria*—a word undoubtedly corrupted from that of *Geometry* as I have already stated—by which they also understand *Arithmetic*, without which Geometry cannot exist, nor can measures and figures exist without numbers. Arithmetic, which is simpler and more formal, does quite well without Geometry, which is more material and coarse, just as figures are more material than numbers. Indeed, just as speech and writing cannot exist without some premeditation of thought, whereas thought can certainly exist without speech or writing. 

They might also, perhaps, have been moved to give these two sciences, joined together, the name of the second—namely Geometry—for it is a modern term, rather than that of the first, Arithmetic, because Plato magnifies it so much in the seventh book of the *Republic*, calling it the knowledge of *That which always is*. <margin>For geometrical knowledge is of that which always exists. <note>original Greek: *τῆς γὰρ ἀεὶ ὄντος, ἡ γεωμετρικὴ γνῶσίς ἐστιν* (Plato, Republic 7.527b).</note></margin> And in another place, according to the citation by Plutarch in the second question of the eighth book of the *Symposiacs* <note>Also known as *Table Talk* (*Quaestiones Conviviales*).</note>, he posits that God practices it continually. On this, he discourses that Lycurgus banished Arithmetical proportion from Lacedaemon <note>Sparta.</note> in order to introduce Geometrical proportion. By the former, he denoted a tumultuous confusion of the Common People, which consists in number, and consequently concerns equality, where everyone is the master "like rats in straw." By Geometry, he denoted reason; because it lies in the difference of lines, longer or shorter. This denotes the authority that the great, and people of virtue, honor, counsel, and foresight, must have over the ignorant and brutal Common Populace—the majority of whom are also vicious, debauched, reckless, and hasty, seeking nothing but equality, than which there is nothing more unjust or pernicious in a state. 

By this means, God, in all things, insofar as they permit and as it can be done, withdraws equality from the world; he observes in its place merit geometrically, and dignity, concluding everything according to reason. Plato, therefore, by "the greater" and "the lesser," describes not only matter, as Aristotle would attribute to him, but forms as well, together with all the compounds of these two, according to the degrees of their essence and perfection—neither more nor less than Pythagoras before him had done through the even and the odd number, and Empedocles through the *Dense* and the *Rare* <note>original: *l'Espoix & le Rare*</note> which he established among the Principles. 

In imitation of this, the Cabalists have constructed systems of occult writing through the path of the aforementioned *Gematria*, established on the number of points on one hand, and lengths on the other, which they afterwards disguise in several ways. As I have already remarked above regarding this, B. de Vigenère <note>Blaise de Vigenère (1523–1596), a French diplomat and cryptographer famous for the "Vigenère cipher."</note> in his treatise on ciphers—wishing not to enter into too long an extension of these lines—contented himself with deducing eight differences, each of which serves reciprocally for two letters. These are discerned by certain small marks and secret notes difficult to perceive, for fear of engendering some suspicion of the ruse; thus does this figure particularly deduce it...

->*Of the Notariacum or Notaricon of the Hebrews.*<-

### CHAP. XIX.

The *Notariacon* of the Hebrews is another admirable mystery for interpreting and clarifying their said Hebrew scriptures and the secrets within them. It is so called נוטריקון <note>Hebrew: *Notariacon*</note>, a word composed of the roots *Notar* and *Tetkon*, meaning to preserve a word or figure; this is because, in the manner of Notaries and legal practitioners, it is fashioned from certain assembled Hebrew letters, each of which—without the joining of syllables—represents and takes the place of an entire word. Sometimes, also through a certain conciseness <term>Laconicism|The use of very few words to convey much meaning, named after the Spartans of Laconia</term> or in the manner of an oracle, a single sound or an entire word carries as much weight as an entire clause, expression, or sentence. This is clearly taught by Elias Levita in his *Thesbite* in the interpretation of this word; Johann Reuchlin (Capnion) in Book 3 of *The Cabalistic Art*; Jean Mercier in his treatise on Hebrew abbreviations; Sixtus of Siena in Book 3 of his *Sacred Library*, the seventh method of Notaricon exposition; Father Louis in Book 10, chapters 12 and 13 of *Divine Hebrew Secrets*; Guy Lefèvre de la Boderie in his Syriac-Chaldean dictionary; and in the introduction by his brother Nicolas to the *Harmony of the World* by Giorgio Veneto. This method of abbreviation, taken from the first letters of Hebrew words and speech (of which they form marks and figures), is called by the Hebrews ראשי תיבות <note>Hebrew: *Rasce Theuoth*</note>, meaning "Head of the Dictions," and is represented among the Hebrews by the two letters רת <note>The initials R and T</note>. These Hebrews say that the word גנת <note>GNT</note> is an acronym <note>original: *in Rasce Theuot*</note> where these three letters signify the three parts of the Cabala, which we call Gematria, Notaricon, and Temurah. This follows a certain Rabbi Joseph of Salems <note>Referencing Joseph Gikatilla, author of Ginnat Egoz</note>, who composed his books under the name *Ghinai Egoz*: "The Garden of Nuts" (from the Song of Solomon, chapter 6) <note>original Latin: *hortum nucis, Cantic. 6*</note>; and from this, many others have attached excellent and pleasant titles to their own books. Gematria is one, and the other method of abbreviation, taken from the last letters of the said words and Hebrew phrases, is called סוף תיבות <note>Hebrew: *Soph Theuoth*</note>, the "End of the Dictions" or terms, and is represented in Hebrew by two other letters, סת <note>The initials S and T</note>. This is confirmed by the aforementioned Reuchlin, Mercier, Guy Lefèvre de la Boderie, and his brother Nicolas in the places cited before. There are also other species of Notaricon among the said Hebrews: the first being when all the Hebrew letters of a word each separately denote as many words as there are letters. The second, when one takes away the first—

The historian Dio <note>Dio Cassius (c. 155–235 AD), a Roman historian of Greek origin.</note> in his life of the aforementioned Augustus reports that Maecenas, his great friend, was the first among the Romans <note>original: "Latins"</note> to invent these Notes. These were more suitable for the clerks who recorded the pleadings of lawyers—just as the speeches and harangues of Orators were collected in ancient times—than for any other purpose. This was due to the promptness and speed of speech, which passes as suddenly as a well-feathered arrow; for each of these characters or Notes represented at least one word, and most often several, as the poet Ausonius <note>Decimus Magnus Ausonius (c. 310–395 AD), a Roman poet and teacher.</note> testifies:

Saint Cyprian also added to them and adapted the whole system for Christian use in the form of a dictionary, as the Abbot Trithemius <note>Johannes Trithemius (1462–1516), a German abbot, polymath, and pioneer of cryptography.</note> explains at length in the "Key" to his *Polygraphy* <note>original: *Polygraphie*</note>. These are more prompt and flow more lightly under the pen, as we see with the clerks of the sovereign Courts, whose speed of hand not only accompanies but even outpaces the swiftest and most nimble tongues of the lawyers. This is likewise seen in all the scribblings <note>original: "chaffouarechements"</note> and drafts of Notaries, Attorneys, and the writs of bailiffs. 

And to return to the aforementioned "Shorthand" <note>original: *Notariacon*</note> of the Hebrews, it does not depart from their accustomed letters, though it is of several sorts: namely, when a syllable or a letter is put for an entire word, and a word for an entire clause, as we have already said above; and conversely, a clause counted as a single term, and a term for a single letter. As one can see in the *Polygraphy* of the aforementioned Trithemius, this is a quite elegant and ingenious invention in truth, were it not for the prolix and tedious meaning rendered by these synonyms joined one after another, and the little substance they ultimately express. Furthermore, there is another branch of this <term>Notariacon: A Kabbalistic system of shorthand or acronyms where each letter of a word represents another word.</term>, where every letter of a single word denotes its own separate word. Here is a very notable example among others cited by Rabbi Yehuda in his *Book of Hope*: that the prophet Jeremiah, having meditated for a long time on the treatise of formation, the <term>Yetzirah: Sefer Yetzirah, or "Book of Formation," a primary text of Jewish mysticism describing the creation of the world through Hebrew letters.</term>, was one day admonished by *Bath Kol*—the "daughter of the voice," which is what they call divine inspiration, like a silent voice coming from heaven—to persevere for three more consecutive years, specifically on the permutations arising from the *Ziruphs* <note>Combinations or joinings of letters.</note> and the diversity of alphabets. Seeing this in this new human creature, Jeremiah suddenly erased the first letter of the last word, which left only מת, *MET*, which means "dead." At this, the Prophet, quite indignant, began to tear his clothes in anger, and asked the creature why it had cut off the *Aleph* from *Emet*? "Because," the creature replied, "everyone everywhere has departed from the faithfulness of the Creator, who formed you in His image and likeness." "And how shall we know Him?" Jeremiah replied. "Write," said this representation in the form of a man, "the alphabets in spaces in this dust..."
