And there is still to consider the firm and solid <term>quadrature</term> <note>squareness, symbolizing stability</note> such as truth must be: which quadrature is perceived both in the shape of these characters, which are all square, and in their value in calculations: insofar as *Aleph* signifies a thousand also, which is the end of all numbers, and the Cube of ten; *Mem* 40, the same ten multiplied by the four that constitute it, because 1, 2, 3, and 4 make ten; and the *Thau* 400, the square of ten, which is 100, multiplied by the same four, or the four tens by ten: for 10 times 40 make 400. So it is that both the figures and the numbers of these three letters אמת *Emet*, truth, are, in whatever way one may take them, always solid; and those of falsehood, שקר *Secher* <note>Sheker</note>, on the contrary, are weak and wavering, following the proverb, *That a lie has short heels*, as presupposing that it is very easy to overturn. Their numbers, moreover, are all of hundreds, which denote the <term>crassitude of matter</term> <note>the density or "thickness" of the physical world</note>, in perpetual change and alteration: for ש *Schin* is worth 300, *Coph* 100, and *Res* 200. As for removing a letter from the middle of a word, Rabbi Simon in the Talmud of the Jews, having been asked why in this passage of Holy Scripture in Job 38:

> LIGHT SHALL BE TAKEN FROM THE WICKED

one eclipsed from מרשעים, *Mersaim*, which means impious or wicked, the letter ע *Ain*, so that there remained מרשים *Mersim*, by a <term>syncope</term> <note>the omission of a letter or sound from the middle of a word</note>, which no longer means impious, but indigent and suffering: because, he replied, he who in this temporal life makes himself nonchalant in the contemplation of the beauty of the sensible world, will by that same means be deficient in the knowledge of intelligible things, of which the former is like a portrait, and consequently falls into misery regarding the world to come. In truth, he who does not observe, and does not take heed of what is here below exposed to our senses, though fleeting and corruptible, will no longer be able to penetrate to the perception of the invisible and permanent which is up there: just as one cannot recognize the interior thought of a man except by speech or writing, and similar signs and outward marks: which is what the Apostle means in Romans 1, already cited, *That the invisible things of God are made manifest and perceptible to the creature of the world, by those things which were made by him*. Just as for the formation of Eve, one of Adam’s ribs was taken away, so that from the male and the female the multiplication of the human race (subject to sin) might occur; in compensation, the number five was taken from Sara to give it to her husband Abraham. By this means, she was made fertile, whereas she had been barren; consequently, he who was to repair the fault of the first fathers <note>The Messiah</note> was to be born according to the flesh. 

The third species of these Hebrew mysteries or ciphers is also of several sorts, like those mentioned above, which all relate to the various combinations and permutations of letters. According to the *Book of Yetzirah* <note>The Sefer Yetzirah, a foundational text of Jewish mysticism</note>, all creatures—past, present, and future—have been, are, and shall be formed by these. For even the great name of God יהוה [the Tetragrammaton] is written therein (<note>original: "per quem fecit & secula"</note> *through whom he also made the worlds*), in which are found six anagrams through the various transpositions of the three letters of which it is woven—given that the letter *He* [ה] is doubled. These are: יהו [Ihu], which denotes the infinite and the high; יוה [Iuh], the low and the deep abyss; היו [Hiu], the front or the East; הוי [Hui], the back or the West; ויה [Vih], the right hand or the southern part; and והי [Vhi], the left and the North. 

This is because the Kabbalists establish the face of God as if it were turned toward the East, due to the excellence and dignity of that direction, which represents the day and the life symbolized by it. The South, in the middle, is the highest point, because the day ascends that far, from which it then descends toward the West, which denotes night and death. Finally, the North represents the deep or the low; it is, moreover, like a mark of that space of time between the death of the body and its rebirth or resurrection with its own soul, which it will take up again in the future age. 

But one must not understand this "deep," according to the words of the Rabbi, son of Carnitol <note>Joseph Gikatilla, 1248–1305, a famous Spanish Kabbalist</note>, in his *Gates of Justice* <note>The Sha'are Orah or "Gates of Light"</note>, to be "low" in the sense of the bottom of a hollow well. Rather, it refers to anything that is the most distant from being followed or attained, which is properly called *Hamok* [עמוק], encompassing both high and low, the ascent and the descent. As in that song of degrees, Psalm 130: <note>original: "De profundis clamaui ad te Domine"</note> *Out of the depths have I cried unto thee, O Lord*, which this Rabbi interprets as the depth from above, which is the *Ain Soph* [אין סוף] <note>The Infinite or "Without End," the divine essence before manifestation</note> or the infinity of the <term>intelligible world</term>, called *Hamok Hamok* [עמוק עמוק], the deep of deeps. In this regard, the aforementioned *Book of Yetzirah* names the depth of above, the depth of below, the depth of the East, that of the West, the depth of the South, and that of the North—in which it extends on all sides. 

In this manner, the complete revolution of the whole universe is perfected; it is nothing other than a circle—but a finite, bounded, and terminated one—whereas the circle of divinity is infinite, following the words of Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus</note>: <note>original: "cuius circumferentia nusquam"</note> *whose circumference is nowhere*. For the world is not the place of God, but God is the place of the world, so that the Angels exclaim in Ezekiel: <note>original: "Benedicta gloria Dei, de suo loco"</note> *Blessed be the glory of God from his place*. ### CHAP. XX.

The Hebrews have at all times held the ten <term>Sephirots</term> <note>The ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself.</note> in high esteem—that is to say, divine measures and numerations, otherwise named by their Cabalists as the garments of Divinity, as we have remarked before. To each of these Sephirots, these Hebrews and Cabalists attribute one of the divine names. The first of these, which refers to the divine essence אהיה <term>Ehyeh</term> <note>Hebrew: "I shall be."</note> and particularly represents the FATHER, is consoled and flows through the order of the Seraphim to the first mobile heaven <note>The *Primum Mobile*, the outermost sphere of the universe in Ptolemaic astronomy.</note>: and from there to all things to which it gives being. It is called <term>Keter</term> or "crown": and is denoted by the letter ש <term>Shin</term>, which has the shape of a crown with three flourishes, and is a symbol of the TRINITY. But in another fashion, the crown, which is perfectly round, is also marked by that "non-value" in counting figures which is called zero, 0, when it is alone and by itself; but when accompanied by a 1, it makes 10. Thus, the marks of numbers are not at all devoid of mysteries contained beneath their shapes. Furthermore, the name of *Ehyeh*—although the Greeks try to represent it by <term>ho on</term> <note>Greek: ὁ ὤν, "The One Who Is."</note> and the Latins by <term>Ens</term> <note>Latin: "Being" or "Essence."</note>, meaning BEING—cannot, however, be well expressed in any language other than Hebrew by a single word, nor translated except by a circumlocution of words. For being made of four letters, it belongs only to God, whose essence it signifies, insofar as it resides within Him without being explained or going outside. For this reason, it is attributed to the Father, and denotes all three tenses in eternity: and a plurality of persons with a unity of nature. Furthermore, the name *Ehieh* is a name of clemence and mercy, like *Iah* and *El*, attributed to the Father who can never be otherwise toward his children; *as a father has compassion on his children* <note>Latin: "quomodo miseretur pater filiorum"</note>, as Psalm 103 says. For this reason, Scripture ordinarily uses it when it is a matter of requesting some grace from Him, as in Numbers 12: Moses, wishing to obtain the healing of his sister Miriam, who had been struck with leprosy, makes his prayer to God in these terms: *Elna Rapha la* <note>Hebrew: אֵל נָא רְפָא נָא לָהּ</note>, "O God of pity, I beseech thee, heal this woman." Likewise multiply the five which is represented by *He* [ה], it will make 25, and five times 25 will give 125. The *Vav* [ו] which is worth six, will do exactly the same, for 6 times 6 makes 36, and six times 36 [makes] 216, by which one can perceive that the numbers denoted by these three letters—ten for *Iod*, five for *He*, and six for *Vav*—always meet at the end of their products <note>These are known as "automorphic" or "circular" numbers because their powers always end in the same digit</note>: which is not the case for others that always go out of themselves, as two times 2 makes four, which is no longer two; nor two times 4 makes eight, which is neither 2 nor four; two times three makes 6 and three times three 9, and so on for the rest. And in fact, God has a double tribunal: one of severity and rigor, at the left hand in the north, designated by Elohim, principally with the adjective גבור Gibor, strong and robust; and the other of clemency at the right hand, and in the south, following this from the third chapter of Genesis, *he walked lightly toward the south* <note>A mystical interpretation of Gen 3:8; standard translations usually say "in the cool of the day"</note>, not wishing to punish our first parents to the utmost. And in the first chapter of the Canticles: *where you feed, where you lie down at midday* <note>original Latin: "vbi pascas, vbi cubes in meridie"</note>. This is what the name יה Iah carries: which, being drawn from the first two letters of the great name יהוה, if you subtract them from אלהים Elohim, there will remain אלם Ilem, "mute": as if this meant to imply that if from the justice designated by Elohim, you separate the name of mercy, it must remain mute. But it seems rather to be the reverse: for when a prince allows himself, through the importunity of prayers or otherwise, to forgive a wrongdoer or moderate the just punishment he has deserved, this is to close the mouths of his judges and gag them, so that they dare not proceed as they should. Whereas, on the contrary, there is nothing that can make them speak louder than a universal denial and refusal of all these manners of grace, pardons, remissions, and abusive abolitions, obtained illegally—true seeds and nurseries of all malversions and crimes. We must therefore seek the understanding of this mystery elsewhere, and presuppose that just as the future, which is the third tense, includes the two...

# HISTORY OF THE ORIGIN OF THE

to the actions and effects of the stars and celestial bodies, or rather of the intelligences that assist them, through appropriate and suitable materials: with words, characters, fumigations, and prayers, as if one were impressing the figure of a seal or signet into wax or other similar material. All this is accompanied by what the Hebrews call כונה <term>Cauanah</term> <note>Hebrew: *Kavanah*, meaning "intention" or "concentration." In Jewish mysticism, it refers to the focused mental state required for prayer or ritual to be effective.</note>, a strong and elevated intention, without which nothing can be properly done; for, approaching close to ecstasy or the ravishing of the spirit, it holds the same place in these admirable operations as the soul does in our body, which it vivifies. Furthermore, there are no occult faculties or virtues—some sown in the heavens, others on earth, like the mold of the matter one wishes to cast, or like our internal conceptions regarding the words or letters that express them—that the mage cannot unite together and bring into action.

Nonetheless, whatever miraculous work one might produce, whether by way of magic or the Kabbalah, or in any other manner, the principal effect must be referred entirely to the will and power of God. For just as man naturally produces his like, which is his work, just as the making of the world is that of the Sovereign Creator, so the mage creates his own through artifice. But as natural things are more perfect than those of art—which does nothing but imitate nature, according to Aristotle in the 2nd book of the *Physics*—so too are divine works to be more esteemed and more accomplished beyond comparison than those of nature. This was even witnessed by Pharaoh’s enchanters in the 8th chapter of Exodus: when Aaron stretched out his rod and brought forth gnats from the dust, they, being unable to do the same through their charms, were constrained to admit, <note>Latin: *digitus Dei hic est*</note> **"this is the finger of God."** 

Thus, all the words, all the sacred names, characters, figures, sigils, and formal numbers—which have more power than any material quality—along with their perfumes, lights, and other such external things that support them, have no virtue or efficacy in magic or Kabbalah, except insofar as they conform to the voice and the hand of the Sovereign God—that is to say, to the word and the scripture. This is why strange words that signify nothing to us—which nevertheless Zoroaster and Orpheus forbid us to alter or change for others, especially the Hebrew ones, which are the primitive source of all others—can do more than meaningful and intelligible words. For although there are many words that seem to us made for pleasure or by chance, signifying nothing in any language whatsoever, they might nevertheless be just like a writing in cipher; while those who do not understand the secret can draw no sense from them, others who know the artifice know very well how to discern what they mean. The same could be true of characters and words which, being unknown to us, do not cease to have some significance to the spirits to whom they are addressed.

This has been treated by us incidentally regarding magic, because it is the science of the celestial world, which comprises within itself the ten heavens or Spheres, which are the instruments and means through which divinity acts upon us: namely, nine mobile ones, and the tenth, firm and stable, called by some the Empyrean heaven, and in scripture the heaven of heaven, in <note>Latin: *Domini Dei tui cælū est, & cælum cæli*</note> "The heaven is the Lord your God's, and the heaven of heaven" (Deuteronomy 10), and in the plural again "the heavens of heavens," which is not without mystery in 1 Kings 8: <note>Latin: *Si enim cœlum, & cœli cœlorum*</note> "If indeed the heaven, and the heaven of heavens..."

# LANGUAGES OF THIS UNIVERSE.

<note>original: "Cœlum & cœli cœlorum te capere non possunt," a reference to 1 Kings 8:27</note>...the heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain thee; and by reason of its firm stability, it is called the land of the living. *When I shall set glory in the land of the living* <note>original: "Cùm dedero gloriam in terra viventium," Ezekiel 26:20</note>, in which is planted the tree of life and the throne of God, seated and placed upon that sea of glass resembling crystal mentioned in Revelation 4 and 15. And if one wished to report here the rare and marvelous things of this magic, it would never be finished. Whoever wishes to see the particulars should read the ancients: Caspar Peucer in his books on the *Principal Kinds of Divinations*; Giambattista della Porta in his books on *Natural and Supernatural Magic*; Jean Wier <note>written here as "J. Vivier"</note> in his books on the *Illusions of Demons*; Gerolamo Cardano in his books on the *Subtlety and Variety of Things*; Jean Bodin in his book on *Sorcerers* and his *Theater of Nature*; and Benedictus Pererius in his books on *Magic*.

To return to the aforementioned enumerations and measures of the ten <term>Sephiroth</term> <note>The ten divine emanations in the Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself.</note>: since ten is the end of all numbers, and consequently the measure of all measures, one appropriates to them the ten categories or <term>predicaments</term> of <term>Dialectic</term> <note>Dialectic refers to the art of logical argument; "predicaments" are Aristotle’s ten categories of being.</note>, which encompass all the circumstances of things: namely, essence or substance, quality, quantity, relation, "when" (which denotes time), "where" (place), situation or position, habit, the agent, and the patient. Then there are five <term>predicables</term> <note>Classifications of the relationship between a subject and a predicate: genus, species, difference, property, and accident.</note>: genus, species, difference, property, and accident. These two together make fifteen, which is the same value denoted by the two letters of this name יה <term>Iah</term> <note>A shortened form of the Hebrew name for God, Yahweh.</note>, in which the *I* (י), which is worth ten, represents the ten predicaments; and the *He* (ה), worth five, represents the five predicables, because all things were made by the power of this holy name.

Furthermore, to these aforementioned ten Sephiroth and the ten celestial spheres correspond the Ten Commandments of the Law, according to Abraham Ibn Ezra in his commentary upon them. The first, which shows the most simple unity of the FATHER, who is like the base and foundation of the whole—*I am the Lord thy God, who brought thee out of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. Thou shalt have no other God but me*—relates to the tenth immobile sphere, as it supports the throne of God: *Heaven is my throne, and earth is my footstool* <note>original: "Cœlum sedes mea est, & terra scabellum pedum meorum," Isaiah 66:1</note>. From there, He moves the <term>Primum Mobile</term> <note>The "First Moved" sphere in the Ptolemaic system, which imparts motion to all other spheres.</note> and consequently all the rest. *All rejoice in the Father who moves them*, says Saint Dionysius in his *Celestial Hierarchy*, speaking of the intelligences <note>Angelic beings associated with the movement of the planets.</note> which, being moved, move the spheres and the celestial bodies over which they preside. Thus, Hermes defines God as being a circle whose center is everywhere and circumference nowhere, which is quite clearly represented by these two symbols of the number 10. The first, which is worth one, is like an indivisible point or the center which is everywhere; for there is no number where unity cannot be found, since they all depart from it and are nothing other than a heap of units strung together. The *o* or zero, which is round in the shape of a circumference, is said to be as if it were in no place, because by itself it does nothing; whereby it relates to the <term>En Soph</term> <note>Hebrew: *Ein Sof*, meaning "The Infinite," the primordial state of God before any emanation.</note>, the un-finished or infinite.

The second commandment—*Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of anything that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water, to adore them*—corresponds to the ninth sphere and the Primum Mobile, which moves and carries with it all the others beneath it in twenty-four hours; and to the SON, who is the first movement of all things, proceeding from the immobile Father. On this subject, Boethius says:

# HISTORY OF THE ORIGIN OF THE

*as the king's purple joined to the conduits:* <note>original Latin: "ut purpura regis iuncta canalibus"</note> that is to say, these influxions from above proceeding from the living source of divine existence, whose root—which is <term>EHIEH</term> <note>Hebrew for "I Am," the name revealed to Moses at the burning bush.</note>—is attached to the intelligible world, the true land of the living: *He will pluck up your root out of the land of the living* <note>original Latin: "Radicem tuam euellet de terra viuentium," Psalm 52:5.</note> and the trunk is the most sacrosanct and ineffable <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH (יהוה).</note> יהוה, the origin of all things, with its principal branches, which are the aforementioned divine names. These, like branches that still push forth shoots, scions, and suckers to serve as grafts, produce several surnames and sub-surnames; in such a way that the entire Law comes to be like a graft upon the single Tetragrammaton, <term>Jehovah</term>, in the same manner that a complete clause of a Scripture consists of words, words of syllables, syllables of letters, and all letters of the <term>Yod</term> <note>The smallest letter of the Hebrew alphabet (י), which begins the name YHWH.</note>, which is the beginning of the ineffable name to which it is also equivalent. For it is also used to represent the entire word, held anciently in such respect and honor by the Israelites that there was only the High Priest alone who wore it engraved on a plate of gold called by the Hebrews ציץ זהב <term>Tzitz Zahab</term>, on the front of his mitre. To him alone it was permitted to express it by its characters, and even then only once in the year, on the tenth day of the Moon of the month of <term>Tishrei</term> (which corresponds to our September), called *Iom Hachepurim*, the <term>Day of Atonement</term>, on which was celebrated the great propitiation and general absolution of all the Jewish people. He would utter it in the depths of the Sanctuary by himself, through a secret tradition of the <term>Kabbalah</term> <note>The Jewish mystical and oral tradition.</note> revealed by God to Moses, and from him to Aaron, in a manner quite different from how the sequence and arrangement of its characters sounds. And as Rabbi Joseph <note>Referring to Rabbi Joseph Gikatilla (1248–c. 1305), a famous Kabbalist.</note> testifies in his *Gates of Light* <note>original French: "Portes de la lumiere," referring to the work "Sha'are Orah."</note>, the ancient Jews considered it an infallible article of faith that whoever uttered it by its own letters, without a very urgent necessity, would have no part in the world to come. This is because it is communicable only to the Creator alone, and there is nothing in it that is common between God and His creatures, as there is in names like צדיק <term>Tzadik</term> (Just), דיין <term>Dayan</term> (Judge), חנון <term>Hannun</term> (Gracious, Pitiful), and other similar ones. This is because it represents the being of God, incomprehensible to all of them, and His substance, with its intrinsic properties and His "quiddity" <note>A philosophical term meaning "essence" or "what-ness."</note>, through a manifest and most perfect demonstration, without any equivocation, mixture, or any outward regard or relation. All other names are derived from divine operations except this one, which for this reason is called the Great Name: *What will you do for your great name?* <note>original Latin: "Quid facies magno nomini tuo?" Joshua 7:9.</note> It does not signify through effects, but through a pure existence, for which it is most redoubtable and fearsome, according to the 98th Psalm: *Let them praise your great name, for it is awesome and holy;* <note>original Latin: "Confiteantur nomini tuo magno, quoniam terribile & sanctū est," Psalm 99:3 in modern numbering.</note> and in the second [Epistle] to Timothy, chapter 2: *Let everyone who calls on the name of the Lord depart from iniquity.* <note>original Latin: "Discedat ab iniquitate omnis qui inuocat nomen Domini."</note> Also, it existed, but it was not read according to the order and sequence of its characters; for it is specifically prohibited in Exodus 20 to take the name of God in vain, which the Rabbis interpret as uttering it from the lips rashly and without occasion. Even the Gentiles, conforming in this to Hebrew traditions, acknowledge that one must not importune the divinity out of season, nor abuse His grace and goodness rashly and at all hours. This is why the Church has prefixed certain days and hours for prayers, more particularly at one time than at another, according to Psalm 55.

This number is held in such high regard by the <term>Cabalistes</term> <note>Kabbalists: Practitioners of Jewish mysticism who believe every letter and number in the Torah holds hidden divine power.</note> that they imagine they can, by its foundation, come to know the number of the stars—just as Hipparchus once attempted with the help of his instruments. However, this is not so according to the 147th Psalmist, who "counts the multitude of stars and calls them all by their names." <note>original Latin: *qui numerat multitudinem stellarum, & omnibus eis nomina vocat.*</note> This is achieved through the repeated multiplications of the 22 letters, which finally arrive at an incomprehensible and ineffable number, incomparably larger than the one mentioned previously; this one reaches 3,403,424,372,953,868,586,410,367,991,040. If one wished to add all 21 multiplications together, each on its own, what would that produce? But they begin only at the letter *Beth*, since *Aleph*, which represents unity, can produce nothing when multiplied by itself and in itself. Thus, 22 times 22 makes 484; 22 times 484 for the letter *Ghimel* makes 10,648; and so on for the rest. This curiosity of numbering is, in truth, entirely frivolous and uncertain, for what foundation can there be in it? It is merely a cover, with very little or no appearance of probability—much like the way the <term>Thalmudistes</term> <note>Talmudists: Scholars of the Talmud, the body of Jewish civil and ceremonial law.</note> strive to count the angels by another path. Yet, beneath this, they include certain secrets for which all this serves as a cipher; following this example, Daniel in Chapter 7 counts the angels by the thousands, as do Ezekiel in his final chapter and the Apocalypse in Chapter 7 for most divine things. 

The Talmudists therefore distinguish the troops and exercises of the angels into six orders, namely <term>Mazalot</term>, <term>El</term>, <term>Ligion</term>, <term>Rihatton</term>, <term>Chirton</term>, and <term>Gistera</term>. The <term>Mazalot</term> are thereafter divided by them into 12 regiments, according to the 12 signs of the Zodiac, each of which contains thirty "banners" called <term>El</term> (matching the number of degrees in each sign), and by this means they arrive at 360. Each <term>El</term> further contains as many <term>Ligion</term>, reaching by this means 108,000. Each <term>Ligion</term> contains 30 <term>Rihatton</term>, making 324,000. Each <term>Rihatton</term> contains 30 <term>Chirton</term>, making 9,720,000. And each <term>Chirton</term> finally being multiplied by 30 <term>Gistera</term>, they arrive at 291,600,000. The grand total is 301,655,160—which does not come close to the aforementioned multiplication of the <term>Ziruphs</term> <note>Ziruph (Tziruf): A Kabbalistic method of permuting and combining Hebrew letters to reveal hidden meanings or create divine names.</note>. But to return to this Kabbalistic rule of...

### HISTORY OF THE ORIGIN OF

**Zairagia** <note>The *Za'iraja* was a complex medieval Arabic device used to "calculate" answers to philosophical or divinatory questions using letter permutations, often involving concentric circles.</note>: we have here adapted its practice to another method. Specifically, we have moved away from the single spherical figure they use—consisting of four or five circles enveloped one within another—into several separate tables to make the whole system more intelligible. Instead of using it for idle divinations, we have redirected its use toward <term>Gematria</term> <note>A Kabbalistic method of interpreting biblical names and phrases by the numerical value of their letters.</note>, which focuses only on the true deciphering of the secret mysteries of scripture and prophetic predictions. 

From this depends true rational **Arithmancy** and formal **Geomancy** <note>original: *Germantie*. While similar to "Geomancy," the author uses it here to describe a science of "measures and forms" that corresponds to the physical world, just as Arithmancy (numbers) corresponds to the intellectual world.</note>. The former symbolizes the intelligible world because numbers are subtle, essential, and further removed from matter than measures; they act as the reasons, relations, and regards to which the types of the sensible world are referred. This is roughly what Aristotle implies in the text previously cited from the 12th book of the *Metaphysics*: *Species are like numbers* <note>original Latin: *Species se habent sicut numeri*.</note>. 

And **Geomancy**, being established upon measures—as forms introduced into matter—corresponds to the sensible world that participates in matter. This world is more refined and formed in the heavens, and more coarse and material on the earth. All of this follows the example of the <term>Sephirot</term> <note>The ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself and creates the universe.</note>: the numbers correspond to the three superior ones, and the measures to the seven inferior ones. 

To these two dependencies of Gematria—Arithmancy and the intelligible world—belong the internal conceptions of our thoughts. To Geomancy belongs the writing that expresses them. For from the plurality of points which consist of numbers—not including that fortuitous projection of points scattered by chance, for that is pure nonsense without foundation from which nothing solid can be drawn <note>A critique of traditional geomancy, which involved making random dots in the sand.</note>—are produced lines, both straight and curved. From these lines, letters are later formed. From letters coupled into syllables and words, a sense is procreated, which manifests and casts outward everything that the understanding can apprehend within. 

This sense is analogous to the spirit that gives life to the parts of a body, which are designated by these letters. In the same way, the body is represented by the word woven from them, naturally representing the inherent property of each thing it signifies—at least in the **Hebrew** language. It is held that **Adam** imposed the true and meaningful names upon all those things that were created. 

And just as in the corruption of an individual, when the form that used to be there fades away, another succeeds it and is introduced in its place; so it is in a context of writing: if the letters are transposed and cast out of their previous order, placement, and disposition, the meaning that was there before alters and changes. Indeed, there are few ways you could turn or assemble the Hebrew characters without some meaning always being found. 

Since letters consist of numbers and measures (which Gematria encompasses), and since words are formed from them—carrying the true essence and <term>quiddity</term> <note>The "whatness" or essential nature of a thing.</note> of the thing they represent—and since this entire Universe is governed by an intellect spread and mixed into all its smallest parts, to which both the past and the future are present: in this rule of Zairagia, one takes the letters of the proposed question as a foundation. For once the letters—through the aid of said numbers and proportions—come to rise out of their primary sense (as if from their earthly matter) into a celestial form, the Soul of the Universe, which is entirely intellectual, attracts them to itself much more easily than if they remained in their sensory thickness. In the same way, spirits elevate the body; the Soul elevates the spirits; and the Intellect or the <term>Neshama</term> <note>The highest level of the soul in Kabbalistic thought, representing pure divine intellect.</note> finally draws the Soul to itself. This is another **Jacob's ladder**, and the **chain of Homer** <note>A classical metaphor for the hierarchical connection between the heavens and the earth.</note>, in imitation of what the Savior said of himself in Saint John 12: *And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all things unto myself.* <note>original Latin: "Ego si exaltatus fuero a terra, omnia traham ad me ipsum."</note>

    It is not, therefore, our intention to teach here anything regarding divination, whether lawful or unlawful, by way of <term>Gematria</term> <note>The practice of interpreting the hidden meaning of words through the numerical value of their letters.</note>; but rather, through this Kabbalistic example, to make it easier to understand the nature of Gematria, which is the source of all the arts of ciphers. In this practice, they proceed in this manner: First of all, they trace a Circle, which they divide into four by two diameters intersecting at right angles, where they mark the first four numerical progressions: 1, 2, 3, 4, as those which govern everything by making 10 when added together. Consequently, they mark the Geometric figures that correspond to them: the point, the line, the surface or triangle, and the Square which represents the Cube and the solid body, having all three dimensions of length, width, and depth. Below that are placed the three Mother letters, *Aleph, Mem, and Shin*, which denote the three Elements: Earth, Water, and Fire. For the Hebrews admit no more than these, rejecting air from this count, as it serves only as a kind of glue or binder for these elements; and by the same means, it fills the vacuum that nature so abhors. In place of this vacuum, they establish here a small circle, taking the place of the zero in ciphers, 0, which serves in calculation for pauses and the distinction of tens. 

    They then add the four seasons of the year and the four parts of the world, with the four winds that come from them: *I will bring the four winds from the four quarters of heaven* <note>original Latin: "Inducam quatuor ventos a quatuor plagis Cæli"</note>, Jeremiah 49. And the four Angels who preside over them in the seventh chapter of Revelation. For the winds, though they are natural impressions of the air in the elementary realm, are nevertheless referred to the rank of spirits in occult philosophy, as can be seen hereafter in extracts from certain Rabbis, conforming to several passages of Scripture, and even in Psalm 148: *Stormy winds that fulfill his word* <note>original Latin: "Spiritus procellarum quæ faciunt verbum eius"</note>. This is why they are sometimes driven away by adjurations and by the sound of bells, which are blessed and exorcised; but more precisely in the 37th chapter of Ezekiel, speaking of the resurrection of our bones:

    *Come from the four winds, O spirit, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live* <note>original Latin: "A quatuor ventis veni spiritus, & insuffla super interfectos istos, & reuiuiscant"</note>; and in Daniel 7: *And behold, the four winds of heaven strove upon the great sea* <note>original Latin: "Et ecce quatuor venti Cæli pugnabant in mari magno"</note>, which the <gloss>commentary</gloss> explains as the four intelligences that preside over the four corners of the world, and this in the great sea of the intelligible, where consist the living, permanent sources of all that is derived here below through the channels of the <term>Sephirot</term> <note>The ten emanations or attributes in Kabbalah through which the Infinite is revealed.</note>, and to which they finally return, just like the springs and rivers that proceed from the sea return back into it. And insofar as the THREE is a symbol of divinity and of the intelligible world, and within us of the *Neshamah* <note>Hebrew: "breath," referring to the highest level of the soul or the Intellect</note>, or Intellect which corresponds to it; and the FOUR represents the Elementary [realm] and the body: and since every middle part participates in both of its two extremes—upon which must be noted what the Apostle in the first [letter] to the Corinthians, chapter 15, calls the mediator composed of divinity and humanity, the "Celestial Man"—they add the Three to the aforementioned Quaternary to make Seven. This number represents heaven because of the equal number of planets which are its primary instruments, and upon which depend nearly all the varieties and alterations down here, both in the production of things and in the fortune of persons; at least according to [Hermes] Trismegistus in the first chapter of his *Pymander* <note>The *Poimandres*, a foundational text of Hermetic philosophy</note>: He consequently fashioned seven governors, who by their revolutions and Spheres envelop the sensible world; the arrangement of which is called fatal destiny, and they form a circle that encloses the other. This they divide into seven spaces, which serve both for the Planets and for the Angels, Intelligences, and Spirits who preside there, otherwise assisting perpetually before the throne face-to-face with the great God, in Revelation 1, and more expressly in chapter 4. There were seven burning lamps before the throne, which are the Spirits of God: which in the following chapter 5 he says are the eyes of the Messiah in the midst of the twenty-four elders. A lamb was there as if it had been put to death, and it had seven horns and as many eyes, which are the seven spirits of God sent into all the earth; for to them is committed the entire dispensation and rule of the celestial court and of this lower world beneath the Sphere of the Moon. These are they who, with their leader as the seventh, designated by the candlestick of the tabernacle, stand continually before the *Mercava* <note>The *Merkabah*, or the Divine Chariot/Throne of God in Jewish mysticism</note>, or Throne of God, like certain secretaries of commands whose execution they entrust to six other subaltern Angels, each furnished with six wings. The names of the six aforementioned major Angels are drawn from the six reversals or Anagrams of these three letters of the great name יהוה <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God. The author mentions "three letters" because the name YHWH uses three distinct Hebrew letters: Yod, He, and Vav</note>, which will be more fully specified hereafter, according to the six constitutions of the World: the high and the low; the front and the back; the right and the left. These seven Angels or intelligences, to which <gloss>to which</gloss> the seven planets are subject through alternating vicissitudes of hours in days, days in weeks, and weeks in 354 annual revolutions with four months, preside successively each in its turn, administering and governing everything that is projected up there in Heaven to be executed on the earth. And of these Angels, the closest to us, and who should be—if not for our own failings—the most familiar to us, is Gabriel. To him belongs the interpretation, among other things, of Dreams, as the one who presides over the Moon, our closest neighbor of all the Stars and celestial bodies. And since she rules the night, just as the Sun does the day, the charge of Dreams—which occur more commonly during that time destined for sleep than during the day—must be referred to her and, consequently, to the intelligence that assists her. In this book, the praises of the Sovereign are incessantly sung by all sorts of Creatures; but it is a Cipher whose Alphabet consists in their harmony, agreement, and the proportion they bear to one another.

These two numbers, three and four, which when added together make 7, if you multiply them by each other, will produce 12—exactly as many as there are signs in the Zodiac. By this, one sees the great affinity the planets have with them. It is the same from 7 to 12 as it is from 6 to 8. For 2 and 4 make 6, and 2 times 4 gives 8. These signs serve as houses <term>domiciles: In astrology, the specific zodiac sign where a planet is said to be "at home" and most powerful</term> for the planets, in the manner of the 64 black and white squares on the back of a game board <note>The author compares the arrangement of the cosmos to the strategic layout of a chessboard</note>, for the different positions of the pieces in a game of chess, and their various arrangements and aspects toward one another. There is nothing more suitable than this to represent the movements of the celestial bodies. The same is true for the multiple combinations of letters, both in general in all kinds of writing, and particularly in square ciphers <note>Likely referring to "magic squares" or cryptographic tables used in mystical traditions</note>, which have several meanings beneath the same character. For the aspects and habits of the planets in the signs, when joined with the four elements from which all bodies are produced, symbolize the characters of writing that constitute words. 

Furthermore, these 12 signs, which Plato calls the "gates of Heaven"—of which Capricorn is called the *Ascendant* <note>The rising point</note> because the Sun begins to climb again within it, and the Crab <note>The sign of Cancer; original: *l'escreuice*</note> the *descendant* because, having arrived there, it declines once more—denote the 12 gates of the Holy Celestial City described in Revelation 21. To these are assigned as many Angels who assist there, divided three by three as guards for each of the four regions of the Heaven: East, West, South, and North, in the exact same way that astrologers distribute them. To each of these signs is assigned one letter from the "twelve simples" <note>In the *Sefer Yetzirah*, a foundational text of Jewish mysticism, the Hebrew alphabet is divided into 3 "mothers," 7 "doubles," and 12 "simples," the latter corresponding to the zodiac signs</note>, so called because they are always pronounced in the same way, just as the signs, for their part, always remain in the same property and virtue. 

All this can be seen in the following table, where the meaning of the said letters is set down alongside the 12 months, which correspond to the 12 signs. And this is the *Third Circle*: by which it is demonstrated to us that Heaven—to which this number of 12 is most fitting—is a passage and intermediary between divine things (designated by the number three) and earthly things (represented by the number four, as those which consist of the four elements). Thus our Savior, who participates in both of these two natures <note>The divine and the human</note>, held this number of twelve in high regard, as one can see in many places in the Gospel. It is seen again in Revelation concerning the aforementioned Holy City, all divided by 12, just as Plato organized his worldly city in the 5th and 6th books of his *Laws*. They are so in agreement with one another that it would not be possible to be more so; from this, one clearly sees the great sympathy and connection that exists between superior things and inferior things.

Consequently, by multiplying the number 7 by 4—which is much like marrying heaven with earth, upon which all the operations and effects of <term>natural magic</term><note>A branch of Renaissance science that sought to understand and utilize the hidden, occult powers within nature (such as magnetism or herbal properties) without resorting to the supernatural or demonic.</note> depend—one produces the 28 <term>mansions of the moon</term><note>The 28 divisions of the sky the moon passes through during its monthly cycle, often used in astrology to determine favorable times for specific actions.</note> within the 12 signs of the Zodiac, which the moon traverses in 28 days. For meanwhile, as the Sun moves away by one degree, the moon reaches it on the 29th day. From this, the fourth Circle is formed: applying to it the <term>intelligences</term><note>Celestial spirits or governing angels believed to guide the movements of the spheres.</note> that preside over it, along with the corresponding Hebrew letters and the significance of the said mansions.

In this way, when this figure of the <term>Zairagia</term><note>An adaptation of the *Zairja*, a complex medieval Arabic divinatory instrument that used concentric, rotating circles to answer questions through letter and number symbolism.</note> is completed, it consists of four circles to represent the four Elements—the principles of all things both above and below—following the <term>Emerald Tablet of Hermes</term><note>A foundational text of Western esotericism attributed to the mythical Hermes Trismegistus, providing the philosophical basis for alchemy and magic.</note>: <note>original: "Quod est superius est sicut quod est inferius, & è conuerso, ad perpetranda miracula rei vnius."</note> "That which is above is like that which is below, and vice versa, to accomplish the miracles of the one thing." And the Kabbalists say to this same purpose: <note>original: "Domus sanctuarij quæ est inferius, disponitur iuxta domum sanctuarij quæ est superius."</note> "The house of the sanctuary which is below is arranged according to the house of the sanctuary which is above."

Of these four Circles, which imitate the four Elements, there is one that remains firm and immobile, just as the Earth does, which serves as the base and foundation of the Universe that rotates all around it: <note>original: "Fundauit Terrā super stabilitatem suam, non inclinabitur in seculum seculi."</note> "He set the earth on its foundations; it can never be moved," from Psalm 104. And the other three circles move following the example of the three noble elements—Water, Air, and Fire—to facilitate the intersections of what one seeks, just as the Planets do.

All this is premised, upon which depends the principal tradition of the marvelous operations of <term>occult Philosophy</term><note>A Renaissance tradition that sought to understand the hidden laws of nature through a blend of magic, alchemy, and Kabbalah.</note>, which is nothing other than a proper attraction and association of celestial virtues acting upon the passive matter of the elements, susceptible to all forms by means of the <term>common spirit</term><note>Also known as the *Anima Mundi* or World Soul, believed to be the vital force connecting the heavens to the earth.</note> spread throughout the universe.

> *From this comes the race of men and of beasts, and the lives of birds,*
> *And the monsters that the Sea bears beneath its marble-like surface.*
> <note>original: "Vnde hominum pecudúmque genus, vitæque volantum / Et quæ marmoreo fert monstro sub æquore Pontus." From Virgil’s *Aeneid*, Book VI.</note>

As for the use and practice of the aforementioned rule of the <term>Zairagia</term><note>The *Zairaja*, a complex medieval Arabic device used to generate answers to questions through numerical and literal permutations.</note>, we will omit it here, as it is not our purpose nor intention; we will satisfy ourselves by saying that everything proceeds by way of commutations and various literal transpositions of the <term>Ziruphs</term><note>From the Hebrew *Tziruf*, a Kabbalistic method of permuting and combining letters to find hidden meanings or mystical names.</note>, along with the correspondences and proportions of formal numbers, from which a new meaning comes to be procreated, no more nor less than by <term>Anagrams</term><note>Rearranging the letters of a word or phrase to form a new one.</note> of reversed words: a truly admirable thing, which manifests to us more and more the infallible divine providence, even in the smallest things. *Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing? and one of them shall not fall on the ground without your Father. But the very hairs of your head are all numbered,* <note>original: "Nonne duo passeres asse væneunt, & vnus ex illis non cadet super terram sine patre vestro? Vestri autem & capilli capitis omnes numerati sunt."</note> Saint Matthew 10. In the order once established by Providence for the course of human affairs, there is nothing fortuitous or by chance in His sight; everything is most wisely governed by Him, by an incomprehensible reason through His administering spirits. Because we have briefly mentioned the winds above, regarding their number: *And he rode upon a Cherub, and did fly: yea, he did fly upon the wings of the wind,* <note>original: "Et ascendit super Cherubim, & volauit super pennas ventorum."</note> Psalm 18. And since this seems to have some affinity with that transmission of thought in the <term>Steganography</term><note>Refers to the *Steganographia*, a book by Johannes Trithemius that disguised a system of magic and spirit communication as a treatise on cryptography.</note> of the Abbot Trithemius and of Agrippa, I will add straight away what is found of a very rare fragment, which some attribute to <term>Rabbi Simeon son of Jochai</term><note>Simeon bar Yochai, a 2nd-century tannaic sage to whom the *Zohar* is traditionally attributed.</note>, author of the <term>Zohar</term><note>The foundational work of Jewish mysticism.</note>; after having inserted here the table of the significance of the Hebrew letters, which also concerns the aforementioned topic.

Solomon says, just as the fire up above is distinct from the four Elements found here below, it is also much purer than they are; and yet, I wish to say something here regarding these <term>living creatures</term><note>original: "animaux". In this context, it refers to the "Holy Living Creatures" or celestial beings seen in the visions of prophets like Ezekiel.</note>. For there are four inferior Elements, each of which has its own inhabitants in its respective place; and above these are the heavens, which also have their own inhabitants, pure and clean, without any trace of corruption. But this fire which is on high is not made of wax, wood, oil, or grease, nor any other such compositions; rather, it is very simple. And the things that live within it are pure Angels—clear and shining, similar to the rays of the Sun, or flames of fire, or sparks, or lucid stars the color of quicksilver or fine gold. # LANGUAGES OF THIS UNIVERSE.

...as blue as the celestial azure of the firmament, from which, in clear weather unhindered by clouds, it is transmitted to our sight through the truth of the other Spheres. These are spirits that represent the prayers of creatures before the **Merkabah** <note>original: "Mercaua"; the Divine Chariot or Throne of God in Jewish mysticism</note> or throne of God; > *“When you prayed with tears, and buried the dead, etc. I offered your prayer to the Lord,”* <note>original: "Quando orabas cum lacrymis, ac sepeliebas mortuos, &c. Ego obtuli orationem tuam Domino"</note> says the Angel **Raphael** to **Tobit** <note>original: "Tobie"</note> in chapter 12. The **Kabbalists** <note>original: "Cabalistes"</note> call the chief and principal among them all **Sandalphon**, and they carry divine oracles and revelations down here to the **Prophets**: and by the same means, [they carry] the thoughts and secret intentions of people imperceptibly, as if by inspiration from one place to another, at whatever great distance it may be, in less than the blink of an eye.

The second animal <note>The author uses "animal" in the sense of a living, ensouled being, from the Latin *anima* (soul)</note> or spirit is darker than the preceding ones, and is compared to the **wind**: its figure, moreover, being whatever it wishes to take according to one of the four **Elements** with which it associates, and it forms itself in this manner: either as Water, or as a cloud, or as a flowing liquid, or in the guise of thick and dark mists, and sometimes like a sound, or the voice of some elemental animal; taking a body in one of these Elements, according to how the matter is disposed to receive the nearest and most suitable species.

The third is the **soul**, of which the Sages say that it willingly accompanies the body, and joins itself to it by means of the spirit: wherefore its figure is often encountered at night in dark places, and is heard and seen: its color being similar to the weather at that time: having a human appearance moreover, and sometimes having the shape of the body from which it departed, such that some see them in cemeteries. Of this sort of animals, our Sages say that the soul which has left a body, and is capable of something, is not, nor ever was, anything but that of a man or a woman: and they call them spiritual and celestial; spiritual for their goodness, celestial because of their subtle simplicity.

The fourth animal is the **Wind**, which we hear well, but we do not see it for all that: just as, on the other hand, there are other things that we see and do not hear at all, such as the **harmony of the heavens**, of which it is spoken in chapter 38 of **Job**, > *“who shall make the harmony of Heaven to sleep,”* <note>original: "concentum Cœli quis dormire faciet"; a reference to Job 38:37</note> and several others, whose bodies are actually perceived by the eye, according to the part from which they have their temporal consistency. Now if the Wind is from the East to the South, it will be naturally hot: if from the West or the North, cold on the contrary. And we see it have a great force and power: for it carries clouds full of water, hail, storms, and tempests: troubles the calm of the sea, and moves great waves therein, breaks, uproots, and throws to the ground the largest trees in the forests, of which it makes a terrible and piteous slaughter. And this is called air as living as fire: but above it is called living and simple: and yet it has a double name, namely fixed and mobile: the mobile is that which moves to various places: and the fixed, that which stops in one of the four corners of the world, although it descends from above, from where those from whom it descended and was created, rush forth to come and bind it. This is a great and powerful worker in the sea, on the earth, and in the air, according to the temperature and disposition from which it comes.

The fifth animal is the **phantom** or the **vision**, that is to say, a shadow of several kinds of likenesses, composed diversely of one another: and this apparition is procreated in a desert place, or corrupted air, sometimes in the form of men-at-arms descending along a ridge, which is called the **ancient army** <note>original: "armee antique"; likely a reference to the folkloric "Wild Hunt" or ghostly processions of soldiers</note>; sometimes it appears...

appears over the waters, in the guise of some beautiful, well-dressed woman: or in the meadows, where it seems to some that it is a herd of cows: but this happens to them through the corruption of their habits, and the malice of their humors, for which they are called <term>demoniacles<note>A term for those believed to be possessed or afflicted by demonic influence, here explained as a medical condition caused by bodily "vapors."</note></term>, because the vicious vapors and fumes of the stomach rise to their eyes, which pervert their sight: so that they imagine seeing many things that do not exist.

The sixth animal is the **Demon**, which descends from the height of the heavens to the abyss, and was created from the first matter without corruption, whereby it never ends, but will persist forever, notwithstanding that it has received some thickness from the darkness enclosed within the depths of the earth. It is, moreover, somewhat complicated by matter, but of a very strong habit of body: and of these, the sages say that through their means, responses were obtained for a long time concerning many things of which people desired to know the truth. But they always dwell in darkness, without ever being separated from it: yet sometimes the Sovereign Creator permits them to take such a form on earth as they please: so that they even change themselves into **Angels of light**, with a very powerful brightness; beautiful and resplendent, almost the equal of the Sun, the Moon, and the clearest stars: or like a good Angel, a cloud, bird, fish, man, or beast: a snake, lizard, and similar crawling vermin, and any other such figure they wish: but all this is impalpable, in the manner of a spirit, or of wind. 

Know furthermore that each of them can, whenever they please, take a body in any one of the four **elements**, although their life depends on **fire**, and their dwelling consists in fire, along with all their actions and maintenance. The Sage says regarding these six kinds of animals that their invocation and appearance, consideration, binding, and deliverance, is sometimes good and lawful, sometimes evil and entirely reproachable, according to the various ends to which it is applied.

You then, who are a lover of **Wisdom** <note>original: "Sapience"</note>, and curious to know the works and wonders of the Creator, do not enter into scruples and doubt that there may be a difference or division between the body and the spirit regarding these six kinds of animals, for they are but one, being made and joined together inseparably forever. The conjunction, moreover, of the spirit and the soul, from which life proceeds, is called **Wind** even in **Job**, chapter 7:

->Remember that my life is wind;<-
<note>original: "Memento quod ventus est vita mea"</note>

So that the living Wind is what we call the spirit and the soul, and it is said to be living when this assembly is made without corruption: but when such a conjunction of these two occurs—namely of the soul and the spirit—whereby a corruptible body intervenes with them, then the spirit and the soul, which were one, are dissociable from the body. Several other beautiful and excellent discourses on this matter are treated after **Rabbi of Castile** <note>likely referring to Joseph Gikatilla, a 13th-century Spanish Kabbalist</note> in his works, **Rabbi Joseph** son of **Carnitol** in his books of the *Gates of Justice* and other ancient and modern Rabbis by **Paulus Riccius** in his Kabbalistic book called *Compendium of the Gates of Light*, and in his *Introductions to the Kabbalah*, and by **Johann Reuchlin** (also called **Capnio**) in book 3 of *The Kabbalistic Art*.

->LANGUAGES OF THIS UNIVERSE.<-
->On the Hebrew mystery of the words Urim & Thummim.<-

### CHAP. XXI.

The Hebrews were accustomed to utter the word **Adonai** <note>Hebrew for "Lord"</note>, one of the Hebrew names of God, wherever the four-lettered name **יהוה** (**Jehovah**) <note>The Tetragrammaton, the sacred four-letter name of God</note>, which is unutterable, was found. This was because it was not permitted for everyone to know how it should be pronounced, nor which vowels represented its characters, nor if some should be doubled or spoken simply. Thus, **Rabbi Avina**, in the book of sanctifications in the **Talmud**, commenting on these words from **Exodus 3**: *I am who I am, I was and I shall be; this is my name eternally, and my memorial from age to age* <note>original: "Ie suis qui suis, fus & seray, c'est mon nom eternellement, & ma remembrance au siecle des siecles"</note>, states that it should not be read as it is written, *Jehovah*, but rather *Adonai*, which signifies Lord. In the book of the **Sanhedrin**, **Rabbi Abba Saul** affirms that whoever pronounces it openly, according to how its letters sound, shall have no part in the world to come. Indeed, in **Leviticus 24**, it is said that an Israelite, for having blasphemed the name of God by expressing it quite distinctly as *Jehovah* and not *Adonai* according to the custom—which was most abominable to the Jews—was stoned. Therefore, this holy name, which very often in Scripture without any other more particular expression is called by a certain <term>antonomasia<note>A rhetorical figure where a title or epithet is used instead of a proper name.</note></term> **השם** (**HaShem**), "the Name" called unutterable, is so designated not so much for the impossibility of its utterance, but for the mysteries it carried regarding the pure essence and substance of God: Three in a most simple and absolute unity, and in a Trinity of persons—a thing entirely incomprehensible to the human spirit, except through faith and belief alone. By this unutterable means, it follows even what **Trismegistus** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, a legendary figure representing ancient wisdom.</note> testifies in the **Poimandres**: *That the name of God cannot be uttered by a human mouth*; and what the oracle of the **Delphic Apollo** also confesses: *That his name cannot be expressed by any speech or word.* For all the letters of this Holy Name, which are only three (as we have said, the letter *He* being doubled), are comprised within the substantive verb, *I am*. From them consist the three tenses: the past, the present, and the future, which denotes the immutable and permanent stability of the divine essence. Nevertheless, **Moses the Egyptian** <note>Moses Maimonides (1135–1204), the great Jewish philosopher and physician.</note>, regarding the place cited above, notes that the priests and the elders of the Hebrew Council gave a lesson on it to their children and their disciples only once a week, to show them both how it should be pronounced and its significance, as well as the deep secrets and mysteries that depended upon it. But after it had been suppressed in the sanctuary due to the depravity of the Israelites—for in the time of **Simeon the Just**, a little before the coming of our Lord **Jesus Christ** (he was the last of the Great Synagogue, and the one who blessed the people using this unutterable Tetragrammaton)—this blessing began to be performed using the name of twelve letters, and consequently by that of forty-two. Even then, these were not shared except with the gentle and humble of heart, of holy and reformed life, who were expressly forbidden from divulging them too haphazardly; rather, they were to keep them secret in their hearts, for fear of profaning them and bringing them to contempt on one hand, and on the other, to avoid inciting the people to idolatry, until finally this mystery...

The Tribes kept this order when camping; whereas in the blessing of Jacob, and in the twelve stones of the **Urim** and **Thummim** <note>Sacred objects used by the High Priest to determine God's will</note>, they were arranged in this fashion: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Zebulun, Issachar, Dan, Gad, Asher, Naphtali, Joseph, Benjamin. In the blessing of Moses, they follow yet another order; and likewise in the enumeration found in the **Apocalypse** <note>The Book of Revelation</note>. On each stone of the twelve aforementioned, there was furthermore engraved on the inside the Divine Name assigned to its Tribe, and on the outside the name of the said Tribe along with six letters; for if the name did not contain that many, others were added until the count reached the said six, so that the whole ensemble shared the number of **seventy-two**, as many as there were letters in the expository name, **Shemhammaphoras** <note>The "Explicit Name" of God, here referring to a 72-letter mystical name</note>, hidden within the fold of the lining of the ornament. In these letters, some say that the names of the Patriarchs **Abraham**, **Isaac**, and **Jacob** (otherwise called **Israel**) were mixed in, in order to complete the entire Hebrew Alphabet, as all the letters were not contained in the aforementioned twelve names of the Tribes. This was called in the Hebrew language **Urim** and **Thummim**, as if one were to say "the declaration of truth," or "illuminations and perfections"—namely, this extensive interpretation of the **Shemhammaphoras** of seventy-two letters. According to **Rabbi Solomon** <note>original: "Rabbi Solomon"; likely Rashi, the famous 11th-century commentator</note>, Moses, by the command of God, secretly inserted this into the lining of this plate, and taught by word of mouth the secret manner of proceeding with it—as **Nehemanides** <note>original: "Nehemanides"; likely Nachmanides, the 13th-century scholar and Kabbalist</note> writes, along with the other principal mysteries of the Law—to the wise and discreet elders of the Law. To this he adds that these **Urim** and **Thummim** were a work of God just like the tables of the **Decalogue** <note>The Ten Commandments</note>, the whole having been given together to the said Moses on Mount Sinai.

**Urim**, moreover, were the sacred names by the virtue of which latent letters came to be elucidated; and **Thummim** were those which rendered the said letters readable. For the spirit of the Priest appointed to inquire of the Lord, by means of these **Urim** and **Thummim**, would come to be enlightened by the **Madregah** <term>Madregah: Hebrew for "step" or "level"; here referring to a specific level of spiritual inspiration</term>, which is one of the degrees of the Holy Spirit—inferior to prophetic visions, but superior to that celestial voice which they call **Batkol**, or "daughter of the voice." The Hebrews hold that this voice announced the future, issuing from between the two Cherubim of the Mercy Seat, and that the place where this voice was heard was called **דביר** (**Debhir**) <note>The inner sanctuary or Holy of Holies</note>, as if one were to say "Oracle," or rather the "familiar discourse of God." This was in use during the time of the second temple; from the return from Babylon until our Lord Jesus Christ, the Priest could arrange the letters that appeared in sight into **Miztarphoth** <note>original: "Miztarphoth"; refers to *tzerufim*, or mystical combinations of letters</note>, or assemblages of words from which some meaning was drawn. For example, when David in the Second Book of Kings <note>Known in modern Bibles as 2 Samuel 2:1</note> consults God as to whether he should go up into one of the cities of **Judah**, they say that these three letters then appeared clearly: **עלו** (**Alu**) <note>original: "עלו"; "Go up"</note>, which means "Go up"—namely, the first letter **ע** (*Ayin*) from the name **Simeon**, the second **ל** (*Lamed*) from that of **Levi**, and the third **ו** (*Vav*) from **Judah**. Thus, this was nothing other than a divine Oracle used in great affairs, following what is written in the 27th chapter of Numbers: *He shall stand before Eleazar the priest, who shall inquire for him the judgment of Urim before the Lord.* <note>original Latin: "Ante Eleazarum sacerdotem stabit, qui interroget pro eo iudicium Vrim coram Domino."</note>

treatise, *Massechtah Iomah* <note>Tractate Yoma, a section of the Talmud concerning the Day of Atonement</note>, the treatise of days, chapter 6. In the first place, it was not permitted for anyone except the King and the President of the Consistory <note>The Sanhedrin, the supreme judicial and religious council of ancient Israel</note> to interrogate or inquire of God by this way of the **Urim** and **Thummim**, and even then only in matters of great importance: such as undertaking a war, or if the Consistory—namely the Court that administered Justice—could not easily decide a cause or reach a settled opinion. In these cases, the King, or the Judge who was inquiring, turned his face toward the Priest he was questioning; and meanwhile, the Priest kept his gaze fixed straight toward the **Urim** and **Thummim**, with the **Shemhammaphoras** <note>The "Explicit Name" of God, a mystical 72-letter name</note> underneath, located in the aforementioned ornament on the chest of the Pontiff <note>The High Priest</note>. Furthermore, the voice of the one who interrogated had to be soft and quiet, and not loud or haughty, but only enough to be slightly heard by the Priest in distinct words. One must not ask two things at once, but only one, unless by chance necessity pressed; for even if two were proposed, the response was nevertheless given only for one. Then, the letters from which the answer was to be formed, by the virtue of the great name **Jehovah**, would begin to brighten and stand out above the others. Thus, the Priest, having a good way to notice them, gathered in his mind what he saw represented there. But if he were incapable or unworthy, they would not illuminate or rise up in any way, and he would draw no response to his demand. Some have written that these **Urim** and **Thummim** were not simply the letters of the name **Shemhammaphoras**, nor any stones added to the twelve on the ornament, but rather those very stones which would shine almost like fire if the Divinity accepted the request; otherwise, they remained in their original state. Indeed, *Ur* signifies fire; and as for **Thummim**, which comes from <gloss>Thom <note>original: תם</note></gloss>, integrity or perfection, this denoted that these gemstones, as true and exquisite parallels in their kinds without any flaw or defect, together gave off a brilliant luster, mingled with various colors such as one sees in opals or in the rainbow, from which the Priest, inspired by an **Enthusiasm** <note>In the classical sense of divine possession or inspiration</note>, came to understand and conjecture what the Divinity presaged. But there was moreover the **Ephod**, which the Seventy-Two <note>The translators of the Septuagint, the Greek Old Testament</note> translated as <gloss>epomis <note>original: ἐπωμὶς, a shoulder-piece</note></gloss> and Aquila <note>A 2nd-century translator of the Hebrew Bible into Greek</note> as <gloss>epiblema <note>original: ἐπίβλημα, a covering or cloak</note></gloss>; we might call it a *Camail* <note>A short mantle covering the head and shoulders</note>, provided it had no hood, or a scapular that reached only to within half a foot of the belt. This **Ephod**, moreover, was woven of gold and three types of purple (Exodus 28 and 39), having on each shoulder-piece a large clasp and binding, wherein was encased a <gloss>Soham <note>original: שהם, the Shoham stone</note></gloss>, which some take for an emerald (Josephus, *Antiquities of the Jews*, Book 3, Chapter 12), others for a sardonyx, and those with more evidence, for an onyx. In each of these were engraved the names of the six Tribes—namely, the six eldest sons of Jacob on the right shoulder, and the other six younger sons on the left—from which Oracles were perceptibly taken, as it is written in 1 Kings 30 <note>1 Samuel 30 in modern bibles</note>. There, David, to know from God if he should pursue those of **Amalek**, had the Priest **Abiathar** apply the **Ephod**, by means of which **Ephod** he obtained a response to two things all at once. ...our Lord Jesus Christ. Others place it more than 400 years earlier, because five things were missing from the second temple that were commonly found in the first, as is contained in the treatise *Yoma, chapter 1* <note>Tractate Yoma is a section of the Talmud focusing on the Day of Atonement</note>. In the commentaries of *R. Kimchi* <note>David Kimchi, a medieval biblical commentator and grammarian</note> on *Psalm 84* and *Haggai*, these are identified as: the Ark of the Covenant, with the mercy seat and the **Cherubim**; the fire that burned continually upon the bronze altar, where sacrifices were burned in the open air without ever being extinguished by rain, snow, wind, or other atmospheric conditions. This fire, having been sent from heaven upon a burnt offering in the time of *Moses and Aaron* (*Leviticus 9*), maintained itself without dying out until the building of the first temple by *Solomon*. At that time, it was renewed again from heaven and lasted until the time of *King Manasseh* and the *Babylonian Captivity*. The Priests then hid it in the depths of a well, and upon the return [from exile], their successors, thinking to draw it out, found in its place a thick liquid. When this was poured over the sacrifices, the fire ignited, as is contained in *2 Maccabees, chapter 1*. The third thing missing was the presence of God, called in *Exodus chapter 40* <term>Shekhinah <note>original: שכינה; the Divine Presence inhabiting the sanctuary</note></term>, which manifested around the Ark; then <term>Nebuah <note>original: נבואה; Prophecy</note></term>, and finally the Oracle of the <term>Urim and Thummim <note>The sacred lot or oracular devices used by the High Priest to determine God's will</note></term>. Furthermore, within the Ark were kept the tables of the *Ten Commandments*, the rod of *Aaron* still adorned with its leaves, flowers, and almonds, the vessel filled with *Manna*, the flask of Holy Anointing Oil used to anoint the Kings and Prophets of *Israel*, and the coffer of the offering from the *Philistines* (*1 Samuel chapter 6* <note>The original text cites "1 Kings," following an older naming convention for the books of Samuel</note>). Additionally, there were the fragments that remained of the first two Tables that *Moses* broke (*Exodus 32*), which were engraved all the way through so that they could be read from both sides, as *Rabbi Solomon* <note>Rashi, the preeminent medieval French rabbi and commentator</note> confirms. However, they were read differently, and their ancient traditions speak of them thus: *Mem setumah ve-Samekh she-be-luhot be-nes hayu omedim* <note>original French transcription: "Mem, Setumah, Veſamech, Beluchth Beniaſaion hauu"; This Hebrew phrase means: "The closed Mem and the Samekh in the tablets stood there by a miracle."</note>. This suggests that the closed or final *Mem* ם and the *Samekh* ס were a source of great wonder because they were closed all the way around. Consequently, it was necessary for the centers of these letters to be suspended in the air without being attached to anything. This manner of the Oracle of the **Urim and Thummim**, where it was necessary to rearrange the letters until some meaning was obtained, was not far removed from that of *Pythian Apollo* at *Delphi* and many other *Pagan* oracles, where the confusion of their tangled and muddled responses had to be arranged into distinct and declarative words.

Therefore, from all the arguments deduced above, we learn that the Hebrews hold that <term>Urim <note>original: אורים</note></term> signifies the truth and perfection of things. Based on subsequent passages of the *Bible*, some interpret this word as "Doctrine," or more properly, "Illustrations of Truth" and all kinds of perfections. *George the Venetian* <note>Francesco Giorgio, a Franciscan friar and Christian Kabbalist</note> does this in several places in his *Harmony of the World*, deriving the word from <term>or <note>original: אור; light</note></term>. *Sebastian Münster* and *Sante Pagnini* <note>Influential Christian Hebraists of the Renaissance</note> agree with this in their Hebrew Dictionaries regarding this word. This, along with the word <term>Thummim <note>original: התמים</note></term> mentioned in *Exodus 28*, *Leviticus 8*, and *Deuteronomy 33*—deriving from <term>Thom <note>original: תם; integrity or perfection</note></term>—are pure Hebrew words translated by the Seventy-Two Interpreters <note>The translators of the Septuagint, the Greek Old Testament</note> as "declaration of truth" or "illuminations and perfections." The *Chaldaic Paraphrast* <note>The author of the Targum, an Aramaic translation/paraphrase of the Bible</note> left them untranslated because the Hebrews were accustomed to hiding and concealing their secrets in meaningful words. Some of the Hebrews have called these words <term>Ruah ha-Kodesh <note>original: רוח הקודש; the Holy Spirit</note></term>,

Others date it more than 400 years earlier, because five things were lacking in the second temple which used to be in the first, as is contained in the treatise *Yoma* <note>original: "Ioma"; a tractate of the Talmud concerning the Day of Atonement</note>, chapter 1.
