### *Of the Cabal of the Tartars.*

IN the Court of the **Great Khan** <note>original: "grand Cham"; the title of the Mongol Emperor</note> of Tartary, there is an infinite number of men quite expert in the science of the stars, who know how to draw up horoscopes and nativities, just as our mathematicians do. These men are maintained at the expense of the King and Emperor; they are of all sorts of nations, such as Christians, **Nestorians** <note>An Eastern Christian sect that spread along the Silk Road</note>, Muslims, and Idolaters, all of whom receive their food, clothing, and upkeep from the King and Emperor. One should not think that these men have such exquisite knowledge, nor such reasons or demonstrations as our astronomers might have, although in the deceptive practice of judicial astrology <note>The branch of astrology used to predict human affairs and events</note>, they show enough proof of their skill. Instead, they only have an **astrolabe** <note>An ancient instrument used to solve problems relating to time and the position of the stars</note>, in which they see the course and disposition of the entire year, as surely or more so than a crowd of almanac-makers and prognosticators. These latter, without any knowledge of celestial science or practical judgment of past things, meddle with impunity in predicting what is to come, both regarding the seasons and the occurrences of the greatest affairs that might befall Princes. Be that as it may, these prognosticators of the Tartars, observing the course of the Moon, also see there how the air should be tempered throughout the year, following the order and disposition of the Planets and signs, and according to the properties of each Moon of the whole year. Thus, they will tell you that in such a Moon it will thunder, there will be lightning, thunderbolts, hail, or rain; there will be war, plague, famine, treasons, ambushes, and other such follies that almanac-makers are accustomed to predicting for us at random. And yet they are not so foolish that they do not know how to use the same caution as those over here, who, though most are quite coarse in matters of belief, nevertheless put God above all and say that "the wise man has command over the stars" <note>A reference to the Latin maxim *Sapiens dominabitur astris*</note>. They have small booklets or tablets that they call *racuin* <note>A transliteration of a local term for astrological tables or calendars</note>, in which is everything that is to happen throughout the year, which they sell quite dearly to whoever wants to know the outcome of the year. ->*On Africa, the third part of the world.*<-

Abraham Ortelius <note>A famous Flemish cartographer and geographer, creator of the first modern atlas.</note> in his *Synonyms* and *Geographical Treasury* writes what follows regarding this third part of the world.
<margin>Africa <term>Αφρικη</term></margin>
Africa, which is called Libya by the Greeks and Africa by the Latins, is called Chamesia in the Sacred Scriptures <note>original: "Chameſia"; likely a reference to the Land of Ham, son of Noah.</note>. Josephus <note>A 1st-century Romano-Jewish historian.</note> calls its people the Phutites. It is considered the third part of the world by the ancients. Joannes Leo <note>Also known as Leo Africanus, a famous traveler and diplomat of the 16th century.</note> writes that it is called Iphricia by the inhabitants. Thevet says that it is named Alkebulan <note>original: "Alkebulā"</note> by the Arabs and Ethiopians, and Besecath by the Indians. In our own tongue, it is generally called the Land of the Moors. In the works of Dioscorides, Serapio reads "Lyonsi" and "Linza," or likewise "Lintouin" for Africa.

There is also Africa Proper, which according to Ptolemy <note>An influential Greco-Roman mathematician and geographer.</note> is the part of Africa along the Mediterranean Sea, between the regions of Mauritania and Cyrene. It is called Zeugitana by Pliny, who divides it into Old and New Africa, as does Dion. It is the Naphthuhim to the Hebrews, according to the testimony of Arias Montanus <note>A Spanish orientalist and editor of the Antwerp Polyglot Bible.</note>. Today, the Kingdom of Tunis is located in this place. See Carthage, Libya, and Zeugitana.

Libya <term>Λιβύη</term> is a region which Stephanus <note>Stephanus of Byzantium, a 6th-century author of a geographical dictionary.</note> writes is also called:
*   Olympia <term>Ὀλυμπία</term> <gloss>meaning celestial or heavenly</gloss>
*   Oceania <term>Ωκεανία</term> <gloss>referring to the ocean</gloss>
*   Eschatia <term>Εσχατία</term> <gloss>meaning the remote or furthest land</gloss>
*   Coryphe <term>Κορυφή</term> <gloss>meaning the summit or peak</gloss>
*   Hesperia <term>Εσπερία</term> <gloss>the western land</gloss>
*   Ortygia <term>Ορτυγία</term> <gloss>land of the quail</gloss>
*   Ammonis <term>Αμμωνίς</term> <gloss>land of the god Ammon</gloss>
*   Ethiopia <term>Αιθιοπία</term> <gloss>land of the burnt-faced people</gloss>
*   Cyrene <term>Κυρήνη</term>
*   Ophiusa <term>Οφιούσα</term> <gloss>abounding in snakes</gloss>
*   Cephenia <term>Κηφηνία</term>
*   and Aeria <term>Αερία</term> <gloss>meaning airy or lofty</gloss>.

To the Hebrews, Libya is Ludim, as witnessed by Arias Montanus. In ancient inscriptions, Libya is more often read with a "y" in the first syllable. In the time of Procopius, that part of Africa which extends from Alexandria to the city of Cyrene was called Libya, as he himself testifies in the sixth book of *On Buildings*. In this stretch is also the Libya of Ptolemy, which he designates as "Proper" at the beginning of the fourth book of his *Geography*, where he numbers it among the eleven regions of Africa; however, in the description of it, he calls it the District of Libya. ...to himself, Gerard Mercator <note>A famous Flemish cartographer (1512–1594) known for the Mercator projection map.</note> calls this same outer region by the same name, with what reliability, I confess is not clear to me. Libya, according to Antonius, is a city in Spain near Calahorra.

According to Pliny, that part of Africa called "Proper" is named Zeugitana; Aethicus calls it Zeugin. Marius Niger thinks that wandering race of men emigrated from this part of Africa, roaming through our Europe region by region in the manner of Nomads, whom the Italians call <term>Zingani</term> and <term>Zingari</term>, the High Germans call <term>Ziegeiner</term>, the Low Germans call <term>Egyptenaren</term> and <term>Heylieden</term> (as if you were to say "heathens" and "Egyptians"). We call them Egyptians because they say they are exiles from Lesser Egypt (where in the world that may be, I confess I do not know; Great Egypt is known to everyone, but I have not yet learned of its division into Greater and Lesser from any trustworthy author). The French call them <term>Baumiens</term> <note>original: "Baumiens"; an old term for Bohemians, then used for Romani people.</note>, as Bellonius testifies. Pius II <note>Pope Pius II, also known as Enea Silvio Piccolomini.</note> says they came from the region of Zogoria located near the Caucasus. Aventinus brings them to us from the borders of Turkey and Hungary. Philippus Bergomas says they come from Chaldea.

Rhodiginus thinks they are Moors and were expelled by the Saracens; Bellonius says they have their origin in Bulgaria and Wallachia (where formerly lived the <term>Sicynni</term>, a word not far from <term>Ziegeiner</term>); and he adds that he found the same race on the journey from Cairo to Macarea. Likewise, he mentions finding them somewhere on the banks of the Nile river, but there too they are considered newcomers. Thevet says they are called there by the Arabs and Moors <term>Rasolheramy</term>, that is, <term>Thieves</term>. The same Bellonius reports that this class of women has a temple near Constantinople in the city of Pera, divided into many small rooms, where they prostitute themselves to Christians as well as Muslims, and he says this is permitted to them by a privilege of the Turkish Emperor. Leo Africanus also mentions that these <term>Zingani</term> live in certain places in Africa, such as in Agadez and on the borders of the kingdom of Borno <note>original: "Rubiæ"; likely referring to the Bornu Empire.</note>. It is established from historians that this people first became known to our Europeans around the year 1417. They are a race of men living under the open sky in extreme poverty; they are filthy, sun-burnt, and everywhere dressed in exotic fashion. They profess to be Christians. But they seek their living by theft and divinations (for they all want to be seen as palm-readers), with which they deceive silly women and children. They have a leader chosen from their dregs, whom they obey. Among themselves they use a proper and peculiar language which no one else understands, which Aventinus, however, asserts he has recognized through experience to be Wendish <note>A term formerly used to refer to Slavic languages.</note>.

HISTORY OF THE ORIGIN OF THE...

The Arabic term *Faraca* <note>Likely from the Arabic root *faraqa*, meaning to divide or separate.</note>, which means as much in the language of the Arabs as "divided" or "partitioned" in our common tongue. There are two reasons for this name: the first is because the Mediterranean Sea divides it from Europe and the Nile from Asia; the second is that King Iphtic <note>Likely referring to the legendary King Ifriqis ibn Qays, from whom the name "Africa" is traditionally derived in Arabic lore.</note>, having been defeated in battle by the Assyrians and driven from his kingdom, fled to this country. Having crossed the Nile, he did not stop until he reached the region where the city of Carthage sits. This is why the Arabs call it Africa (except for the Western part). There is no small dispute among African historians to know truly who populated this third part of the world; some say it was the Palestinians, others those descended from the Sabaeans and other certain peoples of Asia. The Arabs, Adamians, and Ethiopians give it the name *Dalkebulam*; the Indians and Javanese call it *Behecath*, according to André Thevet in his *Universal Cosmography*. As for Africa "Proper," which extends along the Mediterranean Sea between Mauritania and the region of Cyrene—which Pomponius Mela calls "Little Africa," Pliny calls *Zeugitana*, and the Hebrews call *Napthtubem* <note>original: "Napthtubem"; a reference to Naphtuhim from the Table of Nations in Genesis.</note>, according to the report of Benito Arias Montano—it is bounded differently according to Leo Africanus in his *Description of Africa*, Duarte Barbosa in his *Navigations*, André Thevet in the preface of his *Cosmography* and Books 5 and 6, and Abraham Ortelius in table 4 of his *Great Theater of the Universe* and in his *Geographical Synonyms*.

### On the Origin of the Africans.

Josephus, a Hebrew author, in Book 1, Chapter 13 of the *Antiquities of the Jews*, maintains along with the Holy Scriptures that the Africans took their source and origin from the Hebrew Patriarch Abraham, saying these words: "After the death of Sarah, Abraham took Keturah in a second marriage, by whom he had six children, all wise and industrious men: namely Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah <note>The text uses 16th-century variants: Zembrané, Iazaré, Madané, Luſubac, and Sua.</note>. Each of these also had children: for Shuah had Sheba and Dedan, and there were also Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah <note>Text variants: Sabacan, Dadan, Ophré, Anoch, Ebibas, and Eldas.</note>. Abraham sent them all to inhabit other regions; they occupied the Troglodyte country and all of Arabia Felix, which lies along the Red Sea. It is also said that Epher <note>original: "Ophré" or "Apher"</note> departed with great troops and seized Libya, which the children of his successors have possessed since then, naming it Africa after the name of their ancestor." This is why Leo Africanus, speaking of the source of those of his nation, says that their historians are in little agreement on this origin; some hold that they are descended from the Palestinians, who, having been driven out long ago by the Assyrians, fled to Africa, and finding it good and fertile, settled there. Others are of the opinion that they are descended from the Sabaeans, a people of Arabia Felix, before the Assyrians or Ethiopians ever chased them from that country—and this reasoning agrees with the aforementioned opinion of Josephus. But the third opinion is that the Africans are said to be descended from certain peoples of Asia who, being at war with their enemies, came for safety to Greece, which at that time...

But he says that this should be understood to refer to the Africans who are white, namely those who reside in Barbary and Numidia, especially as it seems that by this he intends to support the journey of the Tyrians under Dido when she came to found the city of Carthage. However, the land of the Negroes <note>original: "Negres"</note> was already populated, seeing as King Iarbas the Gaetulian—whose territory is the country of the Negroes or Nigritians—threatened Dido with ruin if she did not agree to his suit, which was to marry her, according to the account of Virgil in his *Aeneid*. 

And thus he concludes that the Negroes or Nigritians all descended from the lineage of Cush <note>original: "Chus"</note>, son of Ham <note>original: "Cham"</note> the cursed, and the eldest of the children of the great Noah. With this consideration, the Nigritians would also be of the blood of the whites, insofar as Mizraim—from whom the Palestinians and Egyptians emerged—was a close relative of Cush, as the aforementioned Josephus maintains in Book 1, Chapter 6 of the aforementioned *Antiquities*. This is a more than necessary conclusion: that however it may be, the Africans came from the race of Ham, and all the Negroes, both of Ethiopia and other countries within Barbary as far as the Cape of Good Hope, have no other source than Cush, as almost all authors are in common agreement. 

Thus one can see how Africa is divided into white and black Moors <note>original: "Mores"</note>, some estimated to descend from Ophre <note>Likely Epher, a grandson of Abraham.</note> or Apher, and from the Palestinians and Sabaeans; and others from Cush, Father of the Ethiopians, who have never hesitated to call themselves Cushites <note>original: "Cuseens"</note> after the name of the first of their race and family. But these peoples are still divided each in their own respect, insofar as the whites are further divided among themselves into five peoples: those of Sanhagia, Musmuda, Zeneta, Hacara, and Gumera. 

The Masmuda <note>original: "Masmuda"</note> are those who reside in the Atlas Mountains in the western part, from Hea to the Servi River; they also reside in the valleys near the aforementioned mountain on the side that faces south. These hold four provinces: Hea, Sus, Gazula, and Marrakesh <note>original: "Maroc"</note>. The Gumera also inhabit the mountains of Mauritania, namely on the side where the Atlas looks toward our Mediterranean, and they stay along the river called Rif, which is near the Pillars of Hercules <note>The Strait of Gibraltar.</note>, and waters all the kingdom of Tlemcen <note>original: "Teleusin"</note>, which is that Mauritania that the Latins called Caesariensis <note>original: "Cesaree"</note>. 

These five peoples have always been at war with one another; those who were the strongest also made themselves masters of the countryside, and by forcing the conquered to serve them, they also compelled them to reside in the cities. The greatest and most victorious built their houses in the fields <note>Referring to rural estates or chateaus.</note>, just as the nobility does in France and other provinces of Europe. Some of these—namely the five white peoples of Africa—spread throughout the African country; such were the Zenetes when they drove out the true lords of the family of Idris <note>original: "Iddris"</note>, from whom the Kings of Fez had originated. Likewise, the Zenetes were driven out by certain Numidians called Zanhagi, who ruined the entire country of Tlemcen and Tamasna <note>original: "Temesme"</note>, putting everyone to the sword except those of their own language and family, and remaining in Doukkala <note>original: "Ducala"</note>.

From there took their beginning the kingdoms of Morocco, Fez, Sus, and Heà, and others of Mauritania, until the conquerors were, some time later, defeated and driven out by the Africans who were relatives of the deceased rebel who had revolted against Al-Qa'im. The Arabs, meanwhile, keep to the countryside, and by this means keep the inhabitants of the cities in check; they are more secure and more respected, feared, and dreaded in the deserts than if they stayed in the cities.

# HISTORY OF THE ORIGIN OF THE

### [LANGUAGES OF AFRICA]

...the coming of the Arabs to Africa, which provides a greater argument that this country was first populated by the Arabs coming from **Arabia Felix** <note>original: "Arabie heureuse," the classical name for the southern Arabian Peninsula, encompassing modern-day Yemen.</note>: but these people for the present use the **Arabic** <note>original: "Arabesque"</note> language more than their own tongue, because of their regular dealings and frequent contact with the Arabs, although they corrupt the pronunciation of the other language and pervert its words, just as happened in Greece and Italy, where the Barbarians altered and corrupted the sweetness and naturalness of the two most beautiful and rich languages in the universe. The Negroes or Blacks of this Africa have languages of their own without having anything in common with that of the Arabs, one of which is named **Songhai** <note>original: "Sungai," the language of the Songhai Empire.</note>, which, being more difficult and less articulated than any of the others, is current and in vogue in the kingdoms of **Galata, Timbuktu, Guinea, Mali, and Gao** <note>original: "Galata, Tombut, la Guinee, Melli & Gago"</note>; the other is called **Guber**, used and spoken in the lands of Guber, Kano, Katsina <note>original: "Chefena," likely referring to the Hausa city-state of Katsina.</note>, Perzegreg, and Wangara <note>original: "Guangra"</note>, where they are beginning to babble the Arabic language a little, though it is poorly pronounced and quite corrupted. The inhabitants of **Bornu** and **Gaoga** have their own particular language, as do those of **Nubia**, the latter having similarities with the Arabic, **Chaldean** <note>original: "Chaldaique," often used in this period to denote Aramaic or Syriac.</note>, and Egyptian languages. Whereas today all the peoples of Africa along the Mediterranean Sea speak the Arabic language, albeit corrupted, except for the inhabitants of **Morocco, Fez, Souss, Tlemcen, Tunis, and Algiers**, who use the ancient **Berber** <note>original: "Barbaresque," referring to the Amazigh languages.</note> or African language, otherwise called Syrian or Moorish, because the Arabs frequent these regions very little; it is true that some among them nevertheless use the Spanish language, because the Spaniards are ordinarily with them, as reported by **Leo Africanus** <note>A famous 16th-century North African diplomat and author of "Description of Africa."</note>, a member of that nation, in book 1 of his *Description of Africa*; **Duarte Barbosa** <note>original: "Odoard Barbosse," a Portuguese explorer.</note>, a Portuguese, in his *Voyages and Navigations*; **Paolo Giovio** <note>original: "Paule Ioue," an Italian historian.</note> in his *Epitome of the Affairs of Muscovy*, chapter 5; **Guillaume Postel** in his treatise on the *Alphabets of the Twelve Languages* and in that of the *Phoenician Letters*, together with the preface to his *Arabic Grammar*; **André Thevet** in book 1, chapter 4, and book 5, last chapter, book 18, chapter 3, and book 20, chapter 1 of his *Universal Cosmography*; **Abraham Ortelius** in table 41 of his *Great Theatre of the World*; **Louis Le Roy** in books 2 and 8 of *On the Vicissitude of Things*; and **François de Belleforest** in book 3, chapter 32 of volume 2 of his *Cosmography*, and book 6, chapters 3 and 4 of the same volume.

Those who have seen and visited Africa far and wide for two or three hundred years until now have asserted that there are **one hundred ninety-seven** kingdoms within it, not counting several large and terrifying deserts, some of which are more than one hundred leagues across. Of these kingdoms, thirty-two are **Muslim** <note>original: "Mahometistes"</note>; the others are Christian, who are subjects of the great **Prester John** <note>original: "Prestegiani," the legendary Christian monarch of the East, here associated with the Emperor of Ethiopia.</note>, Emperor and King of the Ethiopians; others are heretics participating in both **Judaism and Christianity**, such as the kingdom of **Nubia**; others are half-idolatrous and partly steeped in the errors of Muhammad; and some are entirely steeped in the abomination of **Idols**; and others recognize neither God, nor Religion, nor Law, such as those of the **Cape of Good Hope**.

# LANGUAGES OF THIS UNIVERSE.

...several peoples and nations, both Moors and Negroes, each of whom use several and various languages, all different and dissimilar, understood by no others than those who speak them as their mother tongue. This is confirmed by all modern travelers and navigators.

**Leo [Africanus]** <note>original: "I. Leon"; referring to Joannes Leo Africanus, a 16th-century diplomat and author of the *Description of Africa*.</note>, cited above in the first book of his description of Africa, writes that the greater part of the Arabs who are in **Numidia** <note>A historical region in North Africa, primarily in modern-day Algeria and parts of Tunisia.</note> are versifiers who compose beautiful songs, in which they describe their battles along with the manner of hunting and the passions of love with such great grace and eloquence that it is a marvel; they make their compositions in verse and meter in the fashion of the vernacular poets of Italy, such as stanzas and sonnets. This same author, following what was said above, notes that the Arabs hold poetry in high regard and admire it greatly. Devoting themselves to it, they compose verses most often enriched with perfect elegance, even though their language is corrupted in many places; a poet, however little renowned he may be among them, is very welcome before their Lords, who, for the pleasure they receive from their verses, reward them generously. He assures you that it would be impossible for him to express the great grace they possess in their verses. These Arabs are those who presently inhabit the regions toward **Tunis** and **Tlemcen** <note>original: "Telesin"; a city in northwestern Algeria.</note>, who are in the pay of the Kings of those lands, and who go in summer to the frontiers to receive in the month of October from the treasurers of those Kings the pension given to them, after receiving which they retire to their deserts to pass the winter according to their ordinary custom.

A certain African, **Abdul Malik** <note>original: "Habdul Malich"</note>, a chronicler of the city of **Marrakesh** <note>original: "Maroc"</note> in Africa, has composed histories in his language divided into seven parts.

Beyond what we have reported above regarding the vernacular poets among the Arabs, there are also such poets among the Africans, and principally in the city of **Fez** in Africa, who compose verses on various subjects, and especially on love, expressing the passions they suffer for the thing they love; for their affections extend without shame to both sexes, as almost all **Muslims** <note>original: "Mahometistes." The author reflects a common early modern European bias in his description of local customs.</note> do regarding this sin every year on the day of the birth of their <note>original: "faux Prophete"</note> Prophet Muhammad. These poets assemble in the morning in the great square, where the Magistrates and principal men of their cities assist; there, these poets recite their compositions made in praise of the said Muhammad. He who is judged to have done best is praised and gifted by the judgment and sentence of the magistrates. In times past, the Kings had this trial held in their palace and gave to those who did best one hundred **ducats** <note>A gold coin used as a trade currency throughout Europe and the Mediterranean.</note>, a horse, a slave, and one of the most beautiful robes in his wardrobe; and each of the others received fifty ducats to encourage them to do well. But the Kings have forgotten this courtesy, though the Lords of the city of Fez still continue it.

## ON THE KABBALAH OF THE ARABS, TURKS,
## & Africans.

The book of the doctrine of the Prophet Muhammad <note>original: "Mahometh"</note>, received among the Muslims <note>original: "Mahometistes"</note> and followers of the Quran <note>original: "Alcoranistes"</note> as authentic, just as the Quran itself is, together with the Quranic doctors, create a certain Kabbalah <note>Here used to mean a mystical or numerological system of interpretation.</note> of numbers, entirely contrary to the true interpretation of them followed by the wisest in the Scriptures. For they say that the number 1 signifies that there is but one God, without having an equal, son, or companion; in this they show their foolishness, not seeing how much the threefold number <note>The Trinity.</note> is respected in Holy Scripture. The number 2 signifies Adam and Eve; 3 signifies Michael, Gabriel, and *Zaraphiel* <note>original: "Zaraphiel"; this name is unknown to the author, but likely refers to Israfil, the angel who blows the trumpet in Islamic tradition.</note>, a word unknown to us, whom they say are Archangels and Secretaries of the Divinity. By the number 4, they understand the Law of Moses <note>The Torah.</note>, the Psalms of David, the Gospel, and the *Al-Furqan* <note>original: "l’Alfurcam"; a name for the Quran meaning "The Criterion" or "The Distinction."</note>; and by 5, the prayers that God commanded Muhammad for himself and for his people; and 6 signifies the six days in which God made the world with its adornment. The number 7 includes the seven Heavens; 8 signifies the eight Angels who will have the charge of carrying the throne of God when He comes to perform the judgment; and 9 signifies the nine miracles of Moses. The number 10 signifies the ten days of fasting performed by those who go to Mecca—namely, three while going and seven after having completed their pilgrimage. By the number 11 are denoted the eleven stars that Joseph saw bowing down to him; 12 represents the twelve months of the year, but for 13, one must add to the aforementioned eleven stars the Sun and the Moon. By 14, they understand the fourteen luminaries that hang before the throne of God, each of which is one thousand five hundred years in length. By 15, they take the fifteenth day of the month of Ramadan—which they say is the month of March <note>The author incorrectly identifies Ramadan with March; as a lunar month, Ramadan rotates through the solar seasons.</note>—because on that day Muhammad received his Quran from Heaven. The number 16 represents the legions of Cherubim angels who are around the throne of God singing His praises. By 17, they say are understood the names of God which are between the summit of heaven and the deep abysses of the earth, without which—acting as obstacles—the world would be ruined by the heat that hell would vomit upon the earth. By 18, they understand the spaces that are between the air and the throne of God. The number 19 represents the arms of the river of Hell called *Saqar* <note>original: "Zaché"; likely referring to Saqar, one of the levels or names of hell in the Quran.</note>, which will cry out on the Day of Judgment, and to which the damned must respond. As for the number 20, its significance is that on such a number of days in the month of Ramadan, David received the revelation of the Psalms; and 21 because on such a day Solomon was born, just as on the 22nd of Ramadan God pardoned David for his sin regarding the murder of Uriah. They say that the 23rd is sacred to the Nativity of Jesus, son of Mary—which is false, for he was conceived in the month of March and the Virgin gave birth in December. On the 24th, God spoke to Moses; on the 25th, the Sea was divided to give passage to the children of Israel; on the twenty-sixth, God gave the tables of the commandments written or engraved by the very finger of His eternity, according to—

> Joannes Leo <note>Joannes Leo Africanus (c. 1494–1554), a famous Berber Andalusian diplomat and author of *Description of Africa*.</note>, an Arabic author, in Book 3 of his *History of Africa*, in the chapter on Diviners: "Among the Arabs and Africans there is a great number of diviners, who are divided into three types or qualities. In the first are those who predict future things through the knowledge given to them by Geomancy <note>original: "Germantie," likely a corruption of *Géomancie*, a method of divination that interprets markings on the ground or the patterns formed by tossed handfuls of soil, rocks, or sand.</note>, tracing their figures; they pay as much for each as is customary for a person of their standing. The second type consists of others who, placing water in a glass basin along with a drop of oil—which makes it transparent like a steel mirror—say that they see demons passing in large squadrons, some coming by sea and others by land, resembling a great exercise of men-at-arms when they wish to camp and pitch their pavilions. At the moment they see them stop, they interrogate them about the things they wish to be fully informed of, to which the spirits respond with certain movements of the eyes or hands; this shows well enough how devoid of sense are those who put their faith in it. Sometimes they place the vessel in the hands of a child of eight or nine years, whom they ask if he has perceived such or such a demon; and the little child, as simple as he is young, answers them 'yes,' although they never let him answer until they have first coached <note>original: "embouché"; meaning to prime or tell someone what to say.</note> him. And I assure you, there are some so foolish and dull-witted that they believe everything, which is why they spend a great deal of money on it. The third species is of women who make the common people believe they have great familiarity with 'white demons.' And when they wish to divine at the request of anyone, they perfume themselves with certain odors; then (as they say) the spirit they have conjured enters their body. They feign a change in their voice so it seems to be the Spirit giving the answer through their throat. Seeing this, the man or woman who has come to learn something, having received an answer from the demon, leaves some gift with great reverence and humility for the said demon."

> But those who have acquired, beyond their natural beauty, knowledge and experience of things, call these women *Sahacat* <note>original: *Sahacat*, an Arabic term for women who love women</note>, which is equivalent to what is called *Fricatrices* <note>original Latin: *Fricatrices*, literally "rubbers," a historical term for lesbians</note> in the Latin language. To tell the truth, they are afflicted by this wicked vice of using one another carnally; I cannot express it with a more proper term, nor one that suits them better. When they see a woman (among those who come to question them and seek advice on their affairs) who possesses any beauty, they fall in love with her just as a man would. In the name of the spirit, as reward and payment, they demand carnal copulation from her. Those to whom they make this immodest and dishonest demand—being unskilled in such deceptions—most often consent, thinking they are pleasing the demon. There are also many women who, having developed a taste for this game and being enticed by the sweet pleasure they receive from it, pretend to be ill. By this means, they send for one of these divineresses <note>original: *devineresses*, female fortune-tellers or seers</note>, and most often have the husband himself deliver the message. Then, they suddenly reveal their "illness" to them and where the remedy lies. To better cover their wickedness, they make the husband believe—foolish and simple as he is—that a spirit has entered his wife's body. Having her health as his priority, he is told he must give her leave to join the ranks of the divineresses and converse only in their company. They know how to perfectly and easily persuade some "John" <note>original: *Ian*, a period slang term for a simpleton or a cuckold</note>, who, consenting to it, prepares a sumptuous feast for this whole "venerable" band. At the end of the feast, they begin to dance to certain instruments played by the Black people. Then the woman has leave to go wherever she pleases. However, some men, subtly perceiving this trick, drive the spirit out of their wives' bodies with the terrible sound of dull thuds and a good thrashing. Others, pretending to the divineresses that they themselves are possessed by the spirit, deceive them by the same means the women used on their husbands.

The same Joannes Leo <note>referring to Leo Africanus, the 16th-century Moorish diplomat and author of *The Description of Africa*</note> in the book cited above, in the chapter on enchanters, writes the following words after what is stated above.

> There is yet another kind of diviner who are called *muhazzimin* <note>original: *muhazzimin*, likely referring to *mu'azzimin*, those who perform incantations or exorcisms</note>, which means enchanters. They are esteemed for having great power to deliver anyone who is possessed by the devil, for no other reason than that sometimes they emerge with their honor intact when the outcome follows what they requested. When this does not happen, they claim—to hide their ignorance and fraudulent deception—that the demon is an infidel <note>meaning a non-believer or non-Muslim spirit</note>, or else that it is some celestial spirit. Their manner of conjuring them is as follows: they form certain characters within circles in the middle of a hearth or other place; then they paint certain signs on the hand or forehead of the sick person. Having perfumed them with certain scents, they begin the enchantment, conjuring the spirit, asking it by what means it entered this body, where it is from, and what its name is, adding to this a command that it must leave immediately. There is yet another sort of enchanter who governs themselves by a rule called *Zairagia* <note>original: *Zairagia*, referring to the *Zairja*, a complex astrological device used by medieval Arab scholars to find answers to questions through numerical calculation</note>, that is to say, Cabala. But they do not study this science at all to gain knowledge of it, because they believe it is acquired naturally. And (to tell the truth) they give infallible responses to what is asked of them; but this rule is very difficult...

### Concerning the Region of the Ethiopians.

**A**braham Ortelius, in his *Synonyms* and *Geographical Treasury* <note>Abraham Ortelius (1527–1598) was a pioneering Flemish cartographer and the creator of the first modern atlas.</note> regarding Ethiopia <gloss>original Greek: Αἰθιόπια</gloss>, notes that Ptolemy identifies two regions of this name in Africa: one which he designates as lying below Egypt, and the other which he calls "Interior" [Inner] Ethiopia. This latter region is perhaps today's Zanzibar; whereas the former is now inhabited by the Abyssinians and is called "Abexim," or "Hhabas" by Garcia de Orta <note>Garcia de Orta was a 16th-century Portuguese physician and a pioneer of tropical medicine</note>, and—with the Arabic article added—"Alhabas" by Benjamin <note>Benjamin of Tudela, a 12th-century Jewish traveler</note>, the names differing only in the sound of the vowels. Pliny writes that all Ethiopia was formerly called "Etheria" and "Atalantia." These Ethiopians are called "Chusei" [Cushites] both by themselves and by all Asians, according to Josephus; Arias Montanus <note>Benito Arias Montano was a 16th-century Spanish orientalist and editor of the Antwerp Polyglot Bible</note> testifies to me that they are still called "Cushites" by the Cushitans today. Isaac Tzetzes records that they are called "Cepherides." Moreover, you will read that they were also called "Indians" under the entry for "Rhizophagi" [Root-eaters]. Ancient history, however, identifies both Eastern and Western Ethiopians, as Heliodorus names them in his 9th book: the former in Asia, the latter in Africa. Herodotus also places them in Asia among the Indians in his books *Thalia* and *Polymnia*, where the difference between the two groups is described. The *Chronicon* of Eusebius, at the year of the world 3580, has them rising near the Indus River, adding that they later settled around Egypt. Philostratus, in his 3rd book, writes—or perhaps trifles—that they once lived by the Ganges River before there was an African Ethiopia. But even the serious author Pausanias, in the 2nd book of his *Description of Greece*, places them near the Seres [Chinese] people and the island of Seria, where the custom of making silk from worms exists. Claudian, in his poem *On the Old Man of Verona* and in his *Panegyric on Stilicho*, calls these same Easterners "Black Indians." Likewise Tibullus in his 4th book, *In Praise of Sulpicia*. Pomponius Mela calls them the "Black Tribes." Strabo says the "Ethereal Ethiopians" are the furthest peoples within Carthage, reaching as far as the Cinnamon-bearing region. Herodotus, in his 3rd book, mentions the "Macrobians" [Long-lived] Ethiopians, who inhabit Africa toward the Southern Sea. An anonymous ancient commentator on Ptolemy’s *Quadripartitum* names a part of Ethiopia "Great Asia"; in Saint Jerome's *Life of Saint Matthias*, I read: "This is Ethiopia, where there is the incursion of the Apsari and the Port of Hyssus." Dorotheus calls this "Inner Ethiopia." However, in place of "Apsari," he puts "Phasis." Therefore, this Ethiopia—whether real or mythical—is located around Colchis <note>Colchis is an ancient region on the coast of the Black Sea, in modern-day Georgia</note>.

The Memnones <gloss>original Greek: μέμνονες</gloss> were a people of Ethiopia below Egypt according to Ptolemy, Pliny, and Stephanus. If I am not mistaken, Sidonius Apollinaris, in his poem to the elder Valerian, calls them "Memnonian Indians," saying they are scorched by the neighborly face of Aurora <note>Aurora is the Roman goddess of the Dawn; the text suggests they are darkened by being so close to the rising sun</note>.

The Rhizophagi <gloss>original Greek: Ριζόφαγοι, "Root-eaters"</gloss> are a people of Ethiopia dwelling along the Astaboras and Astapas rivers according to Diodorus Siculus. They are also called the Elei <gloss>original Greek: ἔλειοι, "Marsh-dwellers"</gloss> by Strabo in book 16. These Rhizophagi are placed among the Indians near the Estabaras River (as Pierre Gilles translates it) by Aelian in book 17 of *On Animals*; in Conrad Gessner’s printed Greek manuscript, the term "exa-imeni" <gloss>original Greek: ἐξαίμενοι</gloss> is used, but it is clear from Pliny, Mela, Strabo, and Ptolemy that it should read "Astaboras" <gloss>original Greek: ἀσταβόρας</gloss>, as they also describe these Root-eaters near this Astaboras, which is a branch of the Nile. From this passage in Aelian (and others, such as book 16, chapter 33, where he says Libya is near the Indians), it is understood that the Ethiopians living by the Nile were also called "Indians"; and that Virgil, in book 4 of the *Georgics*, was not without ancient authority when he also called these people "Indians" (though "colored" [sun-darkened] to distinguish them from others). Procopius agrees with this in his *On Buildings*.

...where he says the Nile flows out from the mountains of the Indians. Therefore, he calls Ethiopia "India." Hyginus also describes "Thebes of the Hundred Gates" <note>original: "Thebas Hecatompylas"</note> as being in India, and in Book 1 of his *Limits*, he writes that the Indians dwell from Egypt all the way to the Ocean toward the Equator.

We find in the records of the Greeks that the Egyptian land was named by them at various times *Melambolos* <note>original: μελάμβωλος, "black-soiled"</note>, *Hephaistia* <note>original: ἡφωισία, "land of Vulcan"</note>, *Potamia* <note>original: ποταμία, "river-land"</note>, *Ogygia* <note>original: ὠγυγία, "ancient"</note>, and *Aetia* <note>original: αἰθιοπία ὑπό αἴθυμα, perhaps meaning "Ethiopia under the burning heat"</note>. Cephidas, according to Tzetzes—or Pliny in Book 5, chapter 8, and Book 6, chapters 29 and 30 of his *Natural History*, and Solinus in his *Polyhistor*, chapter 33—reports that it was formerly called *Etheria*. However, according to Strabo in Book 2, there was only one part of it that bore this name, which was the final part toward Libya and the region called Cinnamon. 

This country was first named *Atlanie*, after the giant Atlas <note>Atlas was a Titan in Greek mythology, often associated with the Atlas Mountains in Northwest Africa</note> who is said to have reigned in Africa; and that a son of Vulcan named Ethiops, arriving there, gave it his name, *Ethiopia*. Others say that this word "Ethiopia" comes from the Greek word *aitho* <note>original: αἴθω</note>, which signifies "burned," and *ops* <note>original: ὤψ</note>, "face," because the Ethiopian country is situated beneath the Burned or Torrid Zone. Some others hold that this country took its name neither from the Greek words above, nor from Ethiops the son of Vulcan, but from a certain Oriental nation called the *Ethopeans*, which formerly lived along the Indus River. 

Beyond what is said above, I will report that the Ethiopians were formerly called *Auases* by the Egyptians, according to Strabo in Book 2, due to the diversity of colors of the earth in their country, and that the people themselves were distinguished by this variety; because of this, the name has remained with them even now. There is a region called *Gazacie*, named *Abas*, *Hhabas*, and *Alhabas* by good ancient authors (as seen in Girava's *Geography*), the Arabic article "Al" being added as a graceful ornament. From this comes the name *Abassia* <note>Abyssinia</note>, by which the Ethiopians of today are called "Abyssinians" by all the nations of the earth, and are known and understood by this word throughout the East, according to the report of Marco Polo in Book 3, chapter 43 of his travels. 

Strictly speaking, however, the true Abyssinians are those who inhabit Africa toward the North, bordering the deserts that separate Egypt from Ethiopia. They have their faces marked with a hot and glowing iron according to the custom of the country, which has caused many to believe they used this brand in place of Baptism—a thing which is entirely far from their intention. Those of this nation are also named *Nubians*, from the Province of Nubia, which at present is somewhat under the subjection and principality of the great Emperor or Christian King Prester John <note>Prester John was a legendary medieval Christian monarch whose kingdom was long sought by Europeans in Asia and later Africa</note>, of whom we shall speak at length hereafter. 

The Hebrews have written that *Chus* <note>Cush</note>—a Hebrew word—signifies in French "Ethiopian" or "black." This was the name of one of the sons of Ham, son of Noah, from which Chus the Ethiopians have descended and proceeded, named in the Hebrew language *Cushim* <note>original: כּוּשׁים</note>, as confirmed by Josephus in Book 1, chapter 12 of the *Antiquities of the Jews*, Eusebius in Book 9, chapter 4 of his *Preparation*, and St. Augustine in Book 16, chapter 11 of his *City of God*. In fact, these Hebrews call Ethiopia *Chus* in their language, the Portuguese call it *Cussia*, the Greeks *Aithiopia* <note>original: Αἰθιοπίαν</note>, and the Latins *India*. As the interpreter of Hebrew, Chaldean, and Greek names from the Old and New Testament says: "Ethiopia is called *Chus* in Hebrew, and is interpreted as black or blackness; for *Aithiopia* in Greek signifies heat or fire. The region of the Ethiopians, rising from the Indus river near Egypt..."

...Egypt, between the Nile and the Ocean, and in the South under the very vicinity of the sun lies the whole nation itself, which was first called Etheria, then Atlantia, and soon after Ethiopia, after Ethiops, the son of Vulcan; according to Pliny <note>Gaius Plinius Secundus, author of *Natural History*</note>, Book 6, chapter 30; Ptolemy, Book 4, chapter 7; Pliny, Book 5, chapter 8; Ezekiel 29, chapters 10 and 30; Isaiah 11, chapter 11; and Raphael Volaterranus <note>A 15th-century Italian humanist and geographer</note>, Book 12 of his *Geography*. It is very certain that all the Negroes or Black people of Africa, Ethiopia, and other countries that stretch from Barbary <note>A term formerly used for the coastal regions of North Africa</note> to the Cape of Good Hope have no other source than this Cush <note>original: "Chus"</note>, son of Ham <note>original: "Chā"</note>, child of Noah, as almost all Hebrew authors agree. The histories of these Ethiopians also say the same, according to Marinus the Roman, and these people have never found it difficult to call themselves Cushites <note>original: "Chuseens"</note>, after the name of the first of their race and family. This is confirmed by Raphael Volaterranus in Book 12 of his *Geography*; Marco Polo of Venice in Book 3 of his travels; Hayton the Armenian in chapter 54 of his histories; Leo Africanus <note>original: "I. Leon"</note> in Book 1 of his *Description of Africa*; Burchard of Mount Sion <note>original: "F. Brocard"</note> in his description of the Holy Land; Girolamo Cardano <note>original: "H. Cardan"</note> in Book 1 of *On the Variety of Things*; Francisco Álvares in his histories of Ethiopia; Damião de Góis in his treatise on the Ethiopian religion; André Thevet in Book 2, chapter 13, and Book 4, chapter 10 of his *Cosmography*; Arias Montanus; and François de Belleforest in volume 2, Book 6, chapters 3, 22, and 23 of his *Cosmography*; as well as Abraham Ortelius in Table 4 of his *Great Theater of the Universe*.

In this regard, a certain modern figure named Ludovicus Carretus <note>original: "Louys Carrectus"</note>—a Jew by nation and religion who later became a Christian—writes in his epistle to the Jews that the greatest part of the Nubians (so named after a city in their country which is currently bordered on the West by the country of Garga, one of its ancient dependencies, separated by deserts) are of the race of the Israelites. This country extends along the Nile, joining to the South the deserts of Goran toward the region of Amazen; to the North it has the land of Egypt and Barca; and to the East are the Nile and the Ethiopian lands, where the Nile is so low and muddy that it is impossible to find passage to go into Egypt. He claims the greater part of these Ethiopians are descended from the Israelites who were sent from Jerusalem to Ethiopia by Solomon, King of Israel, to the Queen of Sheba at her request, numbering twelve thousand people—namely, one thousand from each tribe of Israel. These Israelites multiplied like the sand of the sea, and each of them followed their own military signs and standards, as is more fully described in the *History of the Kings of Ethiopia* and in the travels to Ethiopia by Don Francisco Álvares, chapters 134, 137, and 138.

### *On the black color of the complexion of the Ethiopians, Negroes, Black people, or Moors of Africa.*

Some ancient Greek and Latin authors have written that the black color of the complexion of the Ethiopians was made and caused by the vehemence and insupportable heat and burning of the sun's rays, which struck directly upon their region located in Africa under the Torrid Zone. However, Herodotus in his third book and Strabo in the 15th book of his *Geography* have denied this for several reasons, attributing it entirely to the seed of their fathers—who were black and curly-haired by nature—who fathered them.

For this reason, the children of *Mizraim* <note>original: "Mitzraim"</note>, his son—who are none other than the Egyptians—were born with a black color, rendered in this way different from other men, as is confirmed by *Rashi on Genesis 12* <note>original: "R. Selo Gen. 12." Referring to Rabbi Shlomo Itzhaki, the medieval commentator</note>. The children of *Cush* <note>original: "Chus"</note>, the first of his sons—who are the Ethiopians—were also born of a very black color, not because of their Province or Region being situated under the violent heat of the Sun’s rays (as most of the ancient Greek and Latin authors have written), but rather because of their origin. This is evidenced by the fact that under the Equator and the Torrid Zone, and in places closest to both tropics among the very black peoples who inhabit them today, there are found several others who are white or chestnut in color. These people are descended from the blood of *Abraham*, *Solomon*, and other Jews, whose ancestors came to live among these Negro or black peoples. Likewise, those who live in *India* under the same climate, or even the same parallel, would be of the same and similar color as the others mentioned above if they did not proceed from a different origin. Furthermore, in the *West Indies*, the Indians are for the most part of an olive or "Indian" color—that is to say, a dark ashen color—except for a few who live in a single place not far from the others, for which reason they are held as enemies by their neighbors. In contrast, the true Ethiopian Negroes or blacks take great pleasure and glory in their black color. What is more, as far as the 35th degree of latitude in Africa beyond the Equator, the peoples there are very black in color, contrary to those who are on this side of the said Equator—among whom are the Spaniards, Sardinians, Syrians, Arabs, Babylonians, Chaldeans, Persians, Susians, Turks, Tartars, Gedrosians, and other peoples situated 35 degrees on this side of the Equator at a similar latitude—among whom no Ethiopian, Negro, or black peoples are currently found. This leads us to believe entirely the opinion of the aforementioned Hebrews, who have asserted that *Cush*, named above and descended from *Ham* (who was white in color like his brothers *Japheth* and *Shem*), fathered these Ethiopians, Negroes, and blacks as a perpetual testimony of the fault and guilt he committed against his own father; as is confirmed by *Gilbert Génébrard* in Book 1 of his *Chronography*, following *Berosus* <note>A Hellenistic-era Babylonian writer and astronomer</note> in Book 3 of his *Antiquities*.

**Jean Bodin**, on the contrary to the characters named above, wrote in chapter 5 of his *Method of History* <note>original: "methode de l'histoire"</note> that which follows: "Now it is enough for us that the center of the east and the west is placed in **America**, because that region is separated from the **Indies** and **Africa** by infinite distances. The **Equator**, however, is the middle of the North and South as far as the whole universe is concerned; but of this hemisphere which is on this side of the **Equator**, it is the 45th degree of latitude: so that whatever lies between there and the pole is assigned to the North; the rest to the South. And since the ancients, except for **Posidonius** and **Avicenna**, defined the habitations of men by the tropical and polar circles, thinking there was no place for health or habitation beyond them, this error must be snatched away. For it has been found by frequent voyages that the region of the **Equator** is most healthy; but under the **Tropics**, the regions burn with incredible heat, and indeed the reason is at hand. For the Sun rises higher at the **Equator**, and is moved much more swiftly because of the size of the circle than in the tropics; furthermore, **Alvaresius** <note>Francisco Álvares, a Portuguese missionary and explorer</note> writes that the waters there freeze with frost in the month of June, provided the South wind blows. To this is added a great force of rains, the incredible height of mountains, and an abundance of forests; finally, the color and face of the men is not at all black, but like that of olives. On the contrary, under the **Tropics** there are violent heats, no rains, no forests, and rare rivers; a perpetual plain of sands, except in **Arabia** the Blessed and certain places in **India**, because of the nature of the East and the mountainous region. Finally, the dark skin of the inhabitants, not only of the **Ethiopians** but also of the **Indians**, as **Ctesias** <note>A Greek physician and historian</note> long ago and our own men have discovered. For I can hardly be persuaded by what a certain learned man relates, that men become black from the curse of **Cush**; and long ago the opinion of **Herodotus** was mocked, who thought the seed of **Ethiopians** was black. For it would be necessary for **Ethiopians** born in **Scythia** <note>An ancient region in Central Eurasia</note> to be black, and **Scythians** born in **Ethiopia** to be white, since all peoples have long ago been mixed by the multitude and frequency of colonies. But we see that men, just like plants, gradually degenerate when the soil is changed. This is the same reason why fire and the sun, as **Aristotle** teaches, stain men with a dark color; furthermore, **Pliny** writes that lions in **Ethiopia** are black, which the poet **Oppianus** testifies to having seen in his book on hunting." This same author, always continuing his discourse, says at the end: "And since under the tropics and both Poles..."

> "The highest extreme of cold and heat is found under the Equator, yet the climate there is the same as for those who are positioned at the 30th degree; for here and there, **White Ethiopians** <note>original: 'Leuco Æthiopes' — a term used by ancient geographers for light-skinned groups in Africa</note> are said to exist. The Maurusians, who are none other than Moors, live at present in Mauritania in Africa, so named from the Greek word <note>original: Μαυρὸς (Mauros)</note> **"black"**, which signifies black according to some authors, because these people are colored with this tint. I do not wish to doubt this, although it seems to me that the entire stretch of the country named Mauritania does not have black people, and that the Nigritians rather deserve such a name; but let us move on, and grant to the ancients what is neither honest nor fitting to deny them through contradiction, since the word has such a meaning that it carries not only blackness, but an obscurity and dark color. Thus, one should not draw a conclusion if there are white people in Mauritania, since we know there are several kinds of Moors. Modern navigators and travelers who have described in detail the Cape of Good Hope and the countries in Ethiopia toward the Indian Sea have written the following regarding the doubt so much debated by many over the matter of the color of these Moors or Negroes. There are those who hold that the heat of the Sun is the cause of this blackness, whereas **Strabo** in book 15 seems to be of the contrary opinion when he says that heat is not the cause of the blackened color; for those who are in their mothers' wombs, even though the Sun has not spread its rays upon them, are nevertheless born black and <term>swarthy <note>original: "bazanez" — tanned or dark-skinned</note></term> upon the earth. He then adds that they become such by the force of their fathers' seed, whom they are made to resemble. Those who attribute and report the cause to the Sun, such as **Alexander of Aphrodisias** in book 1 of *Problems*—who, inquiring why the Sun blackens a man, whitens linen, softens wax, and hardens mud, responds also that the aptitude of the affected matter is the cause of this; for, he says, the materials of our body, except for the <term>phlegm <note>original: "pituite" — one of the four humors</note></term>, whenever they are too heated, they cause the hide and the skin to blacken. With this author agrees **Albert the Great** in his book *On the Nature of Places*, when he says that Southern men, and those who stay in hot and meridional parts, and above all the Ethiopians, are black as much for the heat of the Sun in the places where they stay as for the heated disposition of their bodies. This is because, in the first place, the seed of generation in them is hot, and the <term>womb <note>original: "matrice"</note></term> of the women who receive this seed is also very hot and very dry; from which it happens that the seed of the man, once conceived, being digested by a violent <term>concoction <note>An archaic term for the "cooking" or processing of nutrients and fluids by internal body heat</note></term>, the blood of the formed fruit becomes <term>adust <note>original: "adufte" — a medical term for substances scorched or parched by internal heat</note></term> and burnt. The more subtle moisture being driven out by the humor of the place, that which is coarse and earthy, and is also burnt, remains and causes the blackness in the body and the skin of men. Thus, the more earthy parts are also very strong, and the bones very white, as can be seen in the teeth of Moors; whereas their flesh, tinted by the burnt blood, is blackish and swarthy. All these reasons are very good, and drawn from nature itself, but for my part, I cannot attribute so much to the strength of...

...as we have said, is the winter of the Equinoctial <note>The regions located on or near the Equator.</note> lands. However, as the Sun moves further away, the season there becomes mild and temperate, without any sign of drought, nor scorching, nor lack of fruits, grasses, and greenery—contrary to what the ancients tried to prove with arguments that lacked any truth. Furthermore, we find in the logs and journeys of the aforementioned modern navigators and travelers that the inhabitants of **Quilao** <note>Kilwa, located on the coast of modern-day Tanzania. In the 16th century, the "Indies" often broadly referred to lands across the Indian Ocean.</note>, a country of the Indies, are diverse in color (which contradicts those who attribute the darkness of the complexion to the heat of the country). For they are usually olive-colored, neither white nor black; others there are white like those of Barbary, and others black like the darkest people of Ethiopia. On the **Island of Saint Thomas** <note>São Tomé</note>, situated directly under the Equator, the children of Europeans are as white as in Europe, unless their white wives die and they marry daughters of the Ethiopians <note>The author uses "Ethiopian" as a general term for Black Africans.</note> who have become Christian and live in our fashion; for the children who come from them are no longer white, but rather blackish. This is evident proof that the Sun is not the cause of men being black in Ethiopia and other places, but that this comes from the disposition of the seeds <note>An early reference to the concept of heredity rather than environmental conditioning.</note>.

To conclude this matter, we shall inform the readers that according to the accounts of modern writers who speak of the Negroes, Blacks, or Moors of Africa: after one has passed the land of the **Bazanez** <note>Likely the Sanhaja, a Berber tribal confederation.</note> people, now called **Azanaghes**, who are tawny in color and live on this side of the river **Niger** or **Senegal**, one comes to the land of those Negroes, Blacks, or Moors living beyond the aforementioned river Niger or Senegal. The separation between the said Bazanez and the said Negroes, Blacks, or Moors is formed by the said river Niger, otherwise called the Senegal, the source of which is held to come from the same place as that of the Nile. It has a similar ebb and flow to the Egyptian river, watering and enriching the lands through which it passes in the same way, and nourishing crocodiles and other beasts or aquatic monsters that are commonly seen in the Nile. Because of this river, the whole country is named **Senega** <note>Senegal</note>; looking toward the West is the Great Ocean Sea, to the South is the kingdom of **Gambre** <note>Gambia</note>, and toward the North is this great river which separates (as has been said) the aforementioned Bazanez from the said Negroes, Blacks, or Moors, and marks the beginning of the country called in these times **Lower Ethiopia**. These Negroes, Blacks, or Moors of Senegal are at present **Mahometans** <note>Muslims</note>, though they are not as sophisticated or fixed in their superstition as the white Moors, especially since they have no one to instruct them, and they do not pay much heed to it, particularly since Christians have begun frequenting their lands. These Black people go about entirely naked, except for some coverings of goat skin or cotton to cover their private parts. In this country, though outside the power and jurisdiction of the King of Senegal, are the **Barbarins** and **Seretes** <note>Likely the Berbers and the Serer people.</note>, who are as black as the others. Past this country, one goes to the kingdom of Gambia where the inhabitants are also black, partly idolaters and partly Mahometans. Following this coast, hugging Africa and rounding the **Cape of Palms**, you enter the kingdom of **Guinea**, in which are **Molegete**, **Benin**, and **Manicongre** <note>The Kingdom of Kongo</note>, where there are also many Black people, partly idolaters—changing their gods every day first thing in the morning—and partly Mahometans, as is amply described by **John Leo** <note>Leo Africanus (c. 1494–1554), a famous traveler and geographer whose descriptions of Africa were the primary source for Europeans for centuries.</note>.

### Of the Kingdom of Ethiopia.

We read nothing in all of Holy Scripture, and even less in the secular histories of the ancients, that provides any certain memory of the race, succession, and lineage of the Kings of Ethiopia. It is true, however, that we find it written in ancient histories that Cush <note>In the Bible, Cush is the son of Ham and grandson of Noah, traditionally considered the ancestor of the Ethiopian people.</note> was the first who founded the kingdom of Ethiopia, which still endures to this day, as Marino Sanuto <note>Original: "Marin Romain." Likely referring to the Venetian geographer or a similar chronicler of the era.</note> deduces in his *History of the Ethiopians*, based on the reports from the histories of the Abyssinians. This seems to be what the poet Homer intended to denote when speaking of the great antiquity of this kingdom. These histories of the Abyssinians or Ethiopians state that after this Cush, the first King of Ethiopia, died, six other Kings, his successors, reigned after him. There is no memory of their names in the histories, and it is certain that one cannot truly determine how long they reigned, nor in which city or town of Ethiopia their principal residence was located, until, after these six Kings, the seventh retired to the city of Axum <note>Original: "Caxumo," referring to Aksum, the ancient capital of the Aksumite Empire.</note>. In this city, the principal royal seat of the Ethiopian Kings was established until the time of Jesus Christ, as the aforementioned Marino Sanuto deduces. He states that the greatest certainty we have regarding the lineage of the aforementioned Ethiopians is that Makeda, otherwise known as Nicaula, Queen of Ethiopia and Egypt—as Josephus writes in Book 8 of the *Antiquities of the Jews*—came from Saba, an island of the Nile later called Meroë by Cambyses. She traveled to the great King Solomon in the eleventh year of his reign, had acquaintance with this great King, and had by him a son first named Melich <note>Commonly known as Menelik I.</note>, then David. He was the first who most firmly established the kingdom of Ethiopia, for it is certain, according to the histories of these Ethiopians, that the preceding Ethiopian Kings had no stability or security in their Kingdom until Arue, who first established the seat of his kingdom at Axum for 400 years. Then Agabo his brother for 200; then Ghedur, otherwise called Sabannit, for 100 years, having conquered all of Ethiopia; then Makeda his daughter for 80 years, who was the mother of the said Melich, who reigned 29 years; Audede his son for one year; Auda his brother 11 years; Gegasio 3 years; Zangua 44 years; Gasio 1; Antet 61; Basara 9; Cavada 2; Chauze 10; Endur 9; Guaza 1; Eudrach 1; Chaales 1; Setija 17; Aglaba 3; Auscua 1; Breguas 17; Guaze 17; Beseclugna 17; Baazena 27, under whose reign our Lord Jesus Christ was born. But this is not overly certain nor assured, as Gilbert Génébrard <note>A prominent 16th-century French theologian and Hebraist.</note> demonstrates in his *Cosmography*.

Among modern writers, Don Francisco Álvarez <note>A Portuguese missionary and explorer (c. 1465–1541) who provided one of the first detailed European accounts of Ethiopia.</note>, in his travels through Ethiopia describing the city of Aksum <note>original: "Caxumo"</note>, one of the largest and most spacious cities in all Ethiopia, states that the Ethiopians maintain that this city was once the residence of the Queen of Sheba. She was a native of an Ethiopian city named Sabaim, near the aforementioned Aksum, and she went to visit Solomon, King of Judea, moved by the renown of his great wisdom, as is contained in the Old Testament. The Ethiopian histories—which the aforementioned Álvarez claims to have seen and read in the Abyssinian language <note>Referring to Ge'ez, the liturgical language of the Ethiopian Church.</note>, originally taken from Hebrew and Chaldean—name her Makeda. In this same city, this Queen—named Candace in the 8th chapter of the Acts of the Apostles and by her own name, Judith, who was born two miles from this city—made her ordinary dwelling. She was the first to plant the faith of Jesus Christ in Ethiopia and caused the first church to be built and constructed. This church is still standing and is very beautiful, bearing the title of Saint Mary of Zion, because the sacred table and stone of the altar were brought there from Mount Zion in Jerusalem. This lady was converted to the Christian faith by one of her agents, a Eunuch whom the Deacon Saint Philip instructed in the Gospel doctrine.

->ON THE CUSTOMS AND RELIGION OF THE ETHIOPIANS<-
->& Abyssins.<-

The histories of Ethiopia contain that this Queen of Sheba named Makeda, of whom I have spoken before, having arrived from her own country at the city of Jerusalem to see and know the wisdom of the great Solomon, King of the Israelites, was entertained very familiarly by this great King. By him, she had a child who brought to Ethiopia the true knowledge of the God of Israel, as well as the ways of life and ceremonies of the Jews regarding the act of circumcision. Marius Victorinus <note>A 4th-century Roman grammarian and Christian philosopher.</note> confirms these words, saying that these same histories report that this Queen of Sheba, having visited King Solomon as stated, obtained from him twelve thousand Jews—namely, one thousand from each tribe of Israel—whom she took with her to her country of Ethiopia. These people having greatly increased and multiplied there into families, the nobles of that country have since boasted and bragged of being descended and proceeded from the seed of the Israelites. For this reason, those Ethiopians are still circumcised today—not out of necessity for their salvation, as they assert, but rather to demonstrate and teach the prerogative and grandeur of their bloodline. Or, as written by Ludovicus Carretus <note>A 16th-century Jewish physician who converted to Christianity; his "Epistle to the Jews" was a well-known conversion narrative.</note>, a Jew by nation mentioned above, in his Epistle to the Jews, it is for the sake of the memory and love they bear for our Lord Jesus Christ, who was circumcised. It is true that not all Ethiopians observe such a custom; specifically those who are furthest south, nor those who are close neighbors to the Libyans and the Nigrites <note>A historical term used to describe the peoples of the Niger River region.</note>, because they are for the most part of the superstition of Muhammad. These people are indeed circumcised but do not follow the law of Baptism; and the Cafres <note>From the Arabic 'kafir' (non-believer), a historical term used by explorers for various ethnic groups in Southern Africa who did not practice Islam or Christianity.</note> do not care for either of these ways of doing things. Because they hold that they preserve the articles of the Christian Faith exactly as they were written by the Apostles, they have a sovereign King or Emperor to whom is permitted and given the appointment <note>original: "collation"; the legal right to grant a church benefice or office</note> of all the benefices of the Kingdom—these being his own—as well as other ecclesiastical dignities and prelacies. Although he is neither a priest nor in any way promoted to the sacred order and rank of the clergy, he oversees an infinite number of Archbishops and Metropolitans <note>High-ranking bishops who preside over a provincial capital</note>, each of whom has under him at least twenty Bishops. They have one great and sovereign leader to whom all report, who ordinarily follows the Royal Court and who depends upon the Patriarch of Grand Cairo <note>Historically the Patriarch of Alexandria, who resided in Cairo and oversaw the Ethiopian Church for centuries</note> who formerly resided in Alexandria in Egypt. However, in our own time, they have recognized by letters and by actions the Holy Apostolic See of Rome, not as the appointer or as having the power to establish their Bishops, but only as the head of the Churches and the mother of the flock for the foundation of doctrine, just as Christians have at all times testified concerning this Holy See and the universal Bishop who presides there.

The histories of these Ethiopians recount that this Queen Candace—of whom mention is made in the Acts of the Apostles under the title of Queen of Ethiopia—was named in her own right **Judith**. She was born two miles from **Axum** <note>original: "Caxumo"; the ancient capital of the Aksumite Empire</note>, a city in the Kingdom of Angote in Ethiopia, and she was the first to plant the faith of Jesus Christ our Lord in Ethiopia. She also caused the first church to be built there, which is still standing—very beautiful and magnificent—bearing the title of **Saint Mary of Zion**. This name was given because the Table and sacred stone of the altar were brought there from Mount Zion in Jerusalem; for the Ethiopians have a custom of naming their churches after stones <note>The author refers to the *tabot*, the consecrated wooden or stone slab representing the Ark of the Covenant</note. This Queen was converted to the Christian faith by her agent, **Philip the Eunuch**, whom the Deacon **Saint Philip** (one of the seventy-two disciples) instructed in the Gospel doctrine, as is contained in chapter 8 of the Acts of the Apostles.

This is confirmed by **L. Carretus** in his *Epistle to the Jews*, alleging Psalm 72: *The kings of Sheba and Ethiopia shall offer gifts* <note>original: "Reges Sabæ, & Æthyopiæ, munera offerent"</note>, and Psalm 68: *And furthermore Ethiopia shall clap her hands* <note>original: "præterea Æthyops plaudet manibus suis"; usually rendered as "Ethiopia shall stretch out her hands unto God"</note>; and by **Dom Francisco Alvarez** in chapters 38 and 84 of his *Travels in Ethiopia*, where he reports the Letter of the Ethiopian King **David** sent to Pope Clement VII in the year of Salvation 1524 by the hand of the same Alvarez. It is true that **Friar Brocard**, in his description of the Holy Land, holds that these Ethiopians were taught the Christian religion by **Saint Matthew**. This he took from **Simeon Metaphrastes**, a Greek author who says that the tradition of the fathers holds that this Saint Matthew was the only one among all the Evangelists who wrote his Gospel in the **Hebrew language**, and not in the Syriac language (as some have wished), nor in the Greek language as **John Calvin** has written. This is argued, firstly, because all the ancient Fathers of the Church held it so, and secondly, because all the fragments that **Saint Jerome** cites as being taken from this Gospel are pure Hebrew. The strongest reason is that Saint Matthew did not write only to the Jews and the Syrians, but to all the peoples of the Orient, the furthest of whom used this language as the most learned and grammatical; and even now they use it when celebrating their Masses in that language. For this reason, **Saint Bartholomew** seems to have carried the Gospel of this Saint Matthew with him above all others into those countries. A copy of which **Pantenus**...

...Panthenus, a contemporary of Origen, having traveled to those regions, brought reports from those places to Egypt, according to Eusebius, Book 5, Chapter 10 of his histories <note>Eusebius of Caesarea was a 4th-century historian; here the author refers to his *Ecclesiastical History*</note>. Furthermore, it is probable that this St. Matthew wrote his Gospel in the Hebrew language for the sake of these Ethiopians, whom he knew had been given to him by God for his Apostleship. In fact, those Ethiopians did not understand Syriac in his time, and even less Greek, but certainly Hebrew, which they learned from childhood in their schools—as they still do today, just as we learn Greek and Latin. In this way, we must interpret the words of Chapter 8 of the Acts of the Apostles, speaking of the Eunuch of the Queen of Ethiopia who, while sitting in his chariot, was reading the Prophet Isaiah. St. Jerome, in the life of the aforementioned Panthenus, writes on this subject that around the year of salvation 178, these Indians <note>In early modern geography, "India" was often used broadly to include Ethiopia or any land beyond the Red Sea</note> sent ambassadors to Demetrius, Bishop of Alexandria, to beg him to send them teachers; and that Panthenus was sent there, where he found the said Gospel of St. Matthew written in Hebrew letters and language by the said St. Bartholomew, which he carried back with him upon his return to Alexandria.

Marius Victorius writes that this Christian religion was spread throughout Ethiopia during the time of Abraham and Azba, brother Kings of Ethiopia, around the year of salvation 460. This Church of Axum <note>original: "Caxumo"</note> is the most revered in Ethiopia due to its antiquity, having 150 Canons named **Debereres** <note>Dabtaras: a unique class of lay clergy in the Ethiopian Church responsible for music and liturgy</note>, and as many Monks; for the religious orders are more privileged than all other ecclesiastics. There are two heads called **Nebreti** <note>The *Nebret* is the traditional title for the administrator of the Cathedral of Our Lady Mary of Zion in Axum</note>, one over the Canons and the other over the Monks, each having his own court and administering justice to those committed to his care. These men are richly endowed, receiving every day after the Mass—which is sung in the **Tangique** language <note>The author likely refers to Ge'ez, the liturgical language of Ethiopia, which he classifies as an "ancient dialect of the Chaldean language"</note>, an ancient dialect of the Chaldean language, as I noted earlier in the chapter—their bread and wine from their endowment, except on Good Friday when they eat nothing at all. The King, Archbishops, and Bishops, when traveling through the country or walking in public, always have a cross and a vase full of earth carried before them; so that by the one, they may be warned that they are mortal, and by the other, that through the death and passion of Jesus Christ they are saved. Priests marry there, but monks do not, so as to leave a lineage <note>Ethiopian Orthodox tradition allows secular priests to be married, but monks remain celibate</note>; but if their wives die, they are not permitted to enter into a second marriage. There is a great diversity of religious orders who take vows and profession of chastity, obedience, and poverty, living in common and performing great and admirable abstinences under the rule of St. Anthony and St. Macarius, although they have other holy Abbots and Monks who have built many of their monasteries. Of our saints, they recognize only the glorious Virgin Mary Mother of God, St. Michael, the Apostles, and especially St. Thomas and St. Matthew—the latter having converted the inhabitants of Meroë, and the former having traveled from Ethiopia to the Indies to win over the Indians. Among the Martyrs, they greatly revere St. Stephen and St. George, and of the Confessors, the hermits St. Anthony and St. Macarius—whomever unfortunately blasphemes against them is burned alive in the public square. They have a number of particular saints from among those who lived holily in their own country. They do not confer Baptism upon anyone until they are forty days old if it is a male, and sixty
