-># LANGUAGES OF THIS UNIVERSE<-

**Free Macedonia** <note>original: "Macedoniæ Libera"</note> is the name used in Caesar’s *Civil War*, Book 3. Livy likewise writes that the Romans intended for the **Macedonians** and **Illyrians** to be free. In later periods, mention of "Macedonia I" and "Macedonia II" <note>Referring to the administrative division of the province into Macedonia Prima and Macedonia Salutaris</note> is frequent, and they are often recorded in the records of the Church Councils.

**Thrace** <gloss>original Greek: "Θραακη"</gloss> is a region of Europe celebrated by Ptolemy and others, situated by the Euxine Sea <note>The Black Sea</note>. I also find it written with a diphthong as *Thraecia*. Among the ancients, it was also called **Aria** <gloss>original Greek: "ἀρία"</gloss> and **Perca** <gloss>original Greek: "πέρκη"</gloss>, as well as **Odrysa** <gloss>original Greek: "ὀδρυσά"</gloss> according to Suidas (Livy mentions certain of its people as the *Odrysae*). It was also called **Crestona** <gloss>original Greek: "χρηστόνα"</gloss> by Isaacius, following Lycophron; and **Scython**, as Erythraeus asserts. We find **Trachia** written for **Thracia** quite often among authors of the Middle Ages. Josephus writes that in Hebrew it is named **Tiras** <gloss>original: "Thiras"</gloss>. Ancient writers designate the inhabitants of this Thrace by various names. Herodotus writes that they were called **Bithynians** after they crossed over into Asia; for previously they were called **Strymonians**. They are called **Bardi** by Martianus, and **Dolongi** <gloss>original Greek: "δύλογκοι"</gloss> by Lycophron and Stephanus. Formerly they were named **Briges** <gloss>original Greek: "βρίγες"</gloss>, as Eustathius records. Arrian calls certain of them the **Autonomi** <note>Meaning "those who live by their own laws" or the independent Thracians</note>. Some among them are called **Sapae** and **Sapaei** <gloss>original Greek: "σαπάοι ἢ σαπαῖοι"</gloss> in Strabo, and in Ptolemy, the **Sapaic Prefecture**. Likewise, they are called **Sipii** by Stephanus. Also the **Saii** <gloss>original Greek: "σάϊοι"</gloss>, the **Sinti**, and the **Sintiae** <gloss>original Greek: "σίντοι ἢ σίντιες"</gloss>. Paul the Deacon identifies two Thraces, writing that both were devastated by Attila under the Emperor Valentinian the Younger—perhaps following Xenophon, who in Book 6 of the *Cyropaedia* describes an Asiatic Thrace in addition to this European one. For he thus names **Bithynia**, in which Calpes and Heraclea are located. The *Register of Offices* <note>original: "liber Notitiar.", referring to the *Notitia Dignitatum*</note> and Ammianus (Book 27) list six of its provinces by name. Likewise Sextus Rufus; and these are: Thrace (properly so called), Second Moesia, Scythia, Europa, Rhodope, and Haemimontus. Today it is called by the single name **Romania** <note>In this period, "Romania" or "Rumelia" referred generally to the Byzantine or Ottoman Balkan territories</note>, and it is always so called by Paul the Deacon and Conrad of Lichtenau; likewise Jordanes in his book on the succession of kingdoms. In place of Thrace, Serapio reads **Badachas** in the chapter on the Caltrop <note>A type of plant, *Tribulus*</note> in Dioscorides. Isocrates, in his first *Panegyric* oration, is the authority for the fact that Thracians once lived in the neighborhood of the Athenians. Strabo (Book 11) writes that Thracians with the surname **Saraparae** are said to live above Armenia. See **Saraparae**. Eustathius testifies from "Sacred History" that there is a certain **Mountainous Thrace** in the southern parts of Africa above Alexandria. There is also a Thrace that is a city and island of Arabia Felix <note>The southern Arabian Peninsula</note>, as Diodorus (Book 5) relates. See **Bithynia**.

The **Iazyges** <gloss>original Greek: "ἰάζυγες"</gloss> in Strabo and Ptolemy are a people in European Sarmatia beyond Germany toward the East. Wernherus thinks they are those who today are called the **Iaz**; they have a peculiar and ancestral language. Cromer calls them the **Iasuingi**. Others are called the **Iazyges Metanastae** <gloss>original Greek: "μετανάσται", meaning the "displaced" or "migrant" Iazyges</gloss> by Ptolemy. Niger writes that their region is now called the **Field of the Cumans**. Strabo (Book 7) also mentions the **Royal Iazyges** <gloss>original Greek: "βασιλεῖς"</gloss>. Ovid (in *Letters from the Black Sea*, Book 4) uses *Iazis* as the singular form. Could they be the same as the **Lassii**?

**Pannonia** <gloss>original Greek: "παννονία"</gloss> in Ptolemy is a region of Europe which he divides into Upper and Lower. Optatus the African mentions three Pannonias, contrary to all other writers and ancient coins. Under the Roman Emperors Arcadius, Honorius, and their successors (as is clear from Rufus, Marcellinus, and the *Register of Offices*), these Pannonias were distinguished by several names, such as **Pannonia Prima** (perhaps the same as Upper Pannonia), **Pannonia Secunda** (the same as Lower Pannonia), **Savia**, or...

**Ripensian** <note>original: "Ripenfis"</note>; the *Book of Notices* <note>The *Notitia Dignitatum*, a document of the late Roman Empire's administrative organization</note> also lists **Ripariensian** and **Valeria**. Aurelius Victor, in his *Lives of the Emperors* Decius and Didius Julianus, mentions **Busalian Pannonia** and **Sabaria** <note>Modern Szombathely, Hungary</note>. I believe this region is the same as **Savia**, named after the river Sava, while the former was named after the city of **Busali**. **Cibaliensian Pannonia**, named after the city of **Cibalae** (which Ptolemy places in Lower Pannonia), is mentioned by the Deacon; Cassiodorus, in the third book of his *Various Letters* to the Colosseum, names **Sirmiensian Pannonia** as the former seat of the Goths. **Amantine Pannonia** is also found in the works of Lazius, cited from Ptolemy and Pliny. 

**Upper Pannonia** is today occupied by **Austria**, **Carinthia**, and **Carniola**. The whole of **Lower Pannonia** is, in our time, under the rule of **Hungary**, which is named *Vuegierska* in the Slavonic tongue. **Savian Pannonia** is referred to as **Slavonia** by Lazius. Beatus Rhenanus calls the region of **Valeria** by the name *Krabaten* <note>Likely a reference to Croatia</note>. The part of **Paeonia** facing toward Thrace, where Mount Rhodope is situated, is now called **Clocotinitsa** <gloss>original Greek: "κλοκοτίνιτζα"</gloss>, according to Eustathius. See the booklet by Wolfgang Lazius, written in the German language, concerning the Kingdom of Hungary. The **Pannonians** were also once called **Paeonians** by the Greeks, but not without error, as Dio teaches in his 49th book. More than once, the name is corrupted in Appian’s *Illyrian Wars*, where "Paeonians" is read instead of "Pannonians."

->*Regarding the Tzeruian, Zeruian, Serbian, and Posnanian Region.*<-

Abraham Ortelius, in his *Geographical Synonyms* and *Geographical Treasury*, describes the region of **Moesia** <note>A Roman province in the Balkans, south of the Danube</note> as a region of Europe divided into **Upper** and **Lower**. **Upper Moesia** is called *Zirh* by Leunclavius, *Serbia* by Lazius, *Bosnia* by Cuspinian, *Tzeruia* or *Tzeruiana* and *Zeruiana* by Postellus, *Olmutiensian Moldavia* by Taurinus, and *Wallachia* by Sabellicus. Tzetzes, in his second *Chiliad*, calls it **Hungary**. **Lower Moesia** was at one time called *Flaccia*, as Sabellicus teaches. Pomponius Sabinus names it the "Granary of Ceres." Taurinus believes it is called *Wallachia*, while Lazius, Cuspinian, and Chalcocondylas call it **Bulgaria**. Petancius calls it *Sagoria*.

The **Moesians**, who dwell near Mount Haemus (and comprise the inhabitants of Lower Moesia), are now called **Blachi** <note>Vlachs</note>, according to Nicetas; Pachymerus also mentions them. Regarding the name "Moesia," I wish to add this from the *Plinian Corrections* of Hermolaus: Pliny, Tacitus, Flaccus, Virgil, Martianus, and nearly all Latin manuscripts write this name with the diphthong *oe* <note>Mœsia</note>. The Greeks, however, write it with a *y* <note>Mysia</note>. The spelling *Maesia* (with *ae*) is found in an ancient inscription; Dion Prusaeus teaches, following Homer, that it was once called **Mysia** and later **Moesia**. Jordanes records that Lower Moesia is called **Scythia**. Zosimus, in his fourth book, calls it **Thracian Scythia** and places the city of **Tomis** <note>Modern Constanța, Romania, where the poet Ovid was exiled</note> within it. Ovid, in his *Tristia*, more than once calls the same region **Scythia**, as does Arrian in his *Periplus*. I believe this stretch of land is what Plutarch calls **Pontic Scythia**, and its inhabitants **Scythogermans** <gloss>original Greek: "σκυτοσχυθαν"</gloss>. Polyaenus, in his eighth book, calls the maritime part *Pontica*. I see that the part along the shore of the Euxine Sea <note>The Black Sea</note> is frequently called simply **Pontus** by classical authors such as Ptolemy, Stephanus, and Ovid; Pomponius encompasses it under the name of **Thrace**.

## *On the Tzeruian, or Zeruuian, or Poznanian Language.*
### CHAPTER LXIV.

Guillaume Postel <note>A 16th-century French polymath and linguist known for his study of Oriental languages</note>, in his *Alphabet of twelve different languages* in the characters mentioned above, reported the following concerning this Tzeruian, or Zeruuian, or Poznanian language.

The Tzeruian or Poznanian regions are regions of our Europe, situated between Dalmatia, Illyria, Albania, Macedonia, Thrace, and the region of the Iazyges Metanastes <note>An ancient Sarmatian tribe located between the Danube and Tisza rivers</note>. Bosnia—also called Posne or Bossine—extends from Upper and Lower Pannonia toward the Gepids <note>An East Germanic tribe</note>, whose region forms part of this Bosnia, Posne, or Bossine. The Tzeruian or Zeruuian region, otherwise known as Serbia, is where Upper Moesia <note>original: "Mysie Superieure"</note> was anciently located; it extends from the Danube and Lower Pannonia (otherwise called Libuonia) toward Thrace and Macedonia. This situation moved several very learned linguists to seek the reasons why the inhabitants of these regions, located in the midst of the two most excellent languages of this world <note>Likely referring to Latin and Greek</note>, invented a language of their own, particular to themselves alone. These learned men said the following: around the year of our salvation 300, the Pannonians, Illyrians, Dalmatians, and Moesians had the same and almost identical language, mixed partly with the Greek language, partly with the Italian language, and partly with the German language, due to their proximity. Among all these peoples, a certain Jerome <note>Saint Jerome (c. 347–420 AD). In the Renaissance, the Glagolitic script was traditionally, though incorrectly, attributed to him; it is actually the work of Saints Cyril and Methodius in the 9th century</note>, a Doctor of Theology and Dalmatian by nation, invented the characters of the letters, which he derived partly from Hebrew characters and partly from Greek ones, which we shall represent in the following chapter in a figure. This was done so that these peoples, being different and unlike other peoples in their language, might also be so in the characters of their letters. They used these for so long that the Roman Church was able to tolerate the Greek Church alongside it. But since that Church was separated and forbidden from communion with the Roman Church for certain specific reasons and considerations, those who were closer neighbors to the Greeks invented other characters, mostly Greek, without changing the names and designations of the first and oldest ones. For the former were already hateful to the Greeks because of their separation from the said Roman Church, and to themselves because of the interdiction of their Church.

But it is more appropriate to reveal the cause of such a great schism or division in the Church of Jesus Christ. The Greeks differed from the Latins in that they consecrated using <term>Azymes</term> <note>unleavened bread</note>; in that they believe the Holy Spirit proceeds only from the Father; that they practiced the bill of divorce against an unchaste, sterile, or troublesome wife; and that their Priests married. This last point is common to all Eastern Christians, Indians, Jacobites, Maronites, Armenians, Georgians, Greeks, Vlachs (or Lower Moesians), and to be brief, to all other Priests and Ministers of all other Eastern Nations. This was even practiced among the Christians of the Latin Church until the Council of Vienne <note>Held in 1311–1312, it addressed various reforms, though clerical celibacy had been reinforced by earlier councils like the Lateran</note>. Furthermore, they celebrated only a single Mass in each place, specifically on each Sunday and the feast days of the week.

» which they celebrate according to the calculation and order of the Vernal or
» Spring equinox: The second which they call <term>of the holy Apostles</term> <note>original: "τῶν ἁγίων Ἀποστόλων"</note>, that is to say,
» of the holy Apostles, fifteen days before the feast of Saint John the Baptist, and
» the feasts of Saint Peter and Saint Paul: The third <term>of the All-Holy One</term> <note>original: "τῆς παναγίας", referring to the Virgin Mary as the Panagia</note>, that is
» to say, of the Holy Virgin, during which time many among them fast for the
» time and space of 51 days. Some others during an entire month, before
» the feast of the Assumption of the said Virgin: the fourth during the Advents
» of the nativity of our Lord, during which Lents they use
» only bread, oil, herbs, hard and soft boiled eggs with vinegar;
» regarding the other Ceremonies observed by them, they have them
» in common with us.

Along the Hyrcanian <note>The Hyrcanian Sea is an ancient name for the Caspian Sea.</note> Sea also dwell the Khazars <note>Original: "Gazari"</note>, where the Circassians, Abkhazians <note>Original: "Abgazari"</note>, and Abkhazelli are called so by the Greeks, and they use the Slavonic language even today. For the nation of the Slavs <note>Original: "Sclauenorum"</note> set out with huge forces from Scythia, and, if we believe Solinus, from the depths of Berfilia <note>Berfilia refers to a semi-mythical region in the north, often associated with the lands of the Khazars or the Volga Bulgars.</note> around the six-hundredth year after the incarnation of Christ: they occupied a great part of Europe and Asia. They also occupied Dalmatia and Illyricum. To show, however, how widely it extends, and how great the use of the Sarmatian <note>Slavic</note> language is, I will add the words of Michael of Krakow, the Canon. He traces the origin of the race to Elishah, son of Javan <note>A biblical genealogy common in the Renaissance to explain the origins of European peoples.</note>, from whom the Greek nations are derived. This may be read in his work, in the first book on Sarmatia, chapter 12, and in the following chapter he adds: consider how the language of the Slavs is most ample and diffuse, possessing very many lands. Such as the Serbs, Moesians <note>Original: "Mysii"</note>, Rascians or Bulgarians, and Bosnians—who are at this time subjugated by the Turks. Such also are the Dalmatians, Croats, Pannonians, Slavs, Carniolans, Bohemians, Moravians, Silesians, and the Poles of Greater and Lesser Poland, the Mazovians, Pomeranians, Kashubians, Sorbs, Ruthenians, and Muscovites. All these are Slavs and Wends <note>Original: "Vindelici"</note> inhabiting vast kingdoms. Furthermore, the Lithuanians are now becoming Slavicized <note>Original: "sclauonisant"</note>, as are those of Novgorod, Pskov, Smolensk, and the Ulichs <note>Original: "Ohulici"</note>, etc. These things Michael the Pole records in order. Moreover, concerning the use of the language and its possession, I have previously cautioned when speaking of the languages of the Ruthenians, Lithuanians, and Turks. It is so pleasing to the Turks that they preferred to call the seat of the Roman Empire in the Slavonic dialect *Czarzouuodom* <note>Original: "Czarzouuodom"; the author claims this means "the house of Caesar" (Tsarigrad), though the transcription is likely a corruption of the Slavic term.</note>, that is, the house of Caesar, rather than Constantinople or Byzantium. > » [the] Ionian [Sea]. <note>This continues a sentence from the previous page regarding the geographical reach of the Slavic people.</note> Whether this language should be called Sarmatian <note>Sarmatia was an ancient region of Eastern Europe; the term was often used in the Renaissance to refer to Poland.</note> or Slavonic, it has been treated in a proper commentary by Master Jan Mączyński <note>Original: "Ioannes Macznisky," a Polish humanist and lexicographer (c. 1520–1575) known for his Latin-Polish dictionary.</note>, my most venerable teacher in the Polish language, a young man among the most distinguished in lineage, talent, learning, knowledge of many languages, the Christian religion, humanity, and every kind of virtue. Once he has published these books—which I hope will happen soon, for it will serve the good and ornament not only of his own homeland, Poland, but also of other nations—the work itself will speak to how much the Slavonic speech observes analogy <note>In a linguistic sense, "analogy" refers to the regularity of grammar and structure.</note> as much as Latin or Greek. But I have said too little yet. It will appear that this language of Scythian origin, in its abundance, power, flexibility, elegance, and finally all its virtues, competes with those cultivated languages which alone seem to some to be not barbarian, but human.

A certain Italian author named Mr. Giambattista Palatino <note>Original: "Iean Baptiste Palatin," a 16th-century Italian calligrapher famous for his writing manuals.</note>, a Roman citizen, in his Italian book on the manner of teaching how to write in all types of ancient and modern letters, speaks differently of this matter:

> » It is to be known that the Illyrian peoples, or rather the Slavs <note>Original: "Schiauoni"</note>, have two kinds of alphabets; and those provinces which are more towards the East use that which is similar to the Greek, of which Cyril <note>Saint Cyril, the 9th-century missionary to the Slavs.</note> was the author, and hence they call it *Cyrillitza* <note>Original: "Chiurilizza," referring to the Cyrillic alphabet.</note>; the other provinces, which are more towards the South or towards the West, use that of which Saint Jerome <note>Original: "Hieronymo." In the Renaissance, it was commonly believed that St. Jerome invented the Glagolitic script.</note> was the author, and they call it *Bukvitsa* <note>Original: "Buchuiza," likely referring to the Glagolitic script or the initial letters of the alphabet.</note>, which alphabet is unlike all others in the world. And you should know that the speech of the common people is that very one with which they continually say their offices, and all the people understand it, just as we understand our own vernacular. It is very rich in vocabulary, but very difficult to pronounce for those who were not raised among them from childhood; and they have Missals, Breviaries, and Offices of Our Lady in it, and also the Bible.

That is to say: You must know that the Illyrian peoples, otherwise Slavs, have two kinds of alphabets. The provinces which are more towards the East use the one that is similar to the Greek, of which Cyril was the author, for which reason they call it *Cyrillitza*. The other provinces, which are more towards the midday sun <note>Meaning the South.</note> or towards the West, use the one of which Saint Jerome <note>Original: "sainct Hierosme"</note> was the author, which they call *Bukvitsa*, which alphabet is unlike any other in the universe. And one should know that the speech of the common people is the same and proper language in which they daily say their office, and all the people understand it as we understand our own vernacular; it is very abundant and copious in words, but very difficult to pronounce for someone who has not been long trained in it. And they have in it their Missals, Breviaries, and Offices of Our Lady, and even the Bible.

Aventinus <note>Johannes Aventinus (1477–1534), a Bavarian Renaissance humanist and historian.</note>, in the fourth book of his *Annals*, speaks quite differently of this matter, stating that around the year of salvation <note>Refers to the 9th century AD.</note> a certain individual named Methodius, a Bishop and native of Illyria, first invented the Venedic letters <note>Venedic refers to the Wends or Slavic peoples.</note> and translated the Holy Scripture into the Slavonic language. He persuaded the inhabitants of Dalmatia <note>A region on the Adriatic coast in modern-day Croatia.</note> to no longer use the Latin language or the ceremonies of the Roman Church, but rather their own language and these characters. After this, he went to the kingdom of Bavaria <note>The original French "Boiarie" refers to the Latin *Boiaria* (Bavaria).</note> to persuade the Bavarians of the same, but he was driven out and expelled by the Bishops of that province. From there, he retired to the country of Moravia, where he passed away and was buried in the city of Olomouc <note>Original: "Olimutz."</note>, which is to say the "Mount of Julius."

# HISTORY OF THE ORIGIN OF THE

The Author of the *Chronicle of Poland*, Book 1, Chapter 13, and Filippo of Bergamo, Book 11, state that it was Pope Nicholas who wished to command the Slavs <note>Original: "Esclauons"</note> to perform divine service and administer the Sacraments in the Latin language. When they would not comply with him, he permitted them, by way of a dispensation, to do so in their own language, so that they might appear to do everything according to his statutes. Furthermore, Gregory VII refused the King of Bohemia, Vratislaus <note>The text says "Wladislaus," but Vratislaus II (r. 1061–1092) was the contemporary of Pope Gregory VII who sought this petition.</note>, the right to have divine service celebrated in his lands in this language, because it did not suit Christian institution, nor the languages that were written upon the Title of the Cross of our Lord <note>Referring to the "titulus" or INRI inscription, which was written in Hebrew, Greek, and Latin.</note>, by which the communion of saints is preserved and retained throughout the earth; just as through the diversity of these languages, confusion and dissension take place throughout the world, as is contained in Register 7 to the Duke of Bohemia by this same Pope, and in Olaus Magnus, Book 19, Chapter 39.

Maciej Miechowita <note>The text calls him "Matthias Michou," a famous Polish scholar and physician.</note>, a Pole, in his histories of European and Asiatic Sarmatia; Siegmund, Baron von Herberstein, in his commentaries on Muscovite affairs; and Theodor Bibliander, in his commentary on the common reason of all languages cited above, have held that the word *Sclavi*, or Slavs, signifies serfs and slaves, because this people was subject to being placed in servitude. However, it is more likely (according to the aforementioned) that the Slavs—greatly renowned in times past for their valor and prowess—were thus named from the verb *Slouuo* <note>Refers to *Slovo*, meaning "word" or "speech" in Slavic; the author interprets this as "being famous."</note>, which signifies to do great things and to be famous and renowned, from which the word *Slauuuy* <note>Refers to *Slavny*, meaning glorious or noble.</note> proceeded, which means as much as celebrated and noble. Yet there is no doubt that Jordanes, the historian—an Alan by nation—believed they were named thus because of the "new city" <note>Probably referring to Novgorod, meaning "New City."</note>. The Germans regarded them as enemies and called them *Viltzos* <note>The Wilzi, a medieval Slavic tribal union.</note>. When they were first known in Europe for their great bravery in arms, they were named *Gazaros* <note>The Khazars.</note>, as they are still called today in the language of the Saracens. In fact, the Khazars who live today toward the Hyrcanian Sea <note>The Caspian Sea.</note>, where the Circassians are, are called by the Greeks *Abgazari* or *Abgaselli* <note>Likely referring to the Abkhazians.</note>, who now use this Slavonic language. This nation of Slavs, having emerged and proceeded (according to the aforementioned personages) with a great number of peoples from Scythia around the year of salvation 600, occupied a large part of Sarmatia as far as the Caspian Sea, where the Ziges or Circassians are now—a Slavic people who for some time held the Empire of Egypt under the name of Mamelukes, who were entirely ruined by Selim, father of Suleiman, the Great Lord of the Turks. They also occupied in Europe all that extent of habitable country from the River Tanais <note>The Don River.</note> to nearly half of Germany, surnamed "the Great." Thus, the Bohemians and the Lusatians are colonies of Slavs; and even from the Baltic and Sarmatian Sea to the Euxine Sea <note>The Black Sea.</note> and the Adriatic Sea, where Slavonia is now, although they also occupied Dalmatia and Illyria. The reliable author named Michael the Pole, Canon of Kraków, mentioned above by T. Bibliander in his Book 1, Chapters 12 and 13 on Sarmatia, wrote what follows on this matter according to our translation: the Slavic nation emerged and proceeded from Elishah, son of Javan <note>A biblical reference to the Table of Nations in Genesis 10.</note>, from whom the Greek nations took their origins; from which it must be gathered that the Slavonic language is very extensive.

Slavs, *Sclavi*, *Slovo*, *Slavny*, Sarmatia, Bohemia, Maciej Miechowita, Siegmund von Herberstein, Theodor Bibliander, Olaus Magnus, Jordanes, Khazars, Circassians, Mamelukes, Selim, Suleiman.

### LANGUAGES OF THIS UNIVERSE.

<note>The text continues describing the vast geography of the Slavic language.</note> ...ple and of very great extent, occupying several and diverse provinces and regions, being spoken at present by the Serbians, Mysians <note>An ancient Roman province in the Balkans, roughly modern Bulgaria and Serbia.</note>, Rascians <note>An older name for Serbs, particularly those from the medieval state of Raška.</note>, or Bulgarians; by the Bosnians, at present subjugated by the Great Turk <note>The Ottoman Sultan</note>; by the Dalmatians, Croats, Pannonians, Slavonians, Carnians <note>People from Carniola, modern Slovenia.</note>, Bohemians, Moravians, Silesians, Great and Little Poles, Mazovians, Pomeranians, Kashubians, Sorbs, Ruthenians <note>Ancestors of modern Ukrainians and Belarusians.</note>, and Muscovites. All of these are Wends <note>original: "Vindelices"</note> or Slavs inhabiting various very large and ample kingdoms; even the Lithuanians of today use and employ the Slavic tongue in their speech, along with the people of Novgorod, Pskov, Smolensk, and Halych <note>original: "Nugardiens Plescouiens, Smolnenses, & Ohuliciens"</note>. What is more, the Turks take such delight in the use of this Slavic language that they prefer to call the seat of the Empire by a word from that language, *Czarouudó* <note>Likely a corruption of "Tsarigrad" (Tsar-gorod), meaning "City of the Caesar/Emperor."</note>, which means "House of Caesar," rather than Constantinople or Byzantium. Raphael Volaterranus <note>Raffaele Maffei, a Renaissance humanist.</note> writes the following about it:

> That the ancient Greek letters were almost the same as those that are now Latin is judged by the bronze Delphic tablet, which was dedicated to Minerva in the Palace at Rome and was visible in the library during the time of Pliny, as he himself testifies. Later, they were altered by the Latins, and finally corrupted by the subsequent barbarianism of the Lombards, as can still be seen in their monuments and books; the same fate befell the Greeks as happened to our own, with the neighboring Illyrians corrupting their letters. For this reason, to this very day, the Dalmatians and Illyrians use these characters, which they received from the Greeks and have since debased. <note>original: "Quapropter in hunc vsq; diem Dalmatę & Illyrici his vtuntur characteribus, quos à Graecis acceptos dehonestatūt."</note>

The previously mentioned Siegmund, Baron von Herberstein <note>A famous diplomat and author of "Notes on Muscovite Affairs" (1549).</note>:

> The Slavonic language, which today is called "Sclavonica" by a somewhat corrupted term, is very widely spread: being used by Dalmatians, Bosnians, Croats, Istrians, and along the long stretch of the Adriatic Sea as far as Friuli <note>original: "Forum Iulij"</note> and the Carnians, whom the Venetians call "Charsi"; likewise the Carniolans, Carinthians, and as far as the Drava River; the Styrians below Graz, along the Mur as far as the Danube; and from there the Mysians, Serbs, Bulgarians, and others living as far as Constantinople; furthermore the Bohemians, Lusatians, Silesians, Moravians, and those living along the Váh River in the Kingdom of Hungary; likewise the Poles and Ruthenians who rule very widely, and the Circassians of the "Five Mountains" <note>Referring to the Pyatigorsky region in the Caucasus.</note> by the Black Sea; finally, through Germany beyond the Elbe to the North, the remnants of the Vandals living scattered about use it. Although all these people acknowledge themselves to be Slavs, the Germans nevertheless—taking the name from the Vandals alone—promiscuously call everyone using the Slavonic language "Wenden," "Winden," or "Windisch."

Maciej Miechowita <note>The text calls him "Matthias Michou," a Polish scholar.</note> also previously cited in Book 1, Chapter 13, of his *History of Asiatic Sarmatia*:

> Fifthly, conclude that the language of the Slavs is most extensive and widespread, possessing many lands and provinces, such as the Serbs, Mysians, Rascians or Bulgarians, Bosnians (currently subjugated by the Turk), as well as the Dalmatians, Croats, Pannonians, Slavonians, Carnians, Bohemians, Moravians, Silesians, Great and Little Poles, Mazovians, Pomeranians, Kashubians, Sorbs, Ruthenians, and Muscovites: all these are Slavs and Wends, inhabiting very large kingdoms; but even the Lithuanians are now becoming Slavicized; likewise the inhabitants of Novgorod, Pskov, Smolensk, and Halych—see their Chronicles and Cosmographies.

Sebastian Münster <note>A famous 16th-century cartographer and scholar.</note> in Book 4 of his *Universal Cosmography* has applied himself to describing the histories, chronicles, and cosmographies—or rather, the topographies—of the provinces and regions of Illyria and adjacent lands called today Slavonia, Bosnia, Dacia, Russia, Swabia, Bulgaria, Wallachia, Transylvania, and others, without making ample particular mention of the <meta>language-</meta>

...the Slavic language, <note>The text begins mid-sentence, continuing from the previous page's discussion of regional dialects.</note> otherwise than in the form that I shall set forth hereafter in the chapters on the Poles, the Russians, and the Lithuanians. » This region, which I name Slavonia, was formerly considered under the
» term Illyria, neighboring the Pannonians <note>Ancient people inhabiting the Roman province of Pannonia, covering parts of modern Hungary, Austria, and Croatia.</note>, which at present contains three Prov-
» inces: namely, that which is properly called Slavonia, and which stretches toward
» the West; then Dalmatia, which lies to the South; and Albania, which turns entirely to
» the East. But as for me, I include more under the name of E-

» kish obedience, Illyria and the County of Zara <note>Modern Zadar, Croatia.</note>, Liburnia and Dalmatia, along with the peo-
» ple of Ragusa <note>Modern Dubrovnik.</note>, and their other neighbors who are in Albania. And so you
» see that the extent of this country is quite large, having such limits: to the Levant [East]
» is the Drina, which the ancients called Drane, which passes beyond Rha-
» guse; and toward the West, the Arsa <note>The Raša river in the Istrian peninsula.</note> serves as its boundary, and separates it from Istria; to the
» South lies the Adriatic Sea, and to the North the high mountains of Croa-
» tia; its length is six score leagues <note>120 leagues, roughly 480 kilometers.</note>, namely from the Drina or Drin
» river to that of the Arsa. In width, it contains only thirty, name-
» ly from the shores of the Adriatic Sea to the aforementioned moun-
» tains of Croatia. As for its jurisdiction, it is partly subject to the
» Turk <note>The Ottoman Sultan.</note>, partly to the Venetians, and a little to the King of the Romans <note>The Habsburg ruler of the Holy Roman Empire.</note>: for
» the towns of Slavonia that are along the sea belong to the Ven-
» etian lordship, but those of the mainland obey for the most part the Turk; and
» what is between Segna <note>Modern Senj, Croatia.</note> and the city of Trieste is under the obedience of the King of the
» Romans. But it is the poorest country of all, because ordinar-
» ily the Turks make raids there; which they do not do upon the lands of the
» Venetians, who for that reason are the richest in Slavonia. The inhab-
» itants therein live according to the Roman Church, nonetheless performing their prayers more

> ...and gave their name to the whole province, as much Illyrian as Dalmatian, which at present have no name, any more than the others, where new inhabitants have introduced themselves, who change the names of the lands upon their arrival, just as the Turks do where they settle, and the Slavs <note>Original: *Esclauons*</note> in this land, of whom I shall speak again regarding their first and ancient origin. The same Thevet continues with these words: "All of Slavonia was formerly a very fertile country, having beautiful cities, and a people so valiant that the Roman Emperors, who conquered them, took pride in bearing the title of *Illyricus* <note>A victory title meaning 'Conqueror of Illyria.'</note>. But now the tide has turned, the country being miserable because of the Turk—not that the people have lost their spirit and bravery, which the Turk well knows how to exploit. For the most dashing Janissaries <note>Elite infantry units that formed the Ottoman Sultan's household troops and bodyguards, often recruited from Christian subjects.</note> and the governors of the Provinces are, for the most part, Slavs; just as when I was in Egypt, I saw that the man who was Pasha in Cairo was a Slav. And the Turk does this as much because he knows them to be valiant and of good wit, as also for their great fidelity and loyalty; although it is very difficult to draw them to Islam <note>Original: *Mahometisme*</note> if one does not take them as very young children in their country. Furthermore, having become Turks <note>Meaning they have converted and integrated into Ottoman society.</note>, they are the least troublesome of the renegades, and those who sympathize best with the Christians. But the wickedest peoples are those of Calabria, Naples, and Sicily, and the Greeks—both those from the flat lands and the islanders—who are a hundred times worse than the Turks, Moors, or Arabs, as I have seen through experience."

Whoever wishes to see several discourses on the ancient Slavs should read Procopius <note>A prominent 6th-century Byzantine historian.</note> in Book 1 of the *Gothic War*, Helmold in his *History of the Slavs*, Jan Dubravius in his *History of Bohemia*, Krantz in his *Vandalia* Book 1 and in his preface, Sebastian Münster—previously cited—in Book 4 of his *Cosmography*, André Thevet cited above, and François de Belleforest in Book 3, Chapter 23 of his *Universal History*, and Blaise de Vigenère at the beginning of his *History of Poland*. To be brief, we learn from what is detailed above that the Slavic language is currently understood and spoken by the Slavonians, Serbians, Mysians, Rascians or Bulgarians, Bosnians, Dalmatians, Croats, Pannonians, Slavs, Carniolans, Carinthians, Styrians (in part), Vlachs otherwise called Wallachians, Bohemians, Moravians, Silesians, Poles (both Greater and Lesser), Masovians, Pomeranians, Kashubians, Sorbs, as well as by the Ruthenians and Muscovites <note>Historical terms referring to the peoples of modern-day Ukraine, Belarus, and Russia.</note>, who are Christians of the Greek Church. What is more, the Lithuanians of today are beginning to use this language, along with the people of Novgorod, Pskov, Smolensk, and the Ohuliciens, as the aforementioned authors assert and modern accounts of Northern peoples confirm. In ancient times, this said language was familiar and common among the Mamluks <note>A caste of warrior-slaves who ruled Egypt and Syria; many were of Slavic or Caucasian origin.</note> during the Empire of the Sultans of Egypt and Cairo. At present, it is more common than it has ever been at the court <note>Original: *porte*, referring to the 'Sublime Porte,' the central government of the Ottoman Empire.</note> of the Great Lord of the Turks, but the Arabic, Turkish, and Moorish languages greatly diminish its credit and reputation, for the reasons I have detailed previously in the chapters on the Arabic, Turkish, and African languages. Those who have been to Venice know well enough that several books in this language are currently printed there for those who study it; and it is very certain and assured that it has great agreement and affinity with the Polish language, as Theodor Bibliander <note>A Swiss 16th-century linguist and scholar.</note> well noted in his...

[...a] commentary on the common nature of all languages, making mention of the commentaries of a certain person from Poland named Jan Maoniski <note>Original: *Iean Maozniski*</note>, his preceptor in the Polish language, who asserts in them that the Slavic language <note>Original: *langue Esclauonne*</note> is as beautiful and as sweet as the Greek and Latin languages—whether in its abundance, richness, strength, flexibility, and elegance, or other beauties and perfections attributed to other tongues. A friend of mine living in Poland at present assures me by letter that the Lithuanians of today speak this said Slavic language just as the Poles do, and that this language is common and familiar to several and diverse nations, of which some obey the Roman Church and others follow the Greek schism <note>Referring to the Eastern Orthodox Church</note>. Under the Catholic see are the Poles, Dalmatians, Croats, and Carnians <note>People of Carniola, in modern-day Slovenia</note>; and under the Greek see are the Bulgarians, Russians, part of Lithuania, and Muscovy. Others speaking this same language are infected and imbued with various heresies, such as the Bohemians, Moravian, and Bosnians; some of whom follow the ravings of the Hussites <note>Followers of Jan Hus, a precursor to the Reformation</note>, others embrace the error of the Manicheans <note>Likely referring to the Bogomils, a dualist sect in the Balkans</note>, and some adore idols, as do many of the Lithuanians. In the countryside near Vilnius, the metropolitan city of Lithuania and an Episcopal see, there now live Tatars, in places that have been ordained for them, tilling the earth in their own manner and carrying their merchandise through the country, speaking their Tatar language and living according to the profession and sect of the Alcoran of Muhammad.

A certain personage named Hans Ungnad <note>Original: *Iean Vngenad*</note>, Baron of Sonneg, one of the leaders of the Hungarian army against the Turk, raised by the command of the Emperor Ferdinand, set himself—after the truce made with the Turk—to translate the Old and New Testaments into the Slavic and Croatian languages, together with composing commentaries on the true religion in this same language. He had them printed at great cost and expense, then sent them to be distributed and sold throughout Turkey, to try to induce the Muslims <note>Original: *Mahometistes*</note> to the belief of our Christian religion; I saw and read these commentaries in the hands of a great and learned Polish personage in the city of Paris in the year 1595.

Sleidan <note>Johannes Sleidanus, a 16th-century historian</note> writes in Book 1 that the Emperor Charles IV ordained in the Golden Bull <note>The decree of 1356 that fixed the structure of the Holy Roman Empire</note> that the children of the Electors of the Empire should, in their early years, learn the Latin, Italian, and Slavic languages, so that they might easily speak and communicate with several and diverse nations without any interpreters or translators.

Gesnerus <note>Conrad Gessner</note> and Josias Simler write in their historical *Bibliothecae* that a certain person named Primus Truber of Carniola <note>Primož Trubar, the father of Slovene literature</note> was the first who had a New Testament printed in this language using Latin characters.

Sigismund Gelenius <note>A Bohemian scholar and translator</note>, a Bohemian, composed and had printed in Basel at the house of Froben a *Lexicon Symphonum* <note>A 'Symphonic Lexicon' comparing the sounds and roots of different languages</note>, in which he treats the harmony and consonance of the four familiar languages of Europe: namely, Greek, Latin, German, and Slavic.

# LANGUAGES OF THIS UNIVERSE

Iberia <note>original: *Ἰβηρία*</note>, a region of Asia which Ptolemy also calls the Caucasus. Strabo, in his eleventh book, also writes that the Albanians and Iberians can be called Caucasians. Joannes Tzetzes <note>A 12th-century Byzantine grammarian</note> adds the Abasgians <note>original: *Ἀβασγοὶ*</note>; for he says that the Iberians, Abasgians, and Alans are of one race (though Arrian places the Abasgians <gloss>original: *Ἀβασκοὶ*</gloss> in Colchis). Stephanus seems to call them the Ilaraugatae <gloss>original: *Ἰλαραυγάτας*</gloss>. By Pliny and Mela, they are named the *Georgi* <note>A name likely derived from the Greek word for farmers, 'geōrgoi'</note>. And today they are called Georgians; the region is named Gargania by Aethicus the Sophist. Thevet says—or perhaps invents—that they are called *Gourohs* by the Persians. Eustathius, in his commentary on Dionysius, calls this the Eastern Iberia. Plutarch, the author of *On Rivers and Mountains*, writing from Sosthenes, says this Iberia was once called Pana <gloss>original: *Πανᾶ*</gloss>, after Pan, who was appointed governor of this region by Dionysius; later, it was called Spania <gloss>original: *Σπανίαν*</gloss> by more recent writers.

But if credit is to be given to this author, I would say that the Spaniards—who nearly all classical writers agree originate from this Iberia—took their name from this *Spania* rather than from *Hispalis* <note>The Roman name for Seville</note> (as very many affirm). For they do not call their own origin "Hispalic," but *España* in their native tongue, as if it were *Spania*. For it is evident that the Spanish common people share with the French the habit of prefixing the letter 'E' to Latin words starting with 'S', as seen in the words *schola* (school), *scala* (stair), *scamnum* (bench), *scutum* (shield), *species*, *stella* (star), *scribere* (to write), *studere* (to study), and countless others which they make familiar to their dialects by adding that 'E'. Indeed, Saint Eulogius, who wrote seven hundred years ago, calls it not *Hispania* but *Spania*, as noted by Ambrosio de Morales (who published his life). Saint Luke also calls it so in the Acts. Arias Montanus also testifies in his *Biblical Apparatus* that this Asiatic Iberia is described in the Sacred Scriptures under the name Thabal <gloss>Jerome; Josephus</gloss> <note>Referring to Tubal, son of Japheth, traditionally considered the ancestor of the Iberians</note>, and that the Spaniards who occupy the westernmost part of Europe set out from here. Unless, with Strabo—following Apollodorus, Dionysius, Socrates the Scholastic, and Priscian—one prefers to dream that these people migrated from Spain into Iberia, and to affirm that Iberia was called Spania by them, rather than Pania after Pan. We freely offer this conjecture of ours to the more learned to be examined. Strabo writes that in ancient times, "Iberia" was believed to be whatever lies beyond the Rhône and the isthmus narrowed by the Gallic borders, and that they took the name of Spain only for that which is within the Ebro <note>The Ebro river in Spain, from which 'Iberia' is also derived</note>. Ephorus wrote that the Western Iberians were a great city (or people), as witnessed by Josephus in *Against Apion*. Zonaras perhaps followed him when he says that the most excellent city of Iberia is in Europe. See Spain and Gaul.

mentioned above. In the time of the Great Constantine, these people converted to Christianity, their queen having been cured of a great and mortal illness with which she was afflicted by a manifest miracle occurring to her through the ministry of a certain Christian slave. This was the reason that the said queen, her husband the King, and her people became Christians, at which time their King carried the image of St. George in his banners, escutcheons, and standards. Regarding their ceremonies, which are very close to those of the Greeks, we shall speak of them hereafter in the subsequent chapter on the Serbian <note>original: "Tzeruiane"</note> language. The characters of their letters, which I recovered from their aforementioned Legate or Ambassador in Constantinople, were without names or pronunciations because he departed from that city before being able to give them to me; because of this, I was constrained to obtain them in Venice from a certain person who knew them, and the Armenian language likewise. These characters are in every way—in their order, name, and shape—entirely Greek; however, these Georgians (or *Georgianies*, or Jacobites) distort them somewhat in writing them, adding several other barbaric and strange characters.

Theseus Ambrosius <note>An Italian humanist and linguist, author of the first comprehensive work on Near Eastern languages</note> seems to greatly confuse the form of these characters when he writes the following in his Appendix regarding several and diverse letters:

> "I saw when I was in Rome, under Leo X, the Supreme Pontiff of that name, letters from the Metropolitan of Great Iberia <note>original: 'μεγάλης Ἰβηρίας' (megalēs Ibērias)</note>, written in Greek letters indeed, but very different from the common ones, with a seal on which the image of St. George the Martyr was impressed (for they say it is the banner of that nation); and the signature written by the hand of the Metropolitan himself, with letters so twisted that they were interwoven like a Herculean knot <note>An ancient symbolic knot known for being extremely difficult to untie</note> in a vine-like manner, so that they might take their beginning and make their end together; not even with the eyes of a lynx <note>A common metaphor for exceptionally sharp vision</note> could anyone have discerned them, for the lines of those letters were drawn one over the other in such a way that the fantastic lettering of Giovanni Antonio Talante, however perplexed and entangled in various wraps, would not seem so. Macharius Chius, a monk of the order of St. Basil—who was then staying with me in our canonical house of the Blessed Mary of Peace in the city through the consideration of the then most reverend Cardinal Sauli, and to whom the letters were addressed—even though he was Greek and long-versed in Greek and Arabic letters, could hardly have ever understood them if he had not been assisted by the help of the Georgian <note>original: "Iberi"</note> who brought them. Indeed, posterity might have seen the forms of those letters and the signature of that Metropolitan, explained despite many difficulties, printed in this our tradition, if that immense and always-to-be-lamented calamity and final destruction of my unhappy homeland <note>Referring to the Sack of Pavia in 1527</note> had not taken them from me along with the rest of my numerous supply of books."

T. Bibliander <note>Theodore Bibliander, a Swiss Orientalist and linguist</note> in his *Commentary on the Common Reason of All Languages and Letters*:

> "The Georgians inhabit a very wide region and live near the Armenians, but they are divided between two very powerful kings, both of whom, however, are of the Christian name. Concerning the language and letters, Postellus <note>Guillaume Postel, a famous French polymath and linguist</note> reports these things: From the Greek language, the Georgian and Serbian letters and language flowed. And elsewhere he says: the Georgians use the Greek language in sacred rites; the vulgar tongue is a medium between Tatar and Armenian; they write both with these letters which they have in common with the Jacobites <note>A West Syrian Christian sect</note>, whom they pursue today with singular hatred. It is probable they were invented by the Jacobites who followed the heresy of the Jacobite Patriarch of Alexandria, and they were once in great use among the Churches of the East; the characters are almost Greek in name and shape, but they write them depravedly, and add I know not how many barbaric ones." These remarks seem to be taken from an old and ancient book entitled *The Voyage to the Holy Land*, composed by a certain religious man of the order of Our Lady of Mount Carmel, living in the year of salvation 1487.

### HISTORY OF THE ORIGIN OF THE [GEORGIANS]

named F. Nicolle **Hué**, Doctor in the faculty of Theology. Previously, J. de Mandeville, a Knight living in the year 1322, wrote these very words in his travels composed in the Romance language:

> The Christians who are called Georgians, whom Saint George converted; they honor him more than any other saint in paradise, and they call upon him every day to help them, etc. <note>original: "Los Chrestians que fon appellats Gorgias los quels fent Iordy conuerty, e aell ha horé pus que a null altro sant de paradis, ell appellé tot iórs quells aiut &c." This is an archaic form of the Romance language used by the famous traveler Sir John Mandeville.</note>

To be brief, these Georgians (or *Georgianians*), called *Iurgiálar* by the Turks and Tartars, have the same name and number of letters as the Jacobites and Coptites; however, their characters are much more similar to those of the Greeks, from whom they differ very little. They took this name from the valiant Martyr Saint George, whose image they carried on their banners and ensigns, because it was he who first planted the Christian faith in those regions—the near neighbors of Cappadocia, of which Angorie <note>Modern-day Ankara, Turkey</note> is the capital city. Thus, they have held him in great veneration ever since. Nevertheless, Chalcocondyle <note>Laonicus Chalcocondyles, a 15th-century Byzantine historian</note> records that in the time of Constantine the Great, their Queen was cured of a very grievous illness by a Christian slave, and they were converted to the faith at that time.

Furthermore, Georgia <note>original: "la Georgianie"</note>, as it is now called, is the region that Strabo, Pliny, Ptolemy, and other geographers name Iberia (or Hiberia), which forms a portion of the ancient kingdom of Colchis. it is near Trebizond and the river Phasis—now called the Fasso—which flows into the Pontus Euxinus, or the "Great Sea" <note>The Black Sea</note>. This province extends on one side to the Hyrcanian Sea <note>The Caspian Sea</note> and Greater Armenia. But beyond those who live there today—people who are very poor and miserable in all their ways of life—there are many spread across various parts of Asia. There is even a good number in Jerusalem who, in addition to the Oratory they possess in the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, occupy many holy sites. Specifically, they hold Mount Calvary, where a chapel and altar stand on the very spot where the Cross of our Lord was planted, as well as a church called the Church of the Angels, located where the house of the High Priest Annas once stood. 

In former times, they were so feared and respected by the Moors, the Sultan of Cairo, and later the Turks, that they would enter the city with banners unfurled. They were also exempt from the tribute called <term>Carazzi</term> <note>The Kharaj, a head tax typically levied on non-Muslim subjects</note>, which is collected for every person among all types of Christians. Even to this day, no one has dared to attack them—neither the Turk, nor the Persian, nor the Tartars—despite the fact that they hold to the Christian religion. Nevertheless, they follow the sect of Nestorius, the former Bishop of Constantinople, whose error was condemned at the third Council of Ephesus. This sect posits two persons in our Savior, one divine and the other human, and denies the presence of his body in the Eucharist except at the moment it is consumed. They do not acknowledge the Virgin Mary as the Mother of God, but only as the mother of Jesus Christ insofar as he was a man; they hold other such impieties common to the Jacobites. However, it is perhaps the case that the aforementioned powers have not taken much trouble to attack them because of their poverty and misery, and the difficulty of their terrain, which is not worth conquering. They are left as they are so they may serve as a reciprocal barrier for one another. Indeed, they are no longer as valiant as they used to be; instead, most are now faint-hearted, dull, and idle. These people now follow the traditions of the Greek Church in every way and use that language and script in their services, though they use somewhat different characters in their business and affairs...

# HISTORY OF THE ORIGIN OF THE #

...[ea]ting <note>The word "geants" is the end of "mangeants," meaning eating.</note> neither fish nor any delicacy during Lent, listening most attentively to the word of God, and remaining for a long time in prayer in those places where they have the means to do so without hindrance. They have as their head in spiritual matters a sovereign Bishop whom they call the *Iacelit* or *Iacelique* <note>A corruption of "Catholicos," the title for the head of the Georgian and Armenian churches</note>, to whom nearly all the Christians of the East—scattered across the lands of the Tartars and part of Persia—pay obedience. They recognize him just as we do the Holy Apostolic See of Rome, of which they take no account. Whoever wishes to see more discourses on these Iberians, Georgians, or Georgianians should read Socrates, Book 1 of his *Ecclesiastical History*; Ptolemy, Book 5, Chapter 12, Table 3 of Asia; Appian in his book on the *Mithridatic War*; Procopius, Book 1 of the *Persian War*; Josaphat Barbaro in his *Voyage to Tana*, Chapter 14; Ambroise Contaren in his *Voyage to Persia*; Laonicus Chalcondyles, Book 9 of the *History of the Turks*; Rufinus, Theodoret, and Socrates in their *Ecclesiastical Histories*; and other authors cited by F. de Belleforest in Book 2, Chapter 5 of his *Universal History*, and in Volume 2, Book 3, Chapter 6 of his *Universal Cosmography*. See also what the Lord of Villamont has recently written of these Georgians in Book 2, Chapter 23 of his *Voyages*.

As for the Jacobites, they also have their alphabet arranged in the Greek fashion, and the names of their letters are very similar. They even use this language—which they write with their own characters, which are all Greek but degraded and altered <note>original: "deprauez & peruertis"</note>—for the Ecclesiastical service. For worldly affairs, they use their vernacular, which is a middle ground between Armenian and Tartar, as confirmed by Theseus Ambrosius in his *Introduction to the Chaldean, Syriac, and Armenian languages*, Chapter 5, on the consonants of the Jacobites and Copts. However, this is not a nation, but rather a sect and heresy, having taken its name from a certain Jacob <note>Jacob Baradaeus, the 6th-century bishop who revitalized the Syriac Orthodox Church</note>, a disciple of a Patriarch of Alexandria, who poisoned them with the error of Nestorius <note>The author confuses the Jacobites (who are Miaphysite) with their theological rivals, the Nestorians</note>. They have held to this ever since without deviation, differing from the traditions of the Latin and Greek Churches, from which they were banished and excommunicated long ago by Dioscorus, Patriarch of Constantinople <note>The author likely means the Council of Chalcedon; Dioscorus of Alexandria was actually the leader of the party that became the Jacobites</note>. Even today, their leader is called the *Iacolit*, who ordains their Prelates and Ministers, along with their sacraments after their own fashion, as written by Marco Polo in Book 1, Chapter 6 of his *Voyages*; John Mandeville in his *Voyages*, in the chapter on the law of the Jacobites; and G. Postel in his *Alphabet of Twelve Languages* following Jacques de Vitry, Chapter 38 of his *History of Jerusalem*. This sect took its origin from Eutyches, who among his other impieties maintained that Jesus Christ had not taken his body from the Virgin Mary, but rather had entered her womb like a clear ray of Sun; they furthermore reject all types of images in their temples. They have a chapel for themselves in the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in the city of Jerusalem, where they perform their service separately, just like the Latins, Greeks, Abyssinians <note>Ethiopians</note>, Armenians, Georgians, and Maronites, who do the same as the Chaldeans or Syrians, each in their own place. For these seven nations and types of people are admitted into this Church and have their residence there for those of their kind who go there on pilgrimage. But these Jacobites, without having any specific or fixed permanent dwelling of their own, are spread across various parts of Asia and Egypt, even as far as Nubia and Ethiopia, and in more than forty kingdoms, both on the mainland and in the Islands of the East and South, among the Mohammedans <note>original: "Mahometistes"</note>, from whom they have borrowed their practice of circumcision. In addition to this, they cauterize small children with a hot iron...

They do not confess their sins to Priests, but to God alone; for this purpose, they take a brazier <note>A portable heater or censer.</note> into which they throw a little incense, believing that with the smoke, their offenses rise up to where they are forgiven and erased. They grant communion to both children and adults alike under both kinds <note>Receiving both the bread and the wine during the Eucharist.</note>. As for their language, they have one that is their own and particular to them, just as Hebrew is to the Jews; they likewise have a script, such as it is represented here; but they simultaneously use the languages of the regions where they live and converse, which is most commonly in Cairo.

HISTORY OF THE ORIGIN OF <note>The header is incomplete, continuing from the previous page: "History of the Origin of Alphabets."</note>

Teseo Ambrogio, <note>original: "Thesus Ambrosius" (1469–1540), an Italian canon and one of the first European scholars of Near Eastern languages.</note> in his *Appendix on several and diverse letters of languages* within a letter sent to the late Guillaume Postel, <note>Guillaume Postel (1510–1581) was a French linguist and astronomer known for his work on Oriental languages.</note> seems to assert that he was the first among Europeans to bring to light this Alphabet, along with that of the Coptics, which I will treat hereafter. See what is written of these Jacobites and their ways of life and customs by André Thevet in Book 11, Chapter 18 of his *Universal Cosmography*, and by the Lord of Villamont in Book 2, Chapter 22 of his *Travels*.

In the year 1552, these Jacobites sought a reconciliation with the Roman Pope, Julius III, sending the Legate of the Patriarch of Antioch named Moses of Mardin, <note>original: "Moses Mardenus," a Syrian priest and scholar who helped introduce Syriac printing to Europe.</note> a learned person native to Syria, to make a profession of their faith. This profession is transcribed word-for-word by André Thevet in the place cited above. Modern reports from the Levant confirm that these Jacobites are as they are, and live in the manner we have described above.

->**Concerning the Coptics.**<-

The Coptics have the same names for their letters as the Jacobites, but the characters are somewhat different, also numbering thirty-two. Guillaume Postel, cited above in his treatise on Phoenician letters, confuses them with the Jacobites, although they are more specifically Egyptian and have been Christians for a longer time. Teseo Ambrogio does the same in his *Introduction to the Chaldean, Syriac, and Armenian languages*, Chapter 5, in his *Appendix on several and diverse kinds of languages*. These Coptics are named after the city of Coptos, which Plutarch mentions in his treatise *On Isis and Osiris*, and Pliny in Book 5, Chapter 9, who attributes to it one of the seats and governments of Egypt. 

In the 19th year of his reign, which falls in the year 306 of our salvation, the Emperor Diocletian caused one hundred and twenty thousand <note>original: "six vingts mille"</note> of them to be martyred and confined countless others to exile. Because of this most horrible butchery and execution, they have always begun to count their *Era* <note>term: Era <gloss>The Era of Martyrs, or Diocletian Era, is a calendar system still used by the Coptic Church.</gloss></note>—which is the dating of their years—from that time, just as we do from the birth of our Lord; this was noted by Joseph Scaliger <note>A famous 16th-century scholar who revolutionized the study of chronology and calendars.</note> in Book 3 of *The Correction of Time*. They call the Father *Phiot* <note>Coptic: ⲫⲓⲱⲧ (*p-iot*)</note> and the Son *Pscirim*, <note>Coptic: ⲡ-ϣⲏⲣⲓ (*p-shiri*)</note> and they count using the letters of their alphabet, just like the Hebrews, Chaldeans, Greeks, Macedonians, Dalmatians or Slavs, and others; however, the Arabs and Indians use certain numerical signs <note>Referring to Arabic numerals (0–9) which were relatively new to the West at the time.</note> intended for this purpose, as do the Latins.

# Of the Hetrurians, or Etruscans, and the Etruscan Language.

## CHAPTER LXVII.

We can learn from Latin histories that the Etruscans were among the most ancient peoples of Italy, where, a short time after the universal deluge, Janus the good father—whom some authors believe to have been the same as the good Patriarch Noah, restorer of the human race—came to found twelve cities, just as Cato writes in his *Origins*. From these, through the passage of time, the Romans later borrowed the greatest part of their mysteries and ceremonies, according to Cicero in this legal formula: *Let the Princes of Etruria teach the discipline of the sacred rites; let them provide for the gods through whom they have flourished.* <note>original: "Ethruriæ Principes disciplinam sacrorum docento, quibus Dijs creuerint, procuranto"</note> And furthermore, this concerned auguries and predictions made through the entrails of victims, and the flight of birds, or their songs—first invented by Malotus in Etruria, named Tages by Cicero and Lucian—as well as the interpretation of lightning and fires from heaven, hail and extraordinary rains, monsters, and other prodigies. On this subject, see P. Crinitus, <note>Pietro Crinito (1474–1507), a Renaissance humanist scholar.</note> book 10, chapter 7, of *Honest Discipline*,<gloss>l</gloss> and the subsequent book 25, chapter 2. 

Regarding their letters and writing, it is held that all these twelve cities or tribes used similar characters entrusted only to the Priests, who transposed them according to their own rights, and varied their order, value, and placement at their whim, in the manner of ciphers; sometimes drawing from left to right, as we do, and sometimes the reverse in the manner of the Hebrews, so as to always better hide themselves from the surrounding peoples. This was done so that they could not discover the secret names of the Genii <note>Spirits or guardian deities believed to protect a person or place.</note> or guardian Angels, protectors and patrons who assisted them, along with the manner of their prayers, sacrifices, and offerings used to make them favorable, for fear that they [their enemies] might evoke them to themselves. This "evocation" <note>The Roman ritual of "evocatio deorum" involved formally inviting the tutelary deity of an enemy city to abandon them and come to Rome in exchange for a superior cult.</note> was later practiced by the Romans and was one of the principal means by which their affairs increased. These sacrifices and ceremonies that might please these tutelary deities had required a very long period of observation, established upon a perfect knowledge of the stars; for it is from heaven that the name and office of each Genius is drawn, and consequently from the nature and property of elementary things, each of which has its own particular star corresponding to the intelligence that presides over it. 

The whole matter ultimately relates to the glory of the first immobile intellect, upon whom they depend and from whom they have their being and movement: the sovereign God, namely, disguised to them under the name of Zeus or Jove, <note>original: "Iouis"</note> a word corrupted from the *Jehovah* <note>original: "Iehoua"</note> of the Hebrews. Of these transpositions of Etruscan letters, the two following alphabets bear witness, one of which proceeds in the manner of the Hebrews from right to left, and the other the reverse, like the Greeks and Latins; for otherwise, most of the characters resemble one another. And although it is not found anywhere, according to the learned, that the Latins borrowed theirs from the Etruscans, nevertheless, since we see such a great conformity between them, it is to be believed that they were once the same. It is true that Cato in his *Origins* writes that Turrenus, King of Tuscany, in the year 470 after the founding of

# LANGUAGES OF THIS UNIVERSE.

Rome brought into its subjection its capital city in Etruria, as well as its state and kingdom, and the Etruscans did not wish at that time to receive the Latin letters.

In Volterra—one of the aforementioned twelve cities—one still sees today many old epitaphs and inscriptions on marble tables, sepulchral urns, and statues, which are held to be in Etruscan letters. However, no one can understand anything of them, because the language is extinct and has been entirely lost for a very long time. The most learned Joseph Scaliger, <note>Joseph Justus Scaliger (1540–1609), a leading scholar of the Renaissance known for his work on chronology and philology.</note> in his conjectures on Varro’s *On the Latin Language*, held that the ancient Etruscan language was Aramaic, saying that <note>original: "Saturni nomen esse Tuscū, omnes mihi concedēt, qui sciunt Syriace, & pro certo habet olim Tuscorū linguam Arameam fuisse."</note> "the name of Saturn is Tuscan; everyone who knows Syriac will grant me this, and he holds it for certain that the language of the Tuscans was once Aramaic." For *Saturnus* in the Syriac language signifies "the hidden one": <note>Etruscan origins were often debated by Renaissance scholars who sought to link them to Biblical lineages.</note> whence, in the Latin territory, as if interpreting the name, they called him Latium, and his wife Ops, Latia. And in the Pontifical records of names, she was called "Latia of Saturn," according to Gellius, <note>Aulus Gellius (c. 125 – after 180 AD), author of the *Attic Nights*.</note> book 13, chapter 2, and from him comes the name Latium. The historian Livy, in book 9 of his *Decades*, writes that in ancient times the children of the Romans were accustomed to learn both Greek and Etruscan letters: which were taught in former times to the Etruscans by a certain Demaratus of Corinth. This is confirmed by Cornelius Tacitus in book 11 of his *Annals*, Raphael Volaterranus in book 5 of his *Geography*, and Polydore Vergil in book 1, chapter 6 of *On the Discovery of Things*. What is more, Strabo in book 5 asserted that the Oscan and Sabine languages were for some time observed by those same Romans in the Atellan Poems <note>Atellan Farce: a type of early Roman improvisational comedy featuring stock characters.</note> recited by comedians in the theaters.

Theseus Ambrosius, <note>Teseo Ambrogio (1469–1540), an Italian humanist who published one of the first comprehensive studies of various alphabets.</note> in his *Appendix on many and diverse letters*, speaking of this matter, said:

> Many have recorded that the Etruscans, Volscians, and Oscans had various letters and a varied style of speaking, and I believe there should be no hesitation, even by those who have only touched upon literature with the "tips of their lips" (as they say). Indeed, to speak of the Etruscans, he testifies that other inscriptions were found in Volterra, as well as in the tombs of Tarchon <note>Tarchon was a legendary hero of the Etruscans.</note> with Etruscan letters engraved everywhere. Yet, as for which people specifically owned the elements or marks of the letters preserved on the bronze tablets of Gubbio, <note>The Iguvine Tablets, discovered in 1444, which are the most important source for the Umbrian language.</note> no one (whom I have seen) has yet clearly asserted it. However, I have found the Etruscan alphabet written in various ways in different books and Italian libraries; for in some places it appears written from right to left, as seen below. Indeed, an excellent jurist, very well-versed in the humanities and polished literature, Julius de Juliis Canobinus, sent this alphabet to me with his letters from Bologna in these recent months, and he wrote that he obtained it from Giovanni Achillini, <note>Giovanni Filoteo Achillini (1466–1533), a Bolognese poet and polymath.</note> a truly noble and most refined citizen of Bologna. The Etruscan characters subscribed below were taken from the books of the philosopher Tarquin (or Tarvisinus) and conformed with not a few other copies; they are written in the manner of the Latins, from the left side to the right. Whence such a great variety in writing proceeded, I cannot see. Let others make better conjectures.

See what is written on this matter by P. Crinito, book 3, chapter 3, and book 16, chapter 1, of *On Honest Discipline*. <note>original: "P. Crinit liu. 3. ch. 3. & liure 16. chap. 1. de l'honneste discipline." Pietro Crinito (1475–1507) was an Italian humanist scholar.</note>

Theodore Bibliander in his *Commentary on all languages and letters*. <note>Theodor Bibliander (1505–1564) was a Swiss linguist and reformer who sought to find a common root for all languages.</note>

Furthermore, concerning Etruscan letters, Volaterranus <note>Raffaele Maffei (1451–1522), known as Volaterranus, was a humanist who documented the antiquities of his hometown, Volterra.</note> writes thus: "Many monuments of the ancient Etruscans have recently been unearthed at Volterra with Etruscan letters, which once—according to the testimony of Livy and Pliny—were held in high esteem among the Romans, but are now utterly unknown. In the inscription of a statue, which the same Raphael [Volaterranus] displayed, one may recognize most of the Latin letters: A, E, I, O, V, B, C, D, F, K, L, M, N. Some Greek and Latin letters appear inverted, and some are composed into a single syllable; yet there are authors who assert that these letters came to the Etruscans from Demaratus the Corinthian." <note>original: "Porrò de literis Hetruscis Volaterranus ita scribit... literas à Demaratho Corinthio venisse ad Hetruscos." Demaratus was a legendary figure said to have fled Corinth for Etruria in the 7th century BC, bringing Greek culture with him.</note> After the invasions of the Goths, the Germanic tribes, and the Slavs, and the tearing apart and ruin of the Empire, the provincial speech degenerated further from its origin. This is seen in the province of Dacia in the language of the Vlachs <note>The Vlachs were the Romance-speaking populations of Eastern Europe; their language evolved into modern Romanian.</note>; for *Vlasky* sounds like "Italian" or *Waelschen* <note>original: "Vualhen." A Germanic term used to describe foreigners, specifically Celts or Latin-speakers.</note> to the Slavs. The same happened in the Spains, in Gaul, and finally in Italy itself, in the city that was mistress of nations and the seat of Roman eloquence. Moreover, individual Provinces again have their own dialects. Just as one skilled in languages discerns those using Italian speech: the Lombard, the Tuscan, the Sicilian, the Rhaetian. Similarly in the French language: the Provençal, the Savoyard, the Burgundian, the Parisian, and the Picard; and in the Spanish language: the Catalan, the Castilian, and the Portuguese. This discrepancy of dialect is even more widely spread and scattered, and it grows daily through foreign influence and other means. And yet, learned men who have served their countries well have enclosed these languages into the form of an art [grammar], such as Bembo, Corderius, Drosæus, Ælius Antonius Nebrissensis, and others. <note>These scholars—Pietro Bembo (Italian), Mathurin Cordier (French/Latin), Jean Dresser (Drosæus), and Antonio de Nebrija (Spanish)—were pioneers in formalizing the grammars of their respective vernacular languages.</note> This fact proves that the language of any nation does not shun technical treatment, provided that study and attention are applied.

Regarding what we touched upon above concerning the Genies <note>In the Renaissance context, "Genies" refers to *genii*, the tutelary spirits or guardian angels of people or places.</note> or guardian Angels, protectors, and patrons, and the means of evoking them: We shall say that the Hebrews, in their secret Theology <note>A reference to the Kabbalah.</note>, hold that no one can be overcome here below—as Rabbi Joseph Ben Carnitol <note>Likely Joseph Gikatilla (1248–c. 1305), a Spanish Kabbalist; "Carnitol" is a common corruption of his name in early modern texts.</note> confirms in his book *The Gates of Justice* on this passage: *On that day the Lord Jehovah will punish the host of the high ones on high, and the kings of the earth on the earth* <note>original: "In die illa animaduertet Dominus Iehoua in omnem exercitum excelsum in excelso, & in Reges terræ in terra" (Isaiah 24:21).</note>—unless the Intelligence [Angel] that assists him from above is overcome first and distracted from his protection. This is seen in chapter 28 of Ezekiel, where God, deliberating on the destruction of the city of Tyre, first withdraws the Cherub; and in Daniel 10, concerning that Prince of the Kingdom of Persia—namely, their Genie and patron—who resisted the Angel Gabriel for 21 days until Saint Michael arrived as reinforcement. St. Clement, in book 6 of the *Stromata*: "For among nations and cities, the prefectures of Angels are distributed," <note>original: "Nam per gentes & ciuitates, sunt distributæ Angelorum præfecturæ."</note> which this great personage seems to have drawn from Moses in chapter 32 of Deuteronomy: *When the Most High divided the nations, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of his Angels.* <note>original: "Quando diuidebat altissimus gentes... iuxta numerum Angelorum suorum." ...in the second book of his *Recognitions*, where he says: "There is an Angel for each nation, to whom the administration of that nation has been entrusted by God.
